hen I think of all the struggles, difficulties, and failures of which many complain, and an

anthem in words so simple that a little child could understand, what is the secret of the

Christian life? And then the thought comes to me, can I venture to hope that it will be given to

me to take that glorious, heavenly, divine Lord Jesus and to show Him to these souls so that they

can see Him in His glory? And can it be given to me to open their eyes to see that there is a

Divine, Almighty Christ, who does actually come into the heart and who faithfully promises, "I

will come and dwell with you, and I will never leave you?" Matthew 28:20.

No; my words cannot do that. But then I thought, my Lord Jesus can use me as a simple servant

to take such feeble ones by the hand, encourage, and help them to say, Oh, come, come, come,

into the presence of Jesus and wait on Him, and He will reveal Himself to you. I pray to God that

He may use His precious Word. It is simply the presence of the Lord Jesus.

fields.title: W
fields.body_html:
That is the secret of the Christian's strength and joy. You know that when He was upon earth, He

was present in bodily form with his disciples. They walked about together all day, and at night

they went to the same house, and sometimes slept together and ate and drank together. They

were continually together. It was the presence of Jesus that was the training school of His

disciples. They were bound to Him by that wonderful intercourse of love during three long years,

and in that intercourse, they learned to know Christ, and Christ instructed and corrected them,

and prepared them for what they were afterwards to receive. And now when He is going away,

He says to them: "And behold, I am with you always, to the end of the age." Matthew 28:20.

What a promise! And just as really as Christ was with Peter in the boat, just as Christ sat with

John at the table, as really can I have Christ with me. And more really, for they had their Christ

in the body and He was to them a man, an individual separate from them, but I may have

glorified Christ in the power of the throne of God, the omnipotent Christ, and the omnipresent

Christ.

What a promise! You ask me, how can that be? And my answer is, because Christ is God, and

because Christ after having been made man, went up to the throne and the Life of God. And now

that blessed Christ Jesus, with His loving, pierced heart; that blessed Jesus Christ, who lived on

earth; that same Christ glorified into the glory of God, can be in me and can be with me all the

days.

You say, “Is it really possible for a man in the business, for a woman in the midst of a large and

difficult household, for a poor man full of care; is it possible? Can I always be thinking of

Jesus?” Thank God, you need not always be thinking of Him. You may be the manager of a

bank, and your whole attention may be required to carry out the business that you have to do.

But thank God, while I have to think of my business, Jesus will think of me, and He will come in

and take charge of me.

That little child, three months old, as it sleeps in its mother's arms, lies helplessly there; it hardly

knows its mother, it does not think of her, but the mother thinks of the child. And this is the

blessed mystery of love, that Jesus the God-Man waits to come into me in the greatness of His

love; and as He gets possession of my heart, He embraces me in those divine arms and tells me,

"My child, I the Faithful One, I the Mighty One will abide with you, will watch over you and

keep you all the days."

He tells me He will come into my heart so that I can be a happy Christian, a holy Christian, and a

useful Christian. You say, Oh! If I could only believe that, if I could think that it is possible to

have Christ always, every hour, and every moment with me, taking and keeping charge of me!

My brother, my sister, it is just literally this that is my message to you. When Jesus said to His

disciples, "I am with you always," He meant it in the fullness of the divine Omnipresence, in the

fullness of the divine love, and He longs to reveal Himself tonight to you.

And now just think for a moment, what a blessed life that must be when the presence of Jesus is

always abiding. Isn't that the secret to peace and happiness? If I could just attain (that is what

each heart says) to that blessed state in which every day and all the day I felt Jesus to be

watching and ever keeping me, oh, what peace I would have in the thought, "I have no care if He

cares for me, and I have no fear if He provides for me." Your heart says that this is too good to

be true and that it is too glorious to be for you. Still, you acknowledge it must be most blessed.

Fearful one, erring one, anxious one, I bring you God's promise, it is for me and for you. Jesus

will do it; as God, He is able, and Jesus is willing and longing as the Crucified One to keep you

in perfect peace. This is a wonderful fact, and it is the secret of joy unspeakable. And this is also

the secret of Holiness.

Instead of indwelling sin, an indwelling Christ conquering it; instead of indwelling sin, the

indwelling life and light and love of the blessed Son of God. He is the secret of holiness. "Christ

Jesus, who became to us wisdom from God, righteousness and sanctification" 1 Corinthians

1:30. Remember that it is Christ Himself who is made unto us sanctification. Christ coming into

me, taking charge of my whole being; my nature and my thoughts and my affections and my

will; ruling all things. It is this that will make me holy. We talk about holiness, but do you know

what holiness is? You have as much holiness as you have of Christ, for it is written, "For he who

sanctifies and those who are sanctified all have one source." (Hebrews 2:11), and Christ

sanctifies by bringing God's life into me.

We read in Judges 6:34, "The Spirit of the Lord clothed Gideon." But you know that there is in

the New Testament an equally wonderful text, where we read, "Put on the Lord Jesus Christ,"

(Romans 13:14) that is, clothe yourself with Christ, Jesus. And what does that mean? It does not

only mean, by the imputation of righteousness outside of me, but to clothe myself with the living

character of the living Christ, with the living love of the living Christ. Put on the Lord Jesus.

Oh! What works? I cannot do it unless I believe and understand that He whom I have to put on is

as a garment covering my whole being. I have to put on a living Christ who has said, "Behold, I

am with you always." Matthew 28:20.

Just draw the folds closer round you, of that robe of light with which Christ would array you.

Just come and acknowledge that Christ is with you, on you, and in you. Oh, put Him on! And

when you look at one characteristic of His after another; and you hear God's word, "Have this

mind among yourselves, which is yours in Christ Jesus," (Philippians 2:5) and it tells you He

was obedient unto the death; and then you answer, Christ the obedient one, Christ whose whole

life was obedience, it is that Christ whom I have received and put on. He becomes my life, and

His obedience rests upon me until I learn to whisper as Jesus did, "My Father, your will be done;

I come to do your will." John 6:38.

This, too, is the secret of influence in witness and work. How come it is so difficult to be

obedient, and how come I so often sin? People sing, "Oh, to be wholly Thine," and sing it from

their hearts. How come they become disobedient again? Where does disobedience come from?

And here’s the answer. It is because I am trying to obey a distant Christ, and thus His commands

do not come with power. Look what I find in God's Word. When God wanted to send any man

upon His service, He first met and talked with him, and cheered him time after time. God

appeared to Abraham seven or eight times and gave him one command after another, and so

Abraham learned to obey Him perfectly. God appeared to Joshua and Gideon, and they obeyed.

And why are we not obedient? Because we have so little of this near intercourse with Jesus.

If we knew this blessed, heavenly secret of having the presence of Christ with us every day,

every hour, every minute, what a joy it would be to obey! We could not walk in this

consciousness; “My Lord Jesus is with me and around me”, and not obey Him! Oh, do you not

begin to long and say, this is what I must have, the ever-abiding presence of Jesus! There are

some Christians who try not to be disobedient, who come to their Sunday and weekday duties

most faithfully, and pray for grace and a blessing, and they complain of so little blessing and

power, so little power! And why? Because there is not enough of the living Jesus in their hearts.

I sometimes think of this as the most solemn truth. There is a great diversity of gifts amongst

ministers and others who speak, but I am sure of this, that a man's gifts are not the measure of his

real power. I am sure of this, that God can see what neither you nor I can see.

Sometimes people feel something of it, but in proportion as a man has in reality, not as a

sentiment or an aspiration, or a thought, but in reality, the very spirit and presence of Jesus upon

him, there comes out from him an unseen silent influence. That secret influence is the Holy

presence of Jesus. "Behold, I am with you always." Matthew 28:20. And now, if what I have said

has sufficed just to indicate what a desirable thing it is, what a blessed thing it is to live for, then

let me now give you an answer to the question that arises in more than one heart. I can hear

someone say, "Tell me how I can get this blessed abiding presence of Jesus; and when I have got

it, how I can ever keep it. I think if I have this, I have it all.

The Lord Jesus has come very near to me. I have tried to turn away from everything that can

hinder me and have had my Lord very near. But how can I know that He will always be with

me?" If you were to ask the Lord, "Oh, my blessed Lord Christ, what must I do, how can I enjoy

your never-failing presence?" His first answer would be, "Only believe. I have said it often, and

you only partly understood it, but I will say it again My child, only believe." It is by faith.

We sometimes speak of faith as trust, and it is a very helpful thing to tell men that faith is trust,

but when people say, as they sometimes do, that it is nothing else but trust, that is not the case. It

is a far wider word than trust. It is by faith that I learn to know the invisible One, the invisible

God, and that I see Him. Faith is my spiritual eyesight for the unseen and heavenly. You often

try hard to trust God, and you fail. Why? Because you have not taken time first to see God. How

can you trust God fully until you have met Him and known Him? You ask, "Where ought I to

begin?" You ought, to begin with first believing, with presenting yourself before this God in the

attitude of silent worship and asking Him to let a sense of His greatness and His presence come

upon you. You must ask Him to let your heart be covered over with his holy presence. You must

seek to realise in your heart the presence of an Almighty and all-loving God, an unspeakably

loving God.

Take time to worship Him as the omnipotent God, to feel that the very power that created the

world, the very power that raised Jesus from the dead, is at this moment working in your heart.

We do not experience it because we do not believe it. We must take time to believe. Jesus says,

"Oh, my child, shut your eyes to the world, and shut out of your heart all these thoughts about

religion, and begin to believe in God Himself." That is the first article of the Creed " I believe in

God ."

By believing, I open my heart, to receive this glorious God, and I bow and worship. And then as

I believe this, I look up and I see the Lamb upon the Throne, and I believe that the Almighty

power of God is in Jesus for the very purpose of revealing His presence to my heart. Why are

there two upon the Throne? Is God not enough? The Lamb of God is upon the Throne in your

interest and in mine; the Lamb upon the Throne is Christ Himself, with power as God to take

possession of me. Oh, do not think you cannot get that realisation. And do not think of it as now

only within your reach, but cultivate the habit of faith. "Jesus, I believe in your glory; I believe in

your omnipotence; I believe in your power working within me. I believe in your living, loving

presence with me, revealing itself in Divine power."

Do not be occupied with feelings or experiences. You will find it far simpler and easier just to

trust and say, "I am sure He is all for me." Get rid of yourself for the time; don't think or speak

about yourself, but think about what Jesus is. And then remember it always believes. I

sometimes feel that I cannot find words to tell how God wants His people to believe from

morning to night. Every breath ought to be just believing. Yes, it is indeed true; the Lord Jesus

loves us to be just believing from morning to evening, and you must begin to make that the chief

thing in life.

When you wake up in the morning, let your heart go forth with a large faith in this, and in the

watches of the night let this thought be present with you, my Saviour Jesus is around me and

near me, and you can look up and say, "I want to trust you always." You know what trust is. It is

so sweet to trust. And can’t you now trust Jesus, this presence, this keeping presence? He lives

for you in Heaven. You are marked with His blood, and he loves you; and can’t you say, "My

King, my King, He is with me all the days?" Oh, trust Jesus to fulfil His own promises. There is

a second answer that I think Christ would give if we come to Him believing and say, "Is there

anything more, my blessed Master?" I think I can hear His answer: "My child, always obey."

Do not fail to understand the lesson contained in this one word. You must distinctly take that

word OBEY and obedience, and learn to say for yourselves: "Now I have to obey, and by the

grace of God I am going to obey in everything."

At our recent exhibition at the Cape, Mr. Rhodes, our Prime Minister, went to the gate, thinking

he had got the fee in his pocket. When he got to the gate, however, he found he had not enough

money, and said to the doorkeeper, "I am Mr. Rhodes; let me in and I will take care, you do not

have to suffer." But the man said, "I cannot help that, sir, I have my orders," and he refused to let

Mr. Rhodes in. He had to borrow from a friend and pay before he could pass the gate. At dinner

afterwards, Mr Rhodes spoke about it and said it was a real joy to see a man stick to his order

like that. That is it. The man had his orders, and that was enough for him, and whoever came to

the gate had to pay his fee before he could enter. God's children ought to be like soldiers, and be

ready to say, "I must obey."

Oh! To have that thought in our hearts: "Jesus, I love to obey you." There must be personal

intercourse with the Saviour, and then comes the joy of personal service and allegiance. Are you

ready to obey in all feebleness and weakness and fear? Can you say, "Yes, Lord Jesus, I will

obey?" If so, then give yourself up absolutely. Then your feeling will be, "I am not going to

speak one word if I think that Jesus would not like to hear it. I am not going to have an opinion

of my own, but my whole life is to be covered with the purity of His obedience to the Father and

His self-sacrificing love for me. I want Christ to have my whole life, my whole heart, my whole

character. I want to be like Christ and to obey." Give yourself up to this loving obedience.

The third thought is this: If I say, "My Master, blessed Saviour, tell me all, I will believe, I do

obey, and I will obey. Is there anything more I need to secure the enjoyment of your abiding

presence?" And I catch this answer: "My child, close intercourse with me every day."

Ah, there is the fault of many who try to obey and try to believe; they do it in their strength, and

they do not know that if the Lord Jesus is to reign in their hearts, they must have close

communion with Him every day. You cannot do all He desires, but Jesus will do it for you.

There are many Christians who fail here, and on that account do not understand what it is to have

fellowship with Jesus. Let me try and impress this upon you: God has given you a loving, living

Saviour, and how can He bless you if you do not meet Him? The joy of friendship is found in

intercourse; and Jesus asks for this every day, that he may have time to influence me, to tell me

of Himself, to teach me, to breathe His Spirit unto me, to give me new life and joy and strength.

And remember intercourse with Jesus does not mean half an hour, or an hour in your closet. A man may study his Bible or his commentary carefully; he may look up all the parallel passages

in the chapter; when he comes out of his closet he may be able to tell you all about it, and yet he

has never met Jesus that morning at all. You have prayed for five or ten minutes, and you have

never met Jesus. And so we must remember that though the Bible is most precious, and the

reading of it most blessed and needful, prayer and Bible reading are not fellowship with Jesus.

What we need every morning is to meet Jesus, and to say, "Lord, here is the day again, and I am

just as weak in myself as ever I was; come and feed me this morning with yourself and speak to

my soul." Oh, friends, it is not your faith that will keep you standing, but it is a living Jesus, met

every day in fellowship, worship, and love. Wait in His presence, however cold and faithless you

feel. Wait before Him and say: "Lord, helpless as I am, I believe and rest in the blessed

assurance that what you have promised you will do for me."

I ask my Master once again, "Lord Jesus, is that all?" And his answer is: "No, my child; I have

one more thing." "And what is that? You have told me to believe, and to obey, and to abide near

to you: what would you have more?" "Work for me, my child. Remember, I have redeemed you

for My service; I have redeemed you to have a witness to go out into the world confessing Me

before men." Oh, do not hide your treasure, or think that if Jesus is with you, you can hide it.

One of two things will happen- either you must give all up, or it must come out.

You have perhaps heard of the little girl, who, after one of Mr Moody's meetings, was found to

be singing some of the hymns we all know. The child's parents were in a good position in

society, and while singing those hymns in the drawing room her mother forbade her. One day

she was singing the hymn "Oh, I'm so glad that Jesus loves me," when her mother said, "My

child, how is it that you sing this when I have forbidden it?" She replied, "Oh, mother, I cannot

help it; it comes out of itself." If Jesus Christ is in the heart, He must come out.

Remember, it is not only our duty to confess Him; it is that, but it is something more.

If you do not do it, it is just an indication that you have not given yourself up to Jesus; your

character, your reputation, and you’re all. You are holding back from Him. You must confess

Jesus in the world, in your home, and everywhere. You know the Lord's Command, "Go into all

the world and proclaim the gospel to the whole creation." "And, behold, I am with you,"

meaning, "Anyone may work for Me, and I will be with him." It is true of the minister, the

missionary, and every believer who works for Jesus. The presence of Jesus is intimately

connected with work for Him. You say, "I have never thought of that before. I have my Sunday

work, but during the week I am not doing work for Him."

You cannot have the presence of Jesus and let this continue to be the case. I do not believe you

could have the presence of Jesus all week and yet do nothing for Him; therefore, my advice is to

work for Him who is worthy, His blessing and His presence will be found in the work. It is a

blessed privilege to work for Christ in this perishing world. Oh, why is it that our hearts often

feel so cold and closed up, and so many of us say, "I do not feel called to Christ's work" Be

willing to yield for the Lord's service, and He will reveal Himself to you.

Christ comes with His wondrous promise, and what He says, He says to all believers: "Behold, I

am with you always; that is My promise; this is what I in My power can do; this is what I

faithfully engage to perform; will you have it? “I give Myself to you, O soul.” To each of those

who have come to Him, Christ says, "I give Myself to you, to be absolutely and wholly your

every hour of every day; to be with you and in you every moment, to bless you and sustain you,

and to give you each moment the consciousness of My presence; I will be wholly, wholly,

wholly yours." And now, what is the other side? He wants me to be wholly His. Are you ready to

take this as your motto now, "Wholly for God"?

O God, breathe your presence in my heart that you may shine forth from my life. "Wholly for

God," let this be our motto. Come let us cast ourselves on our faces before His feet. Our

missionary from Nyasaland says he has often been touched by seeing how the native Christians

when they are brought to Jesus, do not stand in prayer; they do not kneel, but they cast

themselves upon the earth with their foreheads to the ground, and there they lie, and with loud

voices cry unto God.

I sometimes feel that I wish we could do that ourselves, but we do not need to. Let us do it in

spirit, for the everlasting son of God has come into our hearts. Are you going to take Him and

keep Him there, to give Him glory and let Him have His way? Come now and say, "I will seek

you with my whole heart; I am wholly yours."

Yield yourself entirely to Him to have complete possession. He will take and keep possession.

Come now. Jesus delights in the worship of His Saints. Our whole life can become one

continuous act of worship and work of love and joy, if we only remember and value this, that

Jesus has said, "Behold, I am with you always, to the end of the age." Matthew 28:20.

fields.title: Personal Profile
fields.body_html:
Gareth, and his wife Anne, were both born and raised in

Wales. They married in 1961 after he had received his

Bachelors of Science with honors in Physics as well as a

Diploma of Education from the University of Wales. In 1975

they immigrated to Canada where Gareth continued in his

chosen profession as a secondary school physics teacher. In

1979 he was invited to pastor a church in Kitchener, Ontario

with the Christian and Missionary Alliance.

Four years later, he received a call to Victoria, British

Columbia where he pastored for the next eight years, and

where they still reside. In 1990 Gareth was invited to serve as

the chaplain on board the Mercy Ship, M/V Anastasis,

working between Europe and West Africa. There he and

Anne ministered to the crew and had many opportunities to

speak at churches, pastors’ seminars, and missionary

conferences.

Since leaving the ship in 1994 Gareth has traveled

extensively, teaching at discipleship training schools and

various conferences. Gareth and Anne have three daughters

and nine grandchildren.

fields.title: Foreword by Keith Price
fields.body_html:
There can surely be no better recommendation for a book than

its having stood the test of clinical trial. That such a test has

been applied to the principles enunciated here is surely

adequate endorsement.

As you read these pages you will sense a shepherd’s heart.

Though a man of science, this man of God has no time for

ivory towers. Having gone through the fires of life’s uphill

experiences himself, he understands what others feel in times

of struggle.

Gareth Evans has proved these principles not only in pastoral

work in Victoria, British Columbia, but also further afield in

places as diverse as Mexico, Africa, Europe, and Australia

where he has been invited to present the material to many

different groups of churches and Christian leaders.

Because of his high view of the inspiration of the scriptures

from which he draws these lessons, I am confident that they

will retain their value until we, being made perfect, no longer

need to take the initiative to restore broken relationships.

Keith Price

Victoria, British Columbia

March, 1996

fields.title: Priorities
fields.body_html:
The Covenant Feast

It was a hot, dusty day as Peter and John, disciples of Jesus,

entered the city of Jerusalem. They had come to celebrate

Pesach, the Feast of the Passover, and were even now

following a man, carrying a pitcher of water, who would lead

them to the place where the feast was to be prepared.

As the Lord had told them, it had not been difficult to find

their guide, for the sight of a man carrying a pitcher of water

was uncommon. That was a task usually done by the women.

He led them to a pleasant two-story house where the host

greeted them warmly. When they had told him their errand,

they were ushered into a large, furnished room on the upper

floor.

It did not take them long to prepare the low-lying table since

the requirements for the feast were well known to both. Bowls

of bitter herbs were alternated with plates of apples,

cinnamon, and almonds. A flask of salt water and some boiled

eggs were placed beside the vessels of wine and there were

several portions of the unleavened bread they called

“matzah.” Soon the hour arrived and Jesus came with the rest

of the disciples.

There was a buzz of excitement and animated conversation as

they entered the upper room. This was to be a celebration

time, the happiest time of the year for all Jews; when they

were reminded again of the great faithfulness of Jehovah. Had

He not delivered them from the bondage of Egypt so many

years ago? Could He not still deliver them from the present

oppression of the Romans?

To the disciples of Jesus this time was probably even more

exciting. They were wondering if the day was near when their

master would reveal Himself to the nation as the long-awaited

Messiah who came to set them free as prophesied by the

prophets of old. They felt they were at a strategic time in the

history of their people. Indeed, this past week had been rather

unusual, and things were coming to a head. It was obvious

that the religious leaders were very shaken by both the

teachings and popularity of Jesus.

I can imagine that the conversation of the disciples was

centered entirely around the events of this past week and

wondering just what significance they had. I’m sure Peter

couldn’t stop talking about the triumphal entry into Jerusalem

just five days earlier, when the crowds had laid their garments

on the dusty road and torn branches from the palm trees to

wave, as they cried out, “Blessed is He who comes in the

name of the Lord, even the king of Israel” (John 12:13).

I can imagine him, head held high, chest out, as he led the

donkey’s colt, upon which the master sat. John and James, the

Zealots (sons of thunder), would have been more impressed

with the way their master had turned over the tables of the

money changers and driven them from the temple. “Did you

see the look on the High Priest’s face? Brother, was he mad!”

They all lowered themselves to a reclining position alongside

the table, still happy in their celebratory mood: it was party

time. Jesus looked on with pleasure as His friends celebrated,

but He knew something that had eluded their understanding:

tomorrow He would die.

What would you do if your doctor told you that you only had

a short time to live? Of course, you’d ask for a second

opinion! And if that also confirmed that you would soon leave

this world, your constant companions, and friends? I know

what I would do. I would quickly finish my present activities

and arrange to be with those most precious to me: my wife,

our daughters, and their families.

I would want to tell them how much I love them and how

proud I am of them. I would encourage them to go on with

Jesus, serving Him and living a life to the praise of His glory.

I would ask them if there is anything for which I need to

apologize to them, any hurts, any unkind words or

thoughtlessness. I would want to make very sure that there

was nothing left undone that could be done in bonding our

relationship one with the other.

I would find very little time to talk about trivial things such

as the latest sports scores or gossip, which occupy so much of

my time otherwise. Indeed, all I’d be doing would be dealing

with priorities . And that night, at the paschal feast, that is just

what the Lord was going to do with His disciples - deal with

priorities !

His Requirements

As was customary, they had all removed their shoes as they

entered this upper room. Their feet were dusty, and the sand

between their toes made them feel rather uncomfortable.

Soon a murmur of discontent could be heard. The bowls of

water were on a table near the door and there were towels

available, but where was the servant girl whose job it was to

wash their feet to refresh them? She should have been here

when they arrived!

I can imagine that it must have been Peter who would be the

first to speak out what they were all thinking. He is so much

like me - always putting his foot in his mouth! “Where’s the

girl? My feet are itching. Has someone made a mistake and

forgotten to tell her? Who planned this feast? Who’s on the

committee?” An embarrassed whispering would be heard as

the others tried to tell him to be quiet. After all, it was the

Master who had made the arrangements! And He doesn’t

make mistakes; even when we cannot understand His

purposes.

Jesus rose from the table and walked toward the bowls of

water.

“Oh good,” thought Peter, “He’s going to call the girl.”

Jesus removed His outer garment, clothed Himself with a

towel, picked up a bowl of water, and turned… towards Peter!

“Oh no,” thought Peter, “He’s going to ask me to do it!”

Instead, Jesus washes the dusty feet of Peter and then, those

of all the others, including Judas Iscariot who would betray

Him and bring about the suffering He was anticipating that

night. Can you imagine the Lord looking up into the eyes of

Judas as He washed his feet? What did He see in those eyes?

Fear? Or guilt? What did Judas see in His master’s eyes? I

wonder, was he able to look? Such love!

Jesus returned the bowl and towel to their place by the door,

put on His outer garment ,and turned toward the disciples.

“I give you an example,” He said, “as I have done to you, so

do you to one another” (John 13:1-20).

The first priority of discipleship is servanthood . We are

charged by the Lord to be servants. It is essential if we desire

to be like Him, who came not to be served, but to serve

(Matthew 20:28). It is the condition of greatness in the

Kingdom of Heaven and an evidence of being filled with the

Spirit (Ephesians 5:18,21).

I do not think that the Lord meant for us to follow Him

literally in washing one another’s feet (though that is a great

blessing to experience), but rather, that we are to seek to

refresh one another from the dust and dirt of walking in this

world. It is impossible to live in this world without some of

its dirt rubbing off on you. How seldom can one read a

newspaper, watch the television, or chat with neighbors or

colleagues without being infected by its poison? Gossiping

and grumbling, so common even among believers, soon rob

us of the joy of walking the Christian way. We need the

cleansing words, the refreshment and encouragement of other

believers. We need to have our feet washed! That is the

purpose of Christian fellowship; however, there is often just

as much ‘dirt’ thrown about among believers as among those

of the world!

Not only are we called to serve one another in the Body of

Christ, but we are also challenged to be servants to those who

would even betray our Lord and not be one of His followers.

Jesus washed the feet of Judas knowing all that was in his

heart. He saw his doubts and frustrations, knew his

politicking and deceit, yet He did not hesitate to wash his feet.

When He finished this task He invited all those who would

recognize Him as master, to do the same.

To have the attitude of a servant is not easy in our self-

centered world. It requires humility - knowing oneself as one

truly is - and acceptance of oneself. When we see ourselves

‘in Christ’ we are not threatened by what others may think of

us. Who cares what others may say when we know we are

pleasing to the Lord? Our confidence is in Him and in His

promises.

Jesus knew what His commission was, where He had come

from, and what His destiny was (John 13:3). This confidence

was the foundation of His servanthood. The Father had given

Him authority, had sent Him into the world, and would

receive Him back again.

We have the same commission and the same destiny! The

World may call us weak or spineless, trying to manipulate our

servant attitude to their own ends. They will take your coat,

compel you to go with them a mile, and make you their slave.

Jesus told us, if that should happen, to give them also your

shirt and go the second mile! In doing so, you are removing

yourself from their slavery and making yourself a voluntary

servant (Matthew 5:40-41).

Shortly after Judas had left the room to do his dirty work,

Jesus taught His disciples a second requirement. “A new

commandment I give to you, that you love one another: just

as I have loved you, you also are to love one another. By this

all people will know that you are my disciples, if you have

love for one another” (John 13:34-35). Note that this is a

commandment, not an option! Have you ever tried to measure

just how much He loves you? That is the only scale by which

He will measure how much you love “one another!”

It would be impossible if it were not for His grace and the

indwelling Holy Spirit He gives.

“To live above with those I love, O, that will be glory! To live

below with those I know - well, that’s a different story!”

(Unknown Author).

We may not like one another, but we are commanded to love

one another! That means no gossiping and no backstabbing,

but instead honoring, preferring one another, bearing one

another’s burden, and so much more…

A third requirement was placed before the disciples. “If you

love me, you will keep my commandments” (John 14:15). He

calls us to be obedient to His word. The Old Testament

prophet, Samuel, rebuked the disobedient King Saul saying,

“Has the Lord as great delight in burnt offerings and

sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the Lord? Behold, to

obey is better than sacrifice, and to listen than the fat of rams.

For rebellion is as the sin of divination, and presumption is as

iniquity and idolatry. Because you have rejected the word of

the Lord, he has also rejected you from being king” (1 Samuel

15:22-23).

Because Saul did not obey the word of the Lord God, he lost

his kingdom and authority. When Jesus spoke to the

multitudes, those who heard Him were filled with amazement

for He spoke as one having great authority (Matthew 7:28-

29).

We who recognize Him as Saviour must also acknowledge

that He is Lord. What He says has the greatest of authority.

We need to be sensitive to hear and recognize His voice day

by day. He said that we, His sheep, should recognize His

voice. Above all, we should hear Him speak to us through the

Scriptures and obey what He says. All believers should be

students of the written Word, living in obedience to its

precepts.

Jesus’ requirements for His disciples are that we serve one

another, love one another, and obey His Word.

His Promises

Besides the three requirements He placed before His

disciples, Jesus also promised them rich blessings. He would

come again and receive them to Himself having prepared a

place “in [His] Father’s house” (John 14:2) for them. They

would do greater works than He did as He would send them

another Helper and would answer the prayers they asked

according to His will. They were to know the blessing of

being in Christ , and to experience the Father’s love.

The Helper, the Holy Spirit, would come to dwell in them and

would lead them to the truth and knowledge of God’s will;

He would bring to their remembrance all they had been taught

by Jesus.

“Let not your hearts be troubled. Believe in God; believe also

in me” (John 14:1).

“Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you. Not as the

world gives do I give to you. Let not your hearts be troubled,

neither let them be afraid” (John 14:27).

“These things I have spoken to you, that my joy may be

in you, and that your joy may be full” (John 15:11).

He promised them - and us - a peace that the world cannot

give or take away, a joy whose measure is fullness, and a

presence who is none other than the Spirit Himself, never to

leave us or forsake us (Deuteronomy 31:6).

Have you experienced these in your walk with the Lord? I

certainly have, but I long for more!

The experience of these promises is contingent on us being

servants , lovers , and obedient to His Word.

fields.title: A Covenant People
fields.body_html:
The Agape Feast

“Jesus took bread and when He had given thanks, He broke it

and said, ‘This is My Body, broken for you. Take and eat!’”

(1 Corinthians 11:23-24). They all did and, in so doing,

identified themselves with the Body of Christ.

“In the same way He took the cup also, after supper, saying,

‘This cup is the new covenant in My blood; do this, as often

as you drink it, in remembrance of Me’” (1 Corinthians

11:25-26). I am struck that none of those present asked Him

what He meant when He said this. I can only assume that they

all understood.

A covenant is an agreement between two parties. “You do this

for me, and I’ll do that for you!” Today, when men make

covenants it is essential that proof be available in the form of

signatures attached to the written agreement. Sadly, the word

of a gentleman is no longer acceptable. In the time of Jesus,

covenants were sealed over a common drink. It would not

have been blood, as more recently among the Native Indians

of North America and the tribesmen of Africa, though all the

covenants of the Old Testament days would have been

signified by the shedding of blood in the slaying of a

sacrificial animal. Indeed, one was said to ‘cut the covenant’

rather than make one.

An interesting story is told concerning Dr. Livingstone, the

great pioneer missionary to Africa. He, with his guides and

bearers, was often taken captive by warrior tribesmen as they

journeyed through the dark continent.

On one occasion, the captives were brought before a hostile

chief who began to berate them for trespassing on his

territory. As he was getting angrier at Livingstone’s silence,

a guide leaned over to the missionary and urged him to ‘cut

the covenant.’ Livingstone did not understand what was being

requested, but he soon recoiled in dismay as he watched his

Christian servant and a chosen young man from the hostile

tribe, perform what was to him, a pagan act. They made a

small cut in their forearms, gathered the blood into a bowl and

drank it together!

The chief then stepped forward and took hold of the string by

which Livingstone was leading a goat, the source of the milk

he so enjoyed. Livingstone was dismayed and then surprised

as the chief pressed a gift into his hands - the copper-tipped

staff with which he had met the trespassing party. They were

then led to a hut where they would spend the night after

receiving a meal from their captors.

Some time later, while journeying through another region of

Africa, Livingstone was captured again and brought before

another hostile chief. This time, however, the chief fell on his

knees before the missionary. It was only then that

understanding came. When the young guide had ‘cut the

covenant’ on behalf of Livingstone, and had sealed it by the

drinking of blood, an agreement was made between them and

the tribe, especially between Livingstone and the chief.

As a token of that covenant agreement, the chief had given

his staff, a symbol of his commitment and support. The

second hostile chief had recognized the staff, understood that

Livingstone had a blood brother and had yielded to that

superior power and authority.

Jesus has made such a covenant with us! We can now walk

tall in this crippled world by His authority! We have a blood

brother Who shed His blood, drank it to the bitter dregs on

our behalf, and gave us the authority of His name (Acts 3:16)!

Our enemy, Satan, and his henchmen, sin and death, should

have no dominion over us (Romans 6:14)!

When Jesus invited His disciples to drink the ‘covenant cup,’

they knew they were indicating their agreement to the terms

of a new covenant. So it is every time we take the emblems

at the Lord’s table. As we eat the bread, we are declaring

ourselves to be the body of Christ . As we drink the cup, we

are covenanting again to be servants to one another, lovers of

one another, and obedient to His Word .

An Unworthy Manner

In his letter to the Corinthians, Paul exhorts us to be very

careful in taking these emblems. If we drink the Lord’s cup

“in an unworthy manner” we may well drink judgment to

ourselves, not recognizing the Lord’s body. “For this reason

many among you (believers) are weak and sick” (1

Corinthians 11:30).

If I bear animosity in my heart to another, or am not living as

a servant , lover , or in obedience , my taking of the bread and

cup is hypocrisy. I am failing to recognize the other as one

with me in the Body of Christ. This may well result in

weakness and sickness coming upon me. This is not from the

Lord - He is not the author of sickness, but I have given the

devil a foothold (2 Corinthians 2:11), and he certainly knows

how to manipulate such footholds for his advantage!

Praying for the Sick

Now I have an understanding of what James meant when he

wrote, “Is anyone among you sick? Let him call for the elders

of the church, and let them pray over him, anointing him with

oil in the name of the Lord. And the prayer of faith will save

the one who is sick, and the Lord will raise him up. And if he

has committed sins, he will be forgiven” (James 5: 14-15).

I often wondered why the elders had to be involved. Couldn’t

anyone pray? Do elders have more prayer power than loving

friends and family? I do not now believe that calling the

elders has anything to do with their prayer power, but rather

their authority . This verse must be linked with Paul’s warning

above, as they are the only verses that give any reference to

reasons why believers may be sick or weak. Of course, we

also are subject to germs, diseases, and sickness just as

anyone in the world, but Paul’s warning must be strongly

expressed to believers.

Should the elders discern that the believer’s sickness may be

associated with a wrong attitude to others in the Body of

Christ, they must exercise their authority as elders in the

church, to charge that one to be reconciled. Only then can

they pray, anointing him with oil (a symbol of the Holy

Spirit’s blessing and protection) in the name of the Lord. The

sick one - the guilty one - will be restored and forgiven.

The Lord’s Prayer

Having taught His disciples the priorities of His heart, our

Lord lifted His eyes toward Heaven and spoke to His Father.

One should take time to read John 17 to hear the cry of Jesus’

heart on the night before He died. Let me walk with you

through these wonderful words, emphasizing a major theme.

“Father, I have finished the work You gave Me to do… I have

manifested Your name (attributes) to these men… and they

have kept Your word. I ask on their behalf… for they are

Yours. They are not of the world, even as I am not of the

world. As You have sent Me into the world, I have also sent

them into the world. I do not only ask for these but also for

all who will believe in Me through their word (which includes

you and I). That they may all be one … that the world may

believe. I have given them Your glory… that they may be

one … as We are One. That they may be perfected in unity ,

that the world may know that You sent Me and that You love

them even as You love Me… I have made Your name

(attributes) known to them… that the love with which You

love Me may be in them, and I in them” (John 17).

God’s name was revealed to Moses when they met on Mount

Sinai; therefore, we can be certain that He is “ The Lord God,

merciful and gracious, longsuffering and abundant in

goodness and truth, keeping mercy for thousands, forgiving

iniquity and transgression and sin” (Exodus 34:6-7).

Truly, Jesus manifested these same attributes to all He met.

God’s Gospel Tract

I cannot take even one page out of the Bible and use it as an

evangelical tract to give to an unbelieving friend. I can quote

from John 3 or follow “The Romans Road” which explains to

them the way of salvation. I can give them the “Four Steps”

or “God’s Wonderful Plan of Salvation,” but I cannot tear one

page out of the Bible and give it away as a gospel tract.

However, I can take whole chapters and even books, to point

out God’s priorities to the believer: His way of salvation. He

has declared that when His people are walking in unity as

servants , as lovers and in obedience , the world will know and

believe !

We are His Gospel tract! It’s time we got our priorities right

and in line with His priorities! We are quick to speak when

we detect heresy of doctrine in one another - isn’t it time we

were just as quick to act against heresy of practice, seeing the

many divisions among believers, so evident to the world?

“For the anxious longing of all creation waits eagerly for the

revealing of the Sons of God” (Romans 8:19).

fields.title: The Body of Christ
fields.body_html:
One Body

“So we, though many, are one body in Christ, and

individually members one of another” (Romans 12:5).

The apostle Paul takes up the theme of the Lord’s upper room

prayer to teach us that the relationship called for in one-to-

the-other serving and loving, is best demonstrated in the

example of a living body. He sees the church as the living

Body of Christ instituted by God. It is not a man-made

organization, but a God-made organism - a living, vital

reality. It is the training and exercise ground for serving and

loving. This is why Christian fellowship is so important.

John Donne, a sixteenth century Anglican priest, wrote, “No

man is an island, entire of itself; every man is a piece of the

continent, a part of the main. If a clod be washed away by the

sea, Europe is the less, as well as if a promontory were, as

well as if a manor of thy friend’s or of thine own were: any

man’s death diminishes me, because I am involved in

mankind, and therefore never send to know for whom the bell

tolls; it tolls for thee.”

His sentiments could well be those of a member of the Body

of Christ, recognizing his interdependence on all other parts

of that body.

Islam teaches that Mohammed was called by God to complete

what Jesus failed to do! Muslims recognize Jesus as a great

prophet, second only to Mohammed, but they believe He

failed in that He was not able to make all people into one

nation. Islam calls peoples of all nations to be one as

Muslims. They have failed to understand that the unity Jesus

came to bring was for those who are members of His

kingdom, and not one of this world. How tragic that there is

such obvious disunity in that kingdom. No wonder Islam is

growing so rapidly!

At conversion, the new birth, we were, “by one Spirit all

baptized into one body” (1 Corinthians 12:13). This includes

Baptists, Anglicans, Pentecostals, and whatever group you

belong to. Not the denominations, but the individuals within

all such groups who know the Lord as a personal Savior, and

know their sins are forgiven through the work finished on

Calvary. The baptism into the Body must not be confused

with the baptism into the Spirit, experienced by the disciples

on the day of Pentecost, and by many since that day. The

former is “by the Spirit into the Body” whereas the latter is

“by the Lord Jesus into the Spirit” (Luke 3:16). We are to be

“in Christ” for justification, and Christ is to be “in us” for

sanctification.

Fullness of the Spirit

One major division in the body is due to various doctrines

concerning this baptism of the Spirit.

Are tongues the initial evidence of being so filled? Are they

evidence at all? I am not getting into that argument except to

say that, whichever view we hold, we should not make our

disagreement a cause for division, that way we are certainly

not exhibiting the reality of any fullness of the Holy Spirit!

He comes to make the presence of Christ, and His will, real

to us. He leads us into truth. I find it rather striking that, when

Paul exhorts us to be “filled with the Spirit” (Ephesians 5:18),

he follows by giving us three evidences of a life so filled:

1. A worshiping attitude speaking to one another in psalms,

hymns, and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in

your heart to the Lord (Ephesians 5:19).

2. A thankful attitude always giving thanks for all things in

the name of our Lord Jesus Christ to God, even the Father

(Ephesians 5:20).

3. A servant attitude and be subject to one another in the fear

of Christ (Ephesians 5:21).

Don’t tell me that you are a Spirit-filled Christian unless these

three are evident in your life!

Paul then continues in his letter to the Ephesians by showing

how this third evidence is worked out in our relationships as:

husband and wife, children and parents, and workers and

masters (Ephesians 5:22-6:9).

The Local Church

I am not among those who consider denominations as such to

be evil. I believe that the Lord established most of them to

enable us to mature as believers within a group of people most

like us in personality and persuasion; however, when our

groupings cause us to be divided from those within the Body

of Christ who do not share our opinions concerning styles of

worship, interpretation of Scriptures, and emphases, we are in

danger of bringing condemnation upon ourselves. We may

not like one another, but we are commanded to love one

another!

There are three major Scripture portions where the apostle

outlines his understanding of the Body of Christ.

1. Ephesians 4:1-16 → We are challenged to walk in a

manner worthy of our calling showing humility, gentleness,

patience, love, and being diligent to preserve the unity of the

Spirit in the bond of peace. For, he declares, “There is ONE

BODY” (Ephesians 4:4). He continues by writing about some

of the grace gifts in verse seven given to that Body. They are

ministry gifts of apostles, prophets, evangelists, pastors, and

teachers, which are given “for the equipping of the saints…

unto maturity” (Ephesians 4:13).

2. Romans 12:1-8 → We are challenged again to give

ourselves as living sacrifices with renewed minds. All

members of the Body do not have the same function, but we

are all interdependent on one another. We all have different

grace gifts (Romans 12:6) with which to serve one another.

Therefore, we must, “Let love be genuine. Abhor what is evil;

hold fast to what is good. Love one another with brotherly

affection. Outdo one another in showing honor” (Romans

12:9-10).

3. 1 Corinthians 12-14 → We cannot separate chapters 12

and 14 from that great chapter on love, chapter 13! The first

fields.title: Chapter Deals With
fields.body_html:
charismata given to that Body. Note that these charismata are

given to the individual, not for their own use, but for the

benefit of the whole Body!

Then Paul expands on his teaching concerning the Body by

showing just how foolish it is for one part of the Body to

claim that they do not need the other parts! The eye cannot

say to the hand, “I have no need of you” or again the head to

the feet, “I have no need of you” (1 Corinthians 12:21). We

need one another!

At the end of this chapter, he gathers together the lists of grace

gifts he recorded in Ephesians and Romans showing them all

to be among his long list of charismata .

Such gifts are of little value unless exercised with love (1

Corinthians 13) and properly in an orderly manner (1

Corinthians 14).

Are you fully functioning in the Body of Christ? Are you

grounded in a local church, serving others, loving others, and

obedient to His Word? If your ministry is wider than the local

church, are you in the right relationship with God to appoint

leaders, and be accountable to them as a member of the same

local expression of the Body?

Some might seek to be an arm reaching out, others a voice

speaking to this world, but I often see myself as nothing more

glamorous than a big toe! As a former pastor, I was often

working in dark and smelly places, feeling under pressure,

dealing with peoples’ problems (sand between the toes).

However, I feel I am privileged when asked to minister

because I get to bring balance to the Body. That surely, is the

main function of the big toe!

fields.title: The Tragic Truth
fields.body_html:
God’s desire, and the priority on the heart of Jesus, is that He

will have a people whose love for one another, and attitude of

servanthood will be such a witness to this world that men and

women will be crying out to know our Lord. They will want

to know the secret of our peace, joy, and harmony. They will

watch our marriages, homes, children, and workplaces, not to

criticize, but to know our secrets.

Having urged his readers to be “filled with the Spirit,” and

expressing one evidence of being so filled, as being “subject

to one another in the fear of Christ” (Ephesians 5:21),Paul

gives examples of how this should be in our relationships.

Christian Marriage → Ephesians 5:22-33

If Christian marriages were what they are supposed to be,

with both parties Spirit-filled and submitted to one another,

honoring, and preferring the other, they would be the mystery

revealed to a watching world. Men would see the relationship

that Jesus has with His bride, the church, and would be drawn

to know Him as the foundation for his marriage also. There

would be a steady path of seekers coming to our home or

church door, rather than rushing, as they now do, to the

divorce courts!

Women would want to honor their own husband above all

other men, because of the love they receive, and men would

want to love their wives because of the honor they receive.

Rather than a vicious circle of abuse and retaliation which is

so common in the world, there would be a delicious circle of

blessing one another in Christ.

It is so tragic that divorce is so common among Christian

believers. What kind of witness is that?

The Christian Home → Ephesians 6:1-4

Where parents are in the right relationships with the Lord and

with one another, their children mature in a secure, loving

home. Most of the counseling I do as a pastor has to do with

wounds received by children growing up in a rather different

situation, though often “Christian” fathers fail to disciple (or

discipline) their children and, instead, provoke them to anger

(Colossians 3:21).

Christian counselors today speak of dysfunctional families

where the child’s ‘love tank’ is not filled with the love it was

created to receive, because the dysfunctional parents are

incapable of providing that love. The child does not

experience the love whose fruit is security, identity, self-

esteem, acceptance, and encouragement. The child does not

experience the love whose fruit is security, identity, self-

esteem, acceptance, and encouragement.

Instead of growing up emotionally and spiritually healthy,

they become just like their parents, dysfunctional. They never

learn to walk tall in a world of bowed shoulders and broken

hearts. The empty space in their love tank is filled with one

thing: anger, which produces a life of rebellion to God’s

purposes. Such children never learn to obey their parents in

the Lord.

“Fathers, do not provoke your children to anger” (Colossians

3:21).

It is so tragic that so many rebellious children are the product

of “Christian” homes. What kind of witness is that?

The Workplace → Ephesians 6:5-9

The Spirit-filled believer is called to be a witness in his

workplace by displaying the attitude of a servant before his

co-workers and employers and should be trustworthy to do

his work well.

I am familiar with a teacher whose school was to be

amalgamated with two others in a major reorganization. All

the teachers from the three schools gathered together to form

a Staff Association to speak on the teachers’ behalf to the

School Governors, expressing their desires for the design of

the new school buildings and their terms of employment.

One man was nominated and seconded for the position of

president for this new association. Another was nominated

and seconded. Then, much to his surprise, my friend was

nominated. Immediately, the two others who had been

nominated withdrew their names in order to second my

friend’s nomination. No other names were presented and he

was elected unanimously to represent all the staff. As he left

the room he expressed amazement to a colleague. “Just wait

till I tell my wife,” he said. “She’ll never believe me!” “Why

not?” replied the colleague, “We all know you’re the only one

we can trust to always speak the truth!”

My friend was the only Christian on the senior staff of those

schools.

Sadly, I am often told by business men (Christians among

them) that the worst people to do business with are Christians.

They want the most out of you for the least payment. They

are the poorest at giving tips, and often the last in settling

debts! Of course, it may well be that we are judged more

harshly by the world than non-believers are, but that is to be

expected!

We are called to have the attitude of servants. We should be

living at a higher level of commitment and workmanship than

the world! Sadly, we all know of Christian employers and

workers who do not display a Spirit-filled work ethic or

relationship with their colleagues. What kind of witness is

that?

Worker Attrition

Most relevant research reveals that the number one reason for

missionaries to leave the field is poor interpersonal

relationships! They have studied for many years in Bible

Schools and language seminaries, interned in home churches,

invested a large portion of their lives in preparation, and, after

one term overseas, have returned home bitter, disillusioned,

embarrassed, and hurt. This ought not to be!

In North America, the average tenure for a pastor in a local

church is fewer than five years. The first year is honeymoon,

the second, familiarity. In the third year, disillusionment sets

in with rumblings of discontent; both the pastor and the

church members have unfulfilled expectations of one another.

The fourth year sees the discontent come to the surface, often

with acrimony and accusations. People take sides, a lot of heat

is generated, and the pastor leaves, usually saying, “I don’t

have to put up with this!” What kind of witness is that?

Church Fights

Have you ever been involved in a church fight? It is not a

pleasant thing! I know of one church, once over three hundred

people, now non-existent. Everyone in that town seems to

know some aspect of the story, and there are many people,

once faithful in attendance, who say that they will never

attend a church again!

The wounds are real because the fighting was bitter. Believers

would fire ‘gunshots’ at one another assassinating one

another, which reverberated all around the town. Satan

gloated, and the Lord wept!

Of course, most of our fighting is kept indoors, or is more

subtle. I read an interesting newspaper article where it told of

a group of ministers establishing support groups for pastors

who had grievances against their church or church

organization. It told of ministers in one denomination, who

were “suing for big money,” and then added that churches are

a lot more brutal to their pastors than businesses are to their

employees, and that the most vicious are in the evangelical

tradition (Christian Week (Canada), June 21, 94).

Look at the Saturday evening church ads in your local

newspaper to see how we compete with one another in the

arena of winning more people to our church - usually from

some other church! It is well documented that most church

growth is transfer growth, not conversion growth. Personal

anecdotes are not to be commended, but I once had an

interesting experience worth recounting.

It was early in the university year and all the local pastors

were invited to meet with the students to tell them about our

churches. We were given two minutes each to make our pitch.

I listened as, one after the other, pastors extolled the virtues

of their churches. “We have a wonderful ‘College and Career

Group’ and can send our bus to pick you up.” “You’ll really

enjoy our music - it’s up-beat, just as young people like it!”

“Most of your fellow students attend our church since we are

located near the campus.” I was roughly the 30th pastor in the

line-up, and was pastoring a small, struggling work. When I

stood, I told the students that we were a small church with no

special programs. We had nothing to offer them, except work

if they wanted to help us reach our neighborhood for Christ.

I sat down - and the students broke into applause!

As the church grew, a substantial number of our congregation

were university students. Why do we compete with one

another for the sheep when we all serve the same Great

Shepherd? What kind of witness is that?

Why do we find it so difficult to honor one another, to love ,

and serve one another? Is it simply our pride getting in the

way while, at the same time, we speak about being filled with

the Spirit? Or are we just ignorant of the fact that we are in a

battle, and that the enemy is very cunning?

Be very sure of this! If it is the Lord’s priority to have a people

in right relationships with one another in obedience to His

Word, it certainly is Satan’s priority to mar such

relationships! “Divide and conquer,” might as well be his

motto.

fields.title: The Devices of Satan
fields.body_html:
When Jesus died on the cross and then rose again, He

conquered Satan and his demonic hosts, taking away all their

power, “having disarmed the powers and authorities He made

a show of them openly” (Colossians 2:15). They now wage

war through lies, deceit, and fear which he works into all

areas of our lives: our attitudes, emotions, thoughts, and even

the physical.

However, they only have power in these areas as we give it

to them! The apostle Paul declared that we are not ignorant of

his devices (2 Corinthians 2:11), but unfortunately that is just

not true for the majority of believers today!

The Devil’s Opportunity

Have you ever been angry? Of course you have. Me too. And

so was Jesus when He saw the money changers in the temple.

I’m sure He was also angry when He saw the multitudes in

deep poverty and with much sickness. His heart grieved when

He saw the results of the disobedience of Adam falling on all

mankind. The feeling of anger is not sin. Feelings are not

moral or immoral - they are amoral. What we do with our

feelings, however, does matter, greatly. Paul exhorts us that

when we are angry we must not sin. Then continues to add,

“and do not let the sun go down on your anger” (Ephesians

4:26).

We must deal with the situation right away. If we allow the

anger within to fester, it will produce a bitterness that will rob

us of God’s best. As long as we are in this world, people will

do us wrong, and offenses will come. Jesus warned us of that

(Luke 17:1). There might be a ‘good’ cause behind our anger

within us, but He has given us His Holy Spirit to enable us to

know grace in those times.

“Strive for peace with everyone, and for the holiness without

which no one will see the Lord. See to it that no one fails to

obtain the grace of God; that no ‘root of bitterness’ springs up

and causes trouble, and by it many become defiled” (Hebrews

12: 15).

If we do not deal with the anger in the appropriate way (which

we will discuss later), we are playing right into the hands of

the enemy! Paul continues by saying “and do not give the

devil an opportunity” (Ephesians 4:27). Later, in the same

portion of Scripture dealing with our conversations with one

another, he warns us that we may be grieving the Holy Spirit

(Ephesians 4:30).

When we bear anger (or other wrong attitudes), the enemy

has access to our thoughts, spreading his lies and deceit to

drive a wedge further in. Soon it appears that reconciliation is

impossible, and he has won that battle.

Jesus warned us to be on our guard (Luke 17:3) and Paul

charged us to be sure that no advantage be taken of us by

Satan (2 Corinthians 2:11). Both are in the context of

forgiveness to those whom we perceive as having wronged

us. An attitude of unforgiveness (like anger) gives the enemy

an advantage - an opportunity - a foothold in our life. The

opposite attitudes of forgiveness and peace defeat him.

The Roaring Lion

Have you ever seen a lion stalking its prey? I haven’t, but I

assume it is much like my cat stalking the birds or mice in our

garden. He crouches very low and moves very slowly so as

not to warn his intended prey of his intentions. He certainly

doesn’t let them know he is coming by making a loud meow!

What, then, does the apostle Peter mean when he tells us to

“Be sober-minded; be watchful. Your adversary the devil

prowls around like a roaring lion, seeking someone to

devour” (1 Peter 5:8)?

In “Pilgrim’s Progress” by John Bunyan, we read that Pilgrim

was approaching the Palace Beautiful which was built for the

relief and security of believers. He now understood why

Timorous and Mistrust, others seeking the Celestial City, had

fled past him in great fear, for the entranceway was guarded

by two lions.

Immediately, Pilgrim’s heart sank and he also became afraid.

If a lion came bounding into your room and roared at you, I

imagine you would react like them - full of fear! I would!

Roaring lions have that effect on us - they are very

frightening.

Soon, Pilgrim noticed that both lions were chained and that,

so long as he walked a narrow path between them, neither

could reach him to cause him harm. We need to understand

that the lion, Satan, has had his teeth pulled and is chained.

He cannot harm the people of God so long as we keep to the

narrow way. Even when we step off the narrow way, the

Father’s love reaches out to bring us back before the enemy

can destroy us. However, he will roar, and many are defeated

by their emotions reacting to the roar.

His roar is often that of the accuser, bringing condemnation.

It was the first time Mary had sung the solo parts in the youth

choir. It went well except for that high note in the chorus

where she was a little weak and wobbly. It was only a quiet

voice whispering in her ear that told her, “You made a fool of

yourself,” but it was the roar of the lion. She vowed never to

sing in public again.

Pastor John had such high hopes when he began ministry at

St. Peter’s church. Now, just two years later he was leaving.

The youth group had not grown in numbers as the senior

pastor had expected, so John was invited to leave. The lion

roared, “you’ll never be successful as a pastor. You’re a

failure!” A week later, he reapplied for the secular job he had

left when he first believed that God had called him into the

pastorate.

Alec had slipped again. He so longed to be free from this

filthy habit of smoking, but it was too tempting when he’d

been offered this cigarette. Now he was feeling guilty, and the

lion roared, “God can’t use you. You’re always letting Him

down!”

Not only does the lion roar at every slip or failure, but he

knows which of our emotions are the most likely to be

affected by the roar. For some it is the emotion of guilt, for

others, it’s fear. Many react to his roar in the emotions of low

self-esteem, lacking confidence. Where do you react?

How sad when the roar of the lion comes through the

thoughtless comment of another believer! It is important in

the Body of Christ to affirm one another to counteract the lies

- the roar of the devil!

The Archer

When one is about to wage a battle, it is good to occupy the

high ground. This enables you to see their moves so that you

can take the appropriate steps to counteract them. We need to

understand as believers, the tremendous privilege we have of

being “in Christ.” Paul declares that God has “exalted Jesus,

far above every rule and authority and power and dominion”

(Ephesians 1:21).

To the Jews, these are the names of the ranks of the demonic

army of Satan, but all of them are far beneath His feet. He has

crushed the head of their master and has all authority over

them. He wills us to exercise that authority so that we may

learn to be overcomers. Those that would reign with Him

must be worthy to wear a crown, and crowns are only to be

given to the overcomers.

“[Christ has] raised us up with him and seated us with him in

the Heavenly places in Christ Jesus” (Ephesians 2:6).

We must live on that higher ground where the only way Satan

can reach us is by firing his fiery arrows. We have also been

provided with a sure defense against those flaming missiles

when Paul writes, “In all circumstances take up the shield of

faith, with which you can extinguish all the flaming darts of

the evil one” (Ephesians 6:16)

As the enemy would throw his lies and accusations against

us, we hold up our shield of faith, remembering that “faith

comes by hearing… the Word of God” (Romans 10:17).

We need to know who we are and the privileges of being “ in

Christ .”

I am…

● A child of God (John 1:12).

● A friend of Jesus (John 15:15).

● A joint-heir with Christ (Romans 8:17).

● Joined to the Lord (1 Corinthians 6:17).

● A member of His Body (Ephesians 5:30).

● Reconciled to God (2 Corinthians 5:18).

● God’s handiwork (Ephesians 2:10).

● A citizen of Heaven (Philippians 3:20).

● A new creation (2 Corinthians 5:17).

● Chosen by God (Colossians 3:12).

● A saint (Ephesians 1:1).

● A stranger to this world (1 Peter 2:11).

● What I am (1 Corinthians 15:10).

● Satan’s enemy (1 Peter 5:8).

● Clothed in righteousness (Ephesians 4:24).

● God’s dwelling place (1 Corinthians 3:16).

● A member of a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy

nation, and a people for God’s own possession (1 Peter 2:9-

10).

In Christ I…

● Am completely forgiven (Romans 5:1).

● Am greatly blessed (Ephesians 1:3).

● Am chosen to be holy (Ephesians 1:4).

● Am sealed by His Spirit (Ephesians 1:13).

● Am predestined to be His child (Ephesians 1:5).

● Have Christ within me (Colossians 1:27).

● Am made complete (Colossians 2:10).

● Am bought back from Satan (Ephesians 1:7).

● Am seated in Heavenly places (Ephesians 2:6).

● Am free from condemnation (Romans 8:1).

● Have direct access to God (Ephesians 2:18).

● May come to God confidently (Ephesians 3:12).

For a more complete list, read your Bible!

It used to be that there was a simple remedy for most minor

ailments, “Just take two aspirins and go to bed!” Today, I

have a simple remedy for most of the minor attacks of the

enemy to offer.

Take two of the above Scriptures each day and meditate on

them. Your faith will soon grow strong, and the fiery arrows

will be less effective against you.

fields.title: Unneeded Baggage
fields.body_html:
“Therefore, since we are surrounded by so great a cloud of

witnesses, let us also lay aside every weight, and sin which

clings so closely, and let us run with endurance the race that

is set before us” (Hebrews 12:1).

Many are hindered in the battle, not because of the roaring

lion or the arrows of lies, but because they have taken upon

themselves a burden that they should not be carrying; they

have been offended by someone and have taken umbrage.

I was at a viewing place, looking down on Gibraltar. There

were many signs warning viewers not to feed the small

monkeys that lived in the surrounding trees. Of course, some

people chose to ignore the signs with the result that soon, a

monkey would land on one’s shoulders. While cameras were

in action, the monkey would begin to tangle its fingers in the

hair so that, when it became painful, the recipient found

difficulty in its removal.

Satan has an army of trained ‘monkeys’ ready to jump on

one’s shoulder to tangle their fingers in their victim’s hair.

We need to recognize the monkey of offense and quickly

remove it before it robs us of our peace.

Many are hindered in the battle, not because they have been

‘wounded’ by others, but because they have taken upon

themselves a burden that they should not be carrying. They

have been offended by someone and have ‘taken umbrage.’

We must realize that offense and sin are very different.

Though the former may be a ‘fruit’ of the sinful life, it is not

a deliberate sinful act of the one who offends. Indeed, we are

told that Jesus was an ‘offense’ to the religious leaders of His

time, and He was without sin. It is my belief that He

deliberately caused offense on more than one occasion, as I

shall present to you shortly.

There may be many causes for offense, but the following are

the most common:

● Personality clashes : People will often use this phrase as

an ‘excuse’ for not getting along with one another!

● False expectations : Probably, the number one reason

pastors and churches separate. We are not very good at

making our expectations known before offense occurs.

● Misunderstandings : Poor communication.

● Gifts and talents : I often see people envy others’

prominence, instead of feeling secure in their own ministry or

‘calling.’

● Pride : An affront to one’s ‘ego.’ (for example: a father

who is angered (offended) by his son’s average grades in

school, believing it reflects poorly on himself).

● Rebellion : The ‘old man’ refuses to die!

A great example of these offenses at work was when a church

was undergoing a renovation - they were rebuilding their

sanctuary. It had been two long years of hard work for the

congregation who were building this church, but God had

proven Himself to be faithful.

There were many stories of ‘miracles’ of provision from

Jehovah Jireh. It was now time to decide the color scheme for

the interior of the sanctuary, so a small committee was formed

of members of the church and John, art master at the local

school, was asked to lead the group. At their first meeting,

John arrived with a portfolio outlining his suggestions (some

say ‘decisions’) for the color scheme. It was not long before

others present expressed their disagreement with his

proposals, having some opinions of their own.

Finally, a vote was taken and a consensus decision made -

that did not reflect the art teacher’s views. John was offended

and the reverberations of his offense were felt in that church

for some time afterwards. Indeed, some even said that that

was when the ‘miracles’ ceased.

John is no different than all of us! It is so easy to be offended

without realizing the terrible negative impact this can have on

ourselves and on the work of Christ. It is a major weapon used

by Satan in defeating us in the battle. Be sure of this - offenses

will come (Luke 17:1). Jesus told us of their certainty and

warned us how we can be kept from stumbling at the offense:

by responding to His requirements for discipleship, made in

the Upper Room

Let us look at some Biblical examples of people who were

offended. We shall seek the cause and note the results of their

offense. Hopefully, we shall also discern the Lord’s purposes

in allowing the offenses to come. He has promised to deliver

us from the ‘evil one,’ but has never promised to deliver us

from offenses! He would, however, teach us to recognize the

offense and to receive His grace in such times of testing.

The various translations of the New Testament can confuse

us on this topic, so let us understand that the Greek word,

“skandalon” is variously translated as “a stumbling block.” In

other words, “an offense,” or “a falling away.”

The Sower and the Seed → Matthew 13:18-21

In the verses above, Jesus teaches a crowd this well known

parable as well as interprets the parable for them, likening the

four types of soil to four types of hearers of the God’s Word.

The ‘stony places’ describes the person who “hears the word

and immediately receives it with joy, yet he has no root in

himself, but endures for a while, and when tribulation or

persecution arises on account of the word, immediately he

falls away” (Matthew 13:20-21).

This is a believer who doesn’t like what the Bible teaches

him. He had anticipated that being a Christian would be easy!

He wanted joy and peace, but wasn’t prepared to take up his

cross (Matthew 16:24), to pay the price of servanthood. By

and by, he is offended and falls away, the result being no fruit !

A Prophet Without Honour → Matthew 13:54-57

Jesus came to His own town of Nazareth where He taught in

the synagogue. His neighbors were astonished at His

teaching, questioning where He received such wisdom. “Isn’t

this the carpenter’s son?” they said. “We’ve known him since

childhood! Who does he think he is?” There is a common

phrase, ‘familiarity often breeds contempt’ and as we read in

verse 57, those from Jesus’ hometown “took offense at Him.”

How many young men and women, responding to God’s call

on their lives, have tried to answer that call, but have been

hindered by the greater ‘wisdom’ of their neighbors:family,

friends, and church leaders! I am reminded of the old prophet

in 1 Kings 13 who was offended because God was using

another young man to proclaim His word. Because of his

offense, the old prophet deceived the young man, the result

being the silencing of his witness, through death!

As a result of their offense in Nazareth, “he did not do many

mighty works there, because of their unbelief” (Matthew

13:58). A sure way to stop the Lord moving in miraculous

ways in your life, is to take offense. The result of their being

offended was no miracles !

The Betrayer → Matthew 26:6-14

Jesus was at the home of Simon, a leper, when a woman came

in with an expensive box of perfumed ointment. She broke it

over the Lord’s feet and began to wipe them with her hair, so

that the fragrance filled the house. Matthew tells us that the

disciples were offended when they saw this ‘waste,’ declaring

that the perfume could have been sold for a high price and the

money given to the poor (Matthew 26:8).

Just after this, Judas Iscariot went to the chief priests in order

to betray his master (Matthew 26:14-16). In John’s account

of this event, we are told it was Judas himself, who made the

complaint, being offended, “not because he cared about the

poor, but because he was a thief, and having charge of the

money bag he used to help himself to what was put into it”

(John 12:6).

I remember when a well-known international charity spent

over one million dollars to make a documentary film about

their work. Many of their supporters expressed indignation at
