slave, but by giving him your coat also, you make yourself

his servant. If he wrongs you by forcing you to go a mile, he

makes you his slave, but by going two miles, you make

yourself his servant (Matthew 5:40-41). If he wounds your

soul, you become an emotional slave, but by praying for him,

you become his servant.

The first call of discipleship is to become a servant , just as

Jesus was for you.

Be Open to Reconciliation

Should there be an opportunity to be reconciled to the one

who wounded you, do not let apprehension or fear hinder you.

The Lord’s priority is not just the healing, which blesses you,

but the reconciliation which blesses Him!

Walk Out Your Healing

Each day, take upon yourself all the armor of God of God as

found in Ephesians 6:10-18. Make this a conscious action,

even speaking out as you do it. “I take on the belt of truth so

that my ‘inner man’ may not be wounded by the lies of the

enemy. I take on the breastplate of righteousness so that the

enemy may never cause my heart to be divided in its

commitment and love for the Lord” and so forth. Only the

“pure in heart” shall see God - those whose hearts are

unalloyed with the dross of this world (Matthew 5:8).

Give Each Wound to the Great Physician

Just as surely as the enemy knows where your wounds are, so

does the Lord. He felt your pain when you were hurt and

longs for your healing; however, He has given the key to you.

As you begin to use it, He is very willing to assist in the

walking out of the healing. As He has revealed the wounds to

you, so He removes the bondages and brings wholeness in

their place, after all, He is the “Great Physician,” the healer,

who took up our infirmities and carried our sorrows and, by

whose wounds we are healed (Isaiah 53:4-5).

Lastly, thank Him for His healing!

fields.title: Chapter 1. An Introduction To Prayer
fields.body_html:
You can only know how to pray if you first know what prayer is!

Have you ever wondered what prayer is, why people pray, or why some always pray like it’s the

most important thing in their life? If so, this book is for you! Many people have learned about

prayer and been blessed by what they were taught. However, some still have questions about it. I

believe this book will answer most if not all, questions about prayer. So why the wait, let's go

right in!

What is prayer?

1. Prayer is an honour, a privilege to fellowship and be in oneness with God. Being in

oneness in this case means that one knows what is at God’s heart and is able to do w hat

God tells him. With this oneness, you can know the mind of Christ, live like Christ, think

like Him, and be perfect as He is. That is what prayer does, it helps you be in that

fellowship, that oneness with God where you can know what to do in every situation in

life. How cool that is!

2. Prayer is a two-way channel. God speaks to us and we are also privileged to talk to Him.

So, prayer is never and shouldn’t ever be considered a one -sided channel where we pray

and walk away. No! God speaks too, and this is the sole purpose of prayer, to commune

with God, know Him better, and get to know what His will is. In your prayer times,

intentionally give God room to talk to you too. That is how you know His heart, and will.

Hallelujah!

3. Prayer is also a necessity. Luke 18:1 says: “Men ought always to pray, and not to faint”

Clearly, this is not a request. The scripture doesn’t say men shall, may, can, or might

pray. Rather, it says that men ought to pray and not faint. This means that prayer must be

a part of your day; prayer times can also be the most interesting times in your day. So, let

prayer be your lifestyle; just like how you eat even when you don’t feel like it.

Jesus Christ, the perfect example

Though He knew He was the son of the Most High God, Jesus was humble enough to pray. We

see this in Luke 6:12: “In these days he went out to the mountain to pray, and all night he

continued in prayer to God.”

Beloved, never be too busy to pray, and never think of a time you don’t need to pray anymore.

P rayer is the pulse of every believer’s life. Without prayer, you cannot commune with God as

Jesus did. Without prayer, you might not know what the Father’s will for your life is. Without

prayer, it might be impossible for you to exercise your authority in Christ. This means taking up

authority and causing the things that are in Christ Jesus to happen. You may also struggle to

activate and walk in the consciousness of the divine presence in your life, and many more

aspects that we will explain in our next chapters.

fields.title: Chapter 2. Importance Of Prayer
fields.body_html:
Once you know how amazing something is, you can’t be forced to desire it!

There is an avalanche of benefits of prayer. As a student, knowing this is important because you

will then be guided on what to expect. By learning how to pray, your spirit will be so ignited to

pray more than ever. As you read what this chapter entails, let your heart and spirit be meek and

open enough to feed your spirit. Take a look at these importances of prayer and let your spirit be

so merry!

1. Prayer helps us commune with God. How beautiful to be one with God, united with the

creator of all things, knowing what’s on His mind and knowing how exactly you can

fulfil what He wants on Earth. This is so amazing!

2. Did you know that sometimes people don’t face the repercussions for their actions

because someone or some people have prayed to God to have mercy upon this guilty

person? That is how powerful prayer is! Your Dad, Mom, any relative or friend might

have done something you don’t even think God can forgive; something big the whole

world can be against, but through prayer, you can ask God to have mercy on them, and

God hears when we pray. God can save your family and friends from the punishment

they would have served for their actions. Glory to God! Here is a very good example in

the Bible where Jesus prayed to God and lives were forgiven.

“And when they came t o the place that is called The Skull, there they crucified him, and

the criminals, one on his right and one on his left. And Jesus said, “Father, forgive them,

for they know not what they do.” Luke 23:33 -34.

So, if you have someone you would like God to forgive, go ahead and pray for them. God

can have mercy on them and even get rid of the punishment they would have served had

you not prayed.

3. The other importance of prayer is that it helps us to focus on God.

“Set your minds on things that are above, not on things that are on earth.” Colossians

3:2. We can set our minds on things above through prayer because prayer helps us focus,

and see what God sees. Man and God are spirits so in prayer, you focus on spiritual

things because you are in fellowship with God, who is a Spirit.

4. When we pray, the Holy Spirit also gives us instructions and guidance. Romans 8:26

says, “Likewise the Spirit helps us in our weakness. For we do not know what to pray for

as we ought, but the Spirit himself intercedes for us with g roanings too deep for words.”

Since the Holy Spirit knows the will of the Father in Heaven, He helps us communicate

the will of the Father and in so, we receive guidance on how to successfully accomplish

or do God’s will. Isn’t that beautiful? Without the Holy Spirit, it’s impossible to fully

understand God’s will.

Acts 13:2 shows us how the disciples received instruction from the Holy Spirit as they

were in fellowship with Him.

“While they were worshiping the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said, “Set apart for me

Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them.”

This is why every Christian should pay attention to the Holy Spirit and listen to Him.

When you pray, let the Holy Spirit guide you because He knows what God wants and

what you need.

5. In prayer, we win! Hallelujah! Blessed be God! As a Christian, it’s important to know

that everything that happens in the physical world first happens in the spiritual. When we

pray, God makes us stronger. We have a special power from Him that helps us succeed

and stay healthy. This power allows us to step on dangerous things, cast out demons in

Jesus' name, and do things that seem impossible to others.

Are you facing a problem? Pray and believe that things will get better each day. God

listens when we pray, and He answers. He has good plans for us, and He helps us

overcome even the toughest challenges.

6. Prayer anchors us. As Christians, we don’t pray to make God change— He never changes.

We also don’t pray to get His attention because we are already impor tant to Him. We are

always in His sight. Praise God! Instead, prayer helps us focus on Him. It reminds us that

we are safe with Him, no matter what. That is why it’s so important to pray all the time,

so we don’t give up or lose hope , but stay connected to God. Take a look at this scripture

in Luke 18:1, “And he told them a parable to the effect that they ought always to pray

and not lose heart.”

7. When we pray, we can speak things into existence. Your life is your responsibility, and

God has given you the Holy Spirit and His Word so you can shape your world. Who you

are and what you experience are a result of your words. With God’s Word, you can

change situations and create new things.

When God made you, He created you in His own image, which means He wants you to

be like Him — a creator. You have the power to create your own reality. For example, you

can refuse to be sick because the one whose image you bear (God) can never be sick. You

can choose to live a great life every day, no matter how you feel.

Some people say life has ups and downs, but I ask them, "Where does the Bible say

that?" That’s not how it should be for a believer. Once I learned the truth, my life has

only been going upward and forward! Praise the Lord! You have control over your life

and everything in it. It’s possible to live a life of continuous success, season after season,

year after year.

Speak over your life and take advantage of what God has given you. Remember, God

doesn’t want you to write a new Bible; He w ants you to understand His Word and live by

it. Declare prosperity and abundance with your own mouth because you are the prophet

of your own life! Hallelujah!

fields.title: Chapter 3. Types Of Prayer
fields.body_html:
“Open your mouth, and I will fill it” Psalm 81:10

Did you know how important it is to pray for yourself, your family, your neighbourhood, and

even for nations and their leaders? Yes, it’s really important! Also, did you know that we pray

differently depending on the season of life we are in? That’s right , because each season has its

own needs.

The Bible says in Ecclesiastes that there is a time for everything, so if it's a time for joy and you

are living in sorrow, you are tuning your spirit the wrong way. This is why I am going to explain

the different types of prayer and when to use them. This way, you will know how to pray in each

season of your life and bring about the right changes! Are you excited? Perfect, let us take a look

at these types of prayer.

Prevailing Prayer

Have you ever prayed, finished, and then felt like you should keep praying about something

specific? It could be about your friend, your cousin, your cat or dog at home, a specific study

subject, a teacher, or anything else.

Sometimes, you feel at peace that everything is taken care of after praying, but other times, you

might sense that you need to keep praying, even though you have just finished praying. This can

happen when the Holy Spirit is guiding you to continue praying for a certain person, situation, or

issue. It doesn’t mat ter whether you're praying in tongues or in your regular language — the

important thing is that you are being led to pray more. I want to talk to you about this kind of

prayer: the prevailing prayer.

I remember one time when I went to a barbecue event with a friend, and for some reason, he

went to the bar. I was shocked to see him, a Christian, confidently sitting in that bar like how one

would sit on a cosy couch. I exclaimed, “Dear Lord Jesus!” Thoug h I tried to talk him out of that

bar, nothing seemed to work. Then, I knew I wouldn’t verbally convince him out of that bar. I

went to the car, locked it, and made it my prayer closet. I had an intense urge to pray, so I started

speaking in other tongues as the Spirit gave me utterance. I couldn’t stop praying. The Holy

Spirit is truly a wonder; within a few minutes, my friend came hurrying over, saying we had to

return to the hotel immediately because we had no business at the bar! Boy, oh boy, I cried for

joy. I was extremely happy because I knew it wasn’t by his own will that he left the bar so

quickly, but by the Will of God. That is the power of prevailing prayer.

Prevailing prayer is powerful and continues until it brings about real change. It’s a ki nd of prayer

led by the Holy Spirit, where you feel a strong urge to pray for something specific. This might

take a week, a month, or even a year, but you keep praying until the result God put in your heart

is achieved. Often, this kind of prayer isn't for yourself but for others — like your church,

community, family, or friends. It's not about personal desires, but about praying for the good of

others, just like we see in the book of Nehemiah.

In the first chapter of the book of Nehemiah, Nehemiah is told that the wall of Jerusalem is

broken and its gates destroyed by fire, which deeply distresses him. Despite serving under a non-

Israelite king, Nehemiah couldn't ignore the suffering of his people. He wept, confessed the sins

of the people and his family, and prayed day and night before the Lord. Nehemiah had a burden

on his heart, caring more about Israel than his position as King Artaxerxes' cupbearer.

Ultimately, Nehemiah successfully rebuilt the wall despite numerous challenges. Praise the Lord

Jesus!

“A s soon as I heard these words, I sat down and wept and mourned for days, and I continued

fasting and praying before the God of heaven. And I said, “O LORD God of heaven, the great

and awesome God who keeps covenant and steadfast love with those who love him and keep his

commandments, let your ear be attentive and your eyes open, to hear the prayer of your servant

that I now pray before you day and night for the people of Israel your servants, confessing the

sins of the people of Israel, which we have sinned against you. Even I and my father’s house

have sinned. We have acted very corruptly against you and have not kept the commandments, the

statutes, and the rules that you commanded your servant Moses. Remember the word that you

commanded your servant Moses, saying, ‘If you are unfaithful, I will scatter you among the

peoples, but if you return to me and keep my commandments and do them, though your outcasts

are in the uttermost parts of heaven, from there I will gather them and bring them to the place

that I have chosen, to make my name dwell there.’ They are your servants and your people,

whom you have redeemed by your great power and by your strong hand. O Lord, let your ear be

attentive to the prayer of your servant, and to the prayer of your servants who delight to fear

your name, and give success to your servant today, and grant him mercy in the sight of this

man.” Nehemiah 1:4 -11.

If there’s one thing to always be conscious of regarding prevailing prayer, it’s that this prayer

always works if you keep praying. To succeed, you need to focus on God's Word. Refuse any

negative thoughts that tell you to quit praying for your loved ones. If God told you to pray about

a thing and He urged you to keep praying until you see results, keep praying, and you will be

amazed by the results.

Prayer of Worship, Thanksgiving, and Praise

The prayer of worship, thanksgiving, and praise is one filled with gratitude, one that exalts God

and expresses his majesty, wondrous deeds, and might.

Psalms 69:30 says: ‘ I will raise the name of the Lord with songs, this shall please the Lord better

than an ox that has horns and hooves .” Hebrews 13:15 “Through him then let us continually

offer up a sacrifice of praise to God, that is, the fruit of lips that acknowledge his name.” What a

life!

Prayer of Intercession

God wants all men to be saved and come to the knowledge of the Truth. He has done everything

He needs to. “For God so loved the world that he gave his only son, that whoever believes in

Him should not perish but have everlasting life” So why don’t some people believe in Jesus

Christ? Why are there people still saying that there is no God? Why do we have people rejecting

the gospel of Jesus Christ?

2 Corinthians 4:3-4 (KJV) says: “But if our gospel be hid, it is hid to them that are lost: In whom

the god of this world hath blinded the minds of them which believe not, lest the light of the

glorious gospel of Ch rist, who is the image of God, should shine unto them.” This means that to

those who believe in Jesus Christ, the gospel is unveiled, and they can understand and live the

gospel, but to those who are lost, the gospel is hidden. Why? It is because the god of this world

(satan) has blinded their minds.

Do you see why it's crucial to pray for them? This kind of prayer is the intercessory prayer, one

where a believer prays for others for change. In our present life, some organisations and people

are working against the gospel, and God wants us to pray for them. If you don't intercede, what

affects the city, nation, and world can also affect you. Recall what Mordecai told Esther: she

would be affected if she didn’t intercede on behalf of the Jews. Another examp le in the Bible is

that of James and Peter. James was killed, but Peter, who was also imprisoned, was spared. The

difference was that believers prayed for Peter. This shows how important and mandatory prayer

is, as it can save many.

Remember, intercession is about making an impact. “First of all, then, I urge that supplications,

prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings be made for all people, for kings and all who are in

high positions, that we may lead a peaceful and quiet life, godly and dignified in every way. This

is good, and it is pleasing in the sight of God our Savior, who desires all people to be saved and

to come to the knowledge of the truth.” 1 Timothy 2:1 -4.

Knowing this, if you are a Christian in a position of authority or have close connections with

someone in power, like Esther, speak on behalf of the Church. You are the garrison in that place.

Use your influence and position to advance the gospel of Jesus Christ.

Prayer of Agreement

“Again I say to you, if two of you agree on e arth about anything they ask, it will be done for

them by my Father in heaven. For where two or three are gathered in my name, there am I

among them.” Matthew 18:19-20. There is power in agreement! When you agree on something

and pray together in one accord, it can be granted to you. Note that there must be more than one

person in agreement. There is specificity in all these kinds of prayers. The prayer of agreement

can be done by 2 or more people.

“So Peter was kept in prison, but earnest prayer for him was made to God by the church. Now,

when Herod was about to bring him out, on that very night, Peter was sleeping between two

soldiers, bound with two chains, and sentries before the door were guarding the prison. And

behold, an angel of the Lord stood next to him, and a light shone in the cell. He struck Peter on

the side and woke him, saying, “Get up quickly.” And the chains fell off his hands. And the angel

said to him, “Dress yourself and put on your sandals.” And he did so. And he said to him,

“Wrap your cloak around you and follow me.” And he went out and followed him. He did not

know that what was being done by the angel was real, but thought he was seeing a vision. When

they had passed the first and the second guard, they came to the Iron Gate leading into the city.

It opened for them of its own accord, and they went out and went along one street, and

immediately the angel left him. When Peter came to himself, he said, “Now I am sure that the

Lord has sent his angel and rescued me from the hand of Herod and from all that the Jewish

people were expecting.” Acts 12: 5 -11.

The church in Acts agreed and prayed unceasingly for Peter while he was imprisoned. The

church prayed until Peter came out. You too can agree on something and it can turn around for

your good.

Prayer of Faith

Faith Faith Faith! What is faith? “Faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of

things not seen” Hebrews 11:1 (KJV). What does it mean? Faith calls what is not as though it

were. See how the ESV puts it. “F aith is an assurance of the things hoped for, the conviction of

things not seen.” Hallelujah! Knowing what faith is, what then is the prayer of faith?

Mark 11:22-23 says: “And Jesus answered them “Have faith in God. Truly, I say to you,

whoever says to this mountain, ‘Be taken up and thrown into the sea’ and does not doubt in his

heart, but believes that what he says will come to pass, it will be done for him. Therefore, I tell

you, whatever you ask in prayer, believe that you have received it, and it wi ll be yours.”

This prayer of faith involves praying to God and speaking to circumstances so that they align

with your desires, without any doubt in your heart. One key aspect of this type of prayer is that it

does not fail, so you should not doubt it! Stand firm on the words you speak and do not waver by

saying you are unsure if it will happen.

“If any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask God, who gives generously to all without reproach, and

it will be given him. But let him ask in faith, with no doubting, for the one who doubts is like a

wave of the sea that is driven and tossed by the wind.” James 1:5-6. Again, faith does not doubt,

at all! You should maintain the right confession.

Note: For this type of prayer, you consider something done after you pray so it differs from the

prevailing prayer that can be made over time until something happens. With the prayer of faith, it

is done once you pray.

With all these, the Holy Spirit can guide you on what type of prayer you require to effect

changes in different areas or situations in life. Yield to Him and He will guide you, always.

fields.title: Chapter 4. Praying In The Spirit
fields.body_html:
We are not of this world, so we do not operate by its standards. Therefore, let us speak the

language of our citizenship — the language of the Spirit.

Firstly, man is primarily a spirit with a soul, living in a physical body. When one confesses with

his/her mouth that Jesus is Lord and believes in his/her heart that God raised him from the dead,

that person will be saved (Romans 10:8-9). This man is then separated from the rest. 2

Corinthians 5:17 says: “Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has

passed away; behold, the new has come.” He becomes a new creation, a superman, a man with

the life of God, a man who can never be disadvantaged in life. With this, he is now in God’s

kingdom, and that is where he belongs. It then becomes very vital for him/her to know the

language where he/she comes from because it can help him/her stay updated on what is

happening in the Kingdom.

How can one know or learn that language? You may ask.

This new creation, Superman, is given a language of the recreated spirit. That is speaking in

other tongues. Some Bible versions render it differently and say it is the language of the

angels. This language is not taught by men but given by God, so mere men cannot understand it

because it is a divine language of God. Isn’t it beautiful speaking the language God knows so

well and not even Satan can understand a word? This is praying in the Spirit. So cool!

Again, you might ask, how can I start speaking this language, speaking in other tongues? One of

the answers to this is by praying to God for the infilling of the Holy Spirit, identified with

speaking in tongues, and in so doing, believe that He has answered and start speaking in other

tongues. As mentioned earlier, do not doubt. The other answer to this is by the laying on of

hands as seen in Acts 19:6 “And when Paul had laid his hands on them, the Holy Spirit came on

them, and they began speaking in tongues and prophesying.”

Other question might still come: “ Must every believer speak in tongues, or it is for the chosen

ones? What happens if we do not pray in tongues? Don’t we have the Holy Spirit if we don’t

pray in tongues? Of what benefit is prayi ng in tongues?” Let’s get right into the details, shall we?

Must all believers speak in tongues?

This question is just like asking if one must eat food. One can eat, or not, but not eating food for

an extended period can negatively affect the body.

As Jesus was leaving for Heaven, He said: “ And these signs will accompany those who believe:

in my name they will cast out demons; they will speak in new tongues; they will pick up serpents

with their hands; and if they drink any deadly poison, it will not hurt them; they will lay their

hands on the sick, and they will recover.” Mark 16:17. This means that speaking in tongues is

not limited to specific people; it is for all who believe in the Lord Jesus Christ. No one should

condemn it or say that it is only for certain individuals. Since you are a spirit and God is a spirit

too, speaking the spirit language should be a priority.

Speaking in tongues is a sign that one has been filled with the Spirit

The disciples were waiting for the Holy Spirit on the day of Pentecost. They were in one accord.

Cloven tongues as of fire sat upon each of them. Look at Acts 2:4. “And they were all filled with

the Holy Spirit and began to speak in other tongues as the Spirit gave them utterance.”

In the Old Testament, the Holy Spirit came upon kings, priests, and judges so that they could

carry out the work and teach God’s people. So He first sat upon them as tongues of fire. After,

He filled them. However, in the New Testament, the Holy Spirit dwells in us and makes us His

temple. He comes upon you to fill you. The evidence that you are filled with the Holy Spirit is

the evidence of the sign of speaking in tongues. Being with the Holy Spirit and being filled with

the Holy Spirit are not the same things. Those that are filled with the Holy Spirit speak in other

tongues. So, speaking in tongues is not meant for the pastors, Bishops, and evangelists alone, it is

for everyone.

Why then should you speak in tongues?

1. It builds you up

“The one who speaks in a tongue builds up hims elf, but the one who prophesies builds up the

church.” 1 Corinthians 14:4. To edify means to build, to construct, and to establish. Jude 1:20

(AMP) says: “But you, beloved, build yourselves up on [the foundation of] your most holy faith

[continually progress, rise like an edifice higher and higher], pray in the Holy Spirit. ” So he

tells us to build ourselves in the most holy faith, praying in the Holy Spirit. That is how

important praying in tongues is. As you speak in tongues, you are edified, and you become

bigger than the circumstances you are facing. Beautiful, isn’t it?

Are you facing a challenge or a condition that seems to have no solution? Is it about your health,

your family, your community, or the nation? You have the power to effect changes in everything

that concerns you. Speak in tongues, keep speaking in tongues, and changes will be effected.

Hallelujah!

2. Speaking in tongues charges you up

In the same book of 1 Corinthians, the one who speaks in tongues edifies themselves. This word

also means charging up. When you speak in other tongues, you are generating power and energy.

Did you charge up in the morning? As you go to class, charge up. Before going to church, charge

up. When you start studying, you will operate well because you have charged up. Praise the

Lord!

4. Speaking in other tongues refreshes you

As a Christian, whenever you feel the need to cool down, perhaps when your mind is

overwhelmed with anything, any issue, speaking in tongues refreshes you. God can speak to you,

guide you, and bring you peace during those moments. “For by people of strange lips and with a

foreign tongue the LORD will speak to this people” Isaiah 28 11.

5. Speaking in tongues allows us to fellowship with the Holy Spirit

When we speak in tongues, we are speaking the language of the Holy Spirit. It's a way to relate

with Him and receive His wisdom, courage, and boldness. This is why everyone should speak in

tongues. When you speak in tongues regularly, you can never be defeated. You will know what

to do and you will be guided by the God of Heaven and Earth, ensuring you stay on the right

path. Hallelujah!

fields.title: Chapter 5. Cultivating The Spirit Of Prayer
fields.body_html:
Whatever you intentionally cultivate grows!

Who is the Spirit of Prayer?

“ Likewise the Spirit helps us in our weakness. For we do not know what to pray for as we ought,

but the Spirit himself intercedes for us with groanings too deep for words.” Romans 8:26

The spirit of prayer is the Holy Spirit, and He is the one who intercedes on our behalf. Through

us, He maintains an atmosphere of prayer in our lives. Everyone should have Him! Whether we

notice it or not, He operates powerfully in us, and without Him, nothing can be done perfectly.

We receive and invite Him by desire. We receive Him the same way we received the Lord Jesus

Christ in our lives; by faith. You cannot perform an act to get the Holy Spirit, not even the good

deeds can make Him come or even fill you. It is by desire and faith.

The Holy Spirit is truly wonderful. If you are thirsty, He will satisfy you. You will find yourself

praying continually. He will lead you into His visions, plans, and purposes. He will express

Himself through you in prayer, and you will know that He is at work! Everyone needs to have

the Spirit of prayer because He is the perfect guide in all things.

One might say: “I have prayed and invited the spirit of prayer to influence my life but I am not

seeing any change.” I will respond to this with an example of a m other who wants her children to

accept the Lord Jesus and be born again. She is praying for her children to see Jesus so that they

can go to church as a whole family. Have you noticed where the problem is coming from? The

problem is in the reason/motive for praying. It is a marvelous thing to pray for souls to come to

Christ, but if the motive is for personal pleasure, it ceases to be a powerful prayer because it is

selfish. “You ask and do not receive, because you ask wrongly, to spend it on your passions.”

James 4:3. Our focus should be on eternity. Perhaps this is why someone hasn't seen any change

even after praying for the Spirit of prayer. As you pray for your friend, teacher, sister or any

other person, always remember to have the right reason for what you are praying for.

How then can we cultivate the Spirit of Prayer? How can we fully benefit from the Holy

Spirit? How can we nurture the Spirit of Prayer?

1. By praying at all times in the Spirit, having faith, and letting it be proven that you operate

by faith and not by sight. This means that you can call things that are not as though they

are. You can command the situation to change because the power is in you. You are

stronger than 10,000 armies! Stronger than malaria, ulcers, cancer, hepatitis, fibroids,

HIV, sickle cells, tumours, and any other sickness or disease. Praise the Lord! Pray in the

Spirit, release mysteries because you have the power to effect changes in your life.

2. We cultivate the Spirit of prayer through meditating on God’s Word. T hrough it, the Holy

Spirit can be stirred and can cause us to pray fervently. The more you read the Word, the

more you know it, and if you can put to work what you have known, and meditate on it

always, you can never be discouraged or disadvantaged. You always grow because you

are feeding and acting on the word of God, and that stirs up the Spirit of Prayer. Diseases

can’t thrive in such atmospheres, sicknesses can’t, and neither can sorrow, condemnation,

or worry!

fields.title: Chapter 6. Prevailing In Prayer
fields.body_html:
We first prevail with God before we prevail with men.

In the context of prayer, prevailing prayer means one that continues with persistence until it

achieves the desired outcome. Before we move any further, I would like us to remember that we

win in the spirit first before the victory is seen in the physical. See how Jacob wanted to return to

his homeland. All of what God had blessed him with was taken and he was ready to go home.

However, he remembered that he had cheated his brother Esau. Esau was now established,

giving Jacob ample reason to be afraid. As he prepared for the journey, his heart was unsettled,

and he found himself alone. Jacob understood that unless he prevailed with God, he wouldn't

prevail with Esau.

That night, an angel appeared to Jacob, and he wrestled with the angel until morning. Jacob

didn’t give up; he held on until the angel blessed him. This showed that Jacob had won with

God, preparing him to succeed with Esau.

“Then he said, “Your name shall no longer be called Jacob, but Israel, for you have striven with

God and with men, and have prevailed.” Genesis 32:28.

Unlike our usual prayers, prevailing prayer arises from a deep burden on one's heart. It's the kind

of prayer the Holy Spirit compels you to continue until you see results. As discussed earlier,

prevailing prayer is essential; it doesn't stop until it achieves its purpose. It goes beyond simply

thanking the Lord for His goodness; it involves intense prayer.

“Likewise , the Spirit helps us in our weakness. For we do not know what to pray for as we ought,

but the Spirit himself intercedes for us with groanings too deep for words.” Romans 8:26.

Without the Holy Spirit, one cannot prevail in prayer because nothing, or so little can be changed

when we pray carnally. Why? We cannot know what exactly is right to say, and how to say it to

effect changes but the Spirit is our guide.

Do you feel like you have done everything but still not seeing results? Keep going! Don't stop

until you succeed. Even if it doesn't seem to work, it actually is. The enemy knows you can win

if you keep pressing on. He only bothers with people who give up because he knows they've

already lost. So, don’t give up! If you feel a burden to pray, make sure you do. God won’t give

you more than you can handle. Whatever He gives you, He also gives you the strength to

overcome! Hallelujah!

But before praying, repenting of anything wrong in your life is important. After that, receive

forgiveness and move on. Speak in other tongues as it helps you accomplish things that are

needed for that matter. Then, speak the word of God with boldness. When the Holy Spirit fills

your heart, you speak the word of God with boldness “And when they had prayed, the place in

which they were gathered together was shaken, and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and

continued to speak the word of God with boldness.” Acts 4:31.

What does prevailing prayer do?

It maintains inspiration. If you are not praying, you will lose the favour/glow that follows it. “Do

not be slothful in zeal, be fervent in spirit, and serve the Lord.” Romans 12:11. Never lag in zeal!

How do you do it? By meditating on the word of God. Do that again and again, and let it become

a part of you.

Prevailing prayer also cleanses and makes us more glorious than we came in before prayer. The

more you pray, the more you glow.

fields.title: Chapter 7. Prayer And Fasting
fields.body_html:
The fast is on because you’re praying, not because you’re not eating.

When we talk about prayer and fasting, some people think it just means not eating, like eating

would be a mistake! It sounds funny, but it’s a common misunderstanding. Many people focus

only on the idea of fasting as a time to avoid food, missing the true purpose.

Fasting isn't just about skipping meals —it’s about replacing food with time spent in prayer and

focusing on God's Word. If you’re just not eating and sleeping all day to pass the time, that’s not

fasting —that’s just starving yourself.

As Christians, we need to understand that fasting is about prayer. We fast because we’re praying,

not just because we aren’t eating. It's a call to spend time in prayer, and as we do that, we make a

conscious decision to refrain from eating.

Acts 13:2 says, “As they ministered to the Lord, and fasted, the Holy Spirit said...” Notice the

order: they ministered to the Lord and fasted. How do you minister to the Lord? Through praise,

thanksgiving, worship, and prayer. The focus was on ministering to the Lord, and because of

this, they fasted.

The Bible additionally shows us that after the Lord spoke to them after they had prayed. This is

one of the benefits of prayer and fasting; you can receive guidance from the Holy Spirit, which

can save you from countless mistakes.

Besides receiving guidance, prayer, and fasting, attune your spirit to the things of God more

deeply.

Through prayer and fasting, you are ministering to the Lord. So, spend time in prayer and

fasting.

Some people say they are fasting but spend the day sleeping or engaging in irrelevant activities

to distract themselves from hunger. I used to be like that, but praise the Lord, the Holy Spirit

guided me on how to pray and fast effectively. Prayer and fasting should focus on prayer and

activities that encourage prayer, such as studying the Bible, worshipping the Lord, praising, and

meditating on the Word. Hallelujah!

Turn off your phone if it will distract you. While many people enjoy receiving updates, it is more

important to receive updates from the Spirit realm during this time. Turn off your TV and set

aside any newspapers or magazines. Focus on activities that encourage you to pray. As

mentioned earlier, it is much better to begin by speaking in tongues, which is praying in the

Spirit. This way, you will be guided on what to say in your understanding; the Holy Spirit will

lead you in what to pray.

One might ask, "When should I fast? Should I fast every day, month, or once a year?"

Firstly, it is an excellent time to fast when your local church, school fellowship or congregation

declares a prayer and fasting program. Never separate yourself from such a call, thinking you

don't feel the need to pray and fast yet, or that you will do it at your own perfect time. No, it

shouldn't be that way. There are things we do together as a community, such as corporate

worship, and many other activities intended for spiritual growth and edification; prayer and

fasting are among them.

If your church calls for prayer and fasting, do not refuse to participate and instead set your times

for starting or ending the fast. This approach is wrong. Exercise discipline and fast as instructed.

This is how you bring about changes in the spiritual realm. Remember, through this practice,

your ability to hear and receive from God is sharpened, and you become more attuned to spiritual

matters. The more you pray and fast, the less likely you are to be caught off guard because you

can perceive things that are about to happen and influence what you want to see in your life and

the lives of those around you. Hallelujah!

Secondly, fast when the Holy Spirit leads you to do so, or when you choose to fast and pray. This

is another perfect opportunity, especially if it's the Spirit guiding you; you will recognise His

leading. Take it seriously and proceed with the fast.

Some people schedule prayer and fasting days or moments as a spiritual discipline, and that's

beautiful. Therefore, whenever and however you are guided to fast, take it seriously. Make

prayer and fasting a part of your spiritual routine.

fields.title: Chapter 8. The First Fruit Of Time
fields.body_html:
How you start your day tells a lot about how the rest of the day will be!

Would you like your day to feel like Heaven on Earth? Think about your daily routine — how do

you start your mornings? What are your priorities, and what’s the first thing you do? If prayer

isn’t at the top of your list, it might be time to switch things up.

Here’s something powerful: everything that happens in the physical world has already been set in

motion in the spiritual world. As Christians, we can create because we’re made in God’s image.

That’s why it’s so important to take control and intentionally shape your day. Many people wake

up and set their intentions, and if you’re not careful, you might end up living according to

someone else’s plans or prayers.

What you do in the first hour of your day matters. Make it a habit to wake up early and bless

your day with prayer. When you do this, you’ll notice your day becomes clearer, and everythi ng

feels smoother. Plus, you open yourself up to receiving guidance from God, who wants you to

succeed and prosper. Let Him direct your path, and you’ll be amazed at how your life is

transformed!

fields.title: Chapter 9. His Return!
fields.body_html:
Prepare yourself to meet the Lord Jesus Christ!

“And there will be signs in sun and moon and stars, and on the earth distress of nations in

perplexity because of the roaring of the sea and the waves, people fainting with fear and with

foreboding of what is coming on the world. For the powers of the heavens will be shaken. And

then they will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with power and great glory. Now when these

things begin to take place, straighten up and raise your heads, because your redemption is

drawing near.” Luke 21:25 -28

Many signs are showing us where we are today and how close we are to the time when nations

will be judged. No matter where you are right now, always remember that Jesus Christ is coming

soon.

Some believe and are eagerly waiting for His return, while others are sceptical and not expecting

Him. But He is coming, so prepare yourself for Him. He is coming for “...all who have loved his

appearing.” (2 Timothy 4:8), those who are ready for Him. The Bible says blessed are those who

are waiting for His return (Luke 12:37).

While at school, home, or anywhere else, live your life as though His return could happen at any

moment because it can indeed happen at any moment. 1 Corinthians 15:52 tells us, “ In a

moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet. For the trumpet will sound, and the dead

will be raised imperishable, and we shall be changed. ”

It has been almost two thousand years since Jesus Christ ascended from this world. The

prophecies ab out His coming are being fulfilled before our eyes. He said: “Surely I come

quickly…” (Revelation 22:20).

Statistics show that today's world is crueler, violent, and filled with terrorism than ever before.

Life's challenges are tougher now than they’ve ever been. So, don’t get caught off guard. Stay in

Christ, live in righteousness, and keep living for Him. Illuminate your world with the Gospel by

preaching the gospel and winning souls to the Lord Jesus Christ. Your reward is great.

As the world is changing, refuse to succumb to its pressure because greater is He that is in you

than he that is in this world. Christ has given you power over all things. Be unshakeable. Live

above the systems of the world.

Christ is coming back! It is not a story or a myth, it is about to happen!

Dedicate your time, resources, and energy to spreading the Gospel until it reaches the ends of the

earth. Prepare yourself and help others prepare for the rapture of the church, too.

fields.title: Chapter 10. A Call To The Word
fields.body_html:
If you want to know the will of God, know His word!

In many meetings, I encourage Christians to make it a priority to know what God wants us to do.

The truth is, you can't know God's plan for your life if you don't read the Bible. It's like a manual

for living, meant to shape who we are.

If you want to understand your purpose and what God has planned for you, spend time in prayer

and read His Word. A Christian who doesn’t read the Bible is missing out on the de eper things of

God. Loving God means wanting to know what pleases Him — and we learn that through His

Word.

If life feels tough or the world seems overwhelming, the Bible is where you’ll find strength,

hope, and guidance. God's Word gives life! It restores, saves, and even heals. When the Bible

says you are the head and not the tail, believe it, and live it!

There’s so much peace and power that come from living God’s Word. Sorrow, fear, and worldly

troubles won't shake you because you know that's not your portion. The Bible gives you the

direction you need every day. Read it, believe it, and boldly live out what it says about you.

You are not like everyone else. You’re chosen, special, and called to show God’s goodness in the

world. You are the light of the world, set apart to radiate His glory. With God living in you,

you’re unstoppable and unshakable. Hallelujah!

fields.title: Chapter 11. Testimonials
fields.body_html:
He has done great things, and we bless His name!

It's exciting to share stories of prayers that were answered! In this chapter, you’ll see examples of

people who prayed and experienced amazing results. Some stories come from the Bible, and

others are real- life testimonies from today’s church. God never stops answering prayers,

especially when we pray in Jesus' Name. Check out these inspiring examples of people who

prayed and saw victory!

Received Strength

Jesus, the author and finisher of our faith, prayed. Though purely divine, he was also purely

human. Through prayer, Jesus was strengthened. “And there appeared to h im an angel from

heaven, strengthening him.” Luke 22:43.

Received a Son

Hannah is also one of the women who prayed and prevailed. She was one of the two wives of

Elkanah, a Levite who lived at Ramah. Despite the fact that she was married, she had no

children, and that upset her. She cried unto the Lord, and she prevailed. She gave birth to a son

whom she called Samuel. Samuel was given unto the Lord, and he did mighty exploits as we see

in 1 st and 2 nd Samuel.

Shamed All Prophets of Baal

Another was Elijah, who prayed for fire to come down from Heaven (1 Kings 18). When the

people of Israel turned away from God and worshipped false gods, especially the false god of

Baal, Elijah prayed for fire on Mount Carmel. This was to prove the only true God. With the

prophets of Baal praying to their God for a response, Elijah prayed after their god did not

answer. The Lord God of Hosts answered by sending fire from Heaven. He prevailed!

Others from the Bible include David, Jonah, Esther, and Job.

Rescued from a terrible accident

Among those outside the Bible is myself. I got into a terrible accident during my O-Level

holidays. I was hit by a motorcycle and almost taken over by a car on the same road, but thanks

be to God, I was saved. No one knew that I would make it; some thought that I was not mentally

okay when I stood up, but God is great. When I called upon the Lord, He saved me! Here I am

10 years later, so beautiful and healthy! Glory to God!

Healed from HIV/AIDS

At my local church, there is a lady who was diagnosed with HIV/AIDS. She was sick all the

time, and many, including some believers, lost hope, but she didn’t! She kept on praying and

believing God for greater things even though she looked like she was about to die. Finally, she

was healed by the power of God. It has been more than 15 years since she was healed, and she is

still negative to this day! Praise the Lord!

Got her results

Biyinzika sat for her university exams but was never given marks. As many told her to repeat

those papers, she refused and prayed. God answered her prayers, and the marks that were

allocated on her academic papers were so excellent that they were a marvel.

Got a job

Exceeding her expectations, Precious got a well-paying job at one of the biggest companies in

the country after praying. She had finished school but hadn’t found a placement. Through

prevailing prayer, she was able to see results, that were beyond her comprehension. Glory to

God!

Isn’t the Lord amazing? Absolutely! And guess what —those aren’t the only testimonies! No

matter what you’re facing, there’s nothing God can’t handle. Nothing is too big for Him!

Surrender it all to God, pray, and watch the testimonies roll in! Hallelujah!

fields.title: Chapter 12. Prayer Of Salvation
fields.body_html:
Christianity is not a religion; it is living the God-kind of life.

God loved the world so much that He gave His Son, Jesus Christ, to die for everyone. Why? So

that you and I would not perish but have everlasting life! Oh wow! I have everlasting life, and so

do you if you are born again. If you are not yet born again, this moment is your opportunity. You

will have eternal life if you believe in Jesus Christ with your heart and declare Him Lord over

your life!

“But you said Jesus Christ died for everyone, why then say it is only those who are born again

that have eternal life?” You may ask. I will start by giving an example of a friend saying that

they have signed a cheque for you. As it is known, money is yours. However, if you don’t mo ve

to the bank to pick up your money and instead throw your cheque away, you won’t have that

money, even when they signed it for you. This is the same thing with eternal life. Our Lord,

Jesus Christ, died for the entire world. However, eternal life is imparted to those who believe in

our Lord Jesus as the Son of the living God, believing that He came, died, and was raised again

and is alive today. When you know, accept, and confess that Jesus Christ is the Lord of your life,

eternal life is immediately imparted in your spirit. That is how eternal life is received. Praise the

Lord!

Would you now want to receive this eternal life, the God-Kind of life? I hereby invite you to

make Jesus Christ the Lord of your life, if you haven’t. Kindly believe and pray thus :

“O Lord God, I believe with all my heart in Jesus Christ, the Son of the living God. I

believe He died for me and God raised Him from the dead. I believe He is alive today. I

confess with my mouth that Jesus Christ is the Lord of my life from this day. Through Him

and in His Name, I have eternal life; I am born again. Thank you, Lord, for saving my

soul! I am now a child of God. Hallelujah!”

Congratulations! You are now a child of God, born of the Word of God. You are a new creature

that is so perfect and righteous because Christ the Lord now lives in you, and has made you His

righteousness. You don’t need to feel it but believe that you are n ow a different person, so

victorious and can now make the wisest decisions ever. Nothing is impossible for you now! Start

reading the Bible and allow God to speak and guide you in His perfect will.

God bless you!

THE END

fields.title: Chapter 1. The Glory Of The Creature
fields.body_html:
With humility, God dwells in the creature while pride, failure and defects await the creature.

For God to dwell in the creature, the creature has to present itself to the creator as an empty

vessel which the creator will fill and manifest his power and goodness.

"Worthy are you, our Lord and God, to receive glory and honour and power, for you created all

things, and by your will they existed and were created." Rev. 4:11.

hen God created the universe, it was with the one object of making the creature partaker

of His perfection and blessedness, and so showing forth in it the glory of His love, wisdom,

and power. God wished to reveal Himself in and through created beings by communicating to

them as much of His own goodness and glory as they were capable of receiving. But this

communication was not giving to the creature something which it could possess in itself, a certain

life or goodness, of which it had the charge and disposal. By no means. But as God is the ever

living, ever-present, ever-acting One, who upholds all things by the word of His power, and in

whom all things exist, the relation of the creature to God could only be one of unceasing, absolute,

and universal dependence. As truly as God by His power once created, so truly by that same power

must He maintain every moment.

The creature not only has to look back to the origin and first beginning of existence, and

acknowledge that it there owes everything to God its chief care, its highest virtue, its only

happiness, now and through all eternity, but also present itself as an empty vessel, in which God

can dwell and manifest His power and goodness.

The life God bestows is imparted not once for all, but each moment continuously, by the unceasing

operation of His mighty power. Humility, the place of entire dependence on God, is, from the very

nature of things, the first duty and the highest virtue of the creature, and the root of every virtue.

And so pride, or the loss of this humility, is the root of every sin and evil. It was when the now

W

fallen angels began to look upon themselves with self-complacency that they were led to

disobedience, and were cast down from the light of heaven into outer darkness. Even so, it was

when the serpent breathed the poison of his pride, the desire to be as God, into the hearts of our

first parents, that they too fell from their high estate into all the wretchedness in which man is now

sunk. In heaven and earth, pride and self-exaltation are the gates and the birth, and the curse of

hell.

Nothing can be our redemption but the restoration of the lost humility, the original and only true

relation of the creature to its God. And so Jesus came to bring humility back to earth, to make us

partakers of it, and by it to save us. In heaven, He humbled Himself to become man. The humility

we see in Him possessed Him in Heaven, it brought Him and He brought it from there. Here on

earth "He humbled himself by becoming obedient to the point of death" (Philippians 2:8); His

humility gave His death value, and so became our redemption. And now the salvation He imparts

is nothing less and nothing else than a communication of His own life and death, His own

disposition and spirit, His own humility, as the ground and root of His relation to God and His

redeeming work.

Jesus Christ took the place and fulfilled the destiny of man, as a creature, by His life of perfect

humility. His humility is our salvation and His salvation is our humility. The life of the saved ones

and that of the saints must bear this stamp of deliverance from sin, and full restoration to their

original state; their whole relation to God and man marked by an all-pervading humility. Without

this, there can be no true abiding in God's presence, or experience of His favour and the power of

His Spirit, but rather, the absence of abiding faith, love, joy, and strength.

Humility is the only soil in which the graces root. Therefore, the lack of humility is a sufficient

explanation for every defect and failure. Humility is not so much a grace or virtue along with

others; it is the root of all, because it alone is the right attitude before God, and allows Him to do

all as God. God has so constituted us as reasonable beings that the truer the insight into the real

nature or the absolute need of a command, the readier and fuller will be our obedience to it. The

call to humility has been too little regarded in the Church because its true nature and importance

have been too little apprehended.

It is not something which we bring to God, or He bestows; it is simply the sense of entire

nothingness which comes when we see how truly God is all, and in which we make way for God

to be all. When the creature realizes that this is the true nobility and consents to be with his will,

his mind and affections form the vessel in which the life and Glory of God are to work and manifest

themselves. He sees humility as simply acknowledging the truth of his position as creature and

yielding to God.

In the life of earnest Christians, of those who pursue and profess holiness, humility ought to be the

chief mark of their uprightness. It is often said that it is not so. May not one reason be that in the

teaching and example of the Church, it has never had that place of supreme importance that belongs

to it. And that this, again, is owing to the neglect of this truth, that strong as sin is as a motive to

humility, there is one of still wider and mightier influence, that which makes the angels, that which

made Jesus, that which makes the holiest of saints in heaven, so humble.

The first and chief mark of the relation of the creature and the secret of his blessedness is the

humility and nothingness which leaves God free to be all. I am sure there are many Christians who

will confess that their experience has been very much like my own in this, that we had long known

the Lord without realizing that meekness and lowliness of heart are to be the distinguishing feature

of the disciple as they were of the Master. Further, that this humility is not a thing that will come

of itself, but that it must be made the object of special desire, prayer, faith, and practice.

As we study the word, we shall see the very distinct and oft-repeated instructions Jesus gave His

disciples on this point, and how slow they were in understanding Him. Let us, at the very

commencement of our meditations, admit that there is nothing as natural to man, nothing as

insidious and hidden from our sight, nothing as difficult and dangerous as pride.

Let us feel that nothing but determination and perseverance, while waiting on God and Christ, will

discover how lacking we are in the grace of humility, and how impotent to obtain what we seek.

Let us study the character of Christ until our souls are filled with the love and admiration of His

lowliness. And let us believe that, when we are broken down under a sense of our pride, and our

impotence to cast it out, Jesus Christ Himself will come in to impart this grace too, as a part of His

wondrous life within us.

NOTE A

All this is to make it known the region of eternity that pride can degrade the highest angels into

devils, and humility raise fallen flesh and blood to the thrones of angels. Thus, this is the great end

of God raising a new creation out of a fallen kingdom of angels. For this end, it stands in its state

of war between the fire and pride of fallen angels, and the humility of the Lamb of God, that the

last trumpet may sound the great truth through the depths of eternity, that evil can have no

beginning but from pride, and no end but from humility.

The truth is this, pride may die in you or nothing of heaven can live in you. Under the banner of

the truth, give yourself up to the meek and humble spirit of the Holy Jesus. Humility must sow

seed, or there can be no reaping in Heaven. Look not at pride only as an unbecoming temper, nor

at humility only as a decent virtue: for one is death, and the other is life, one is all hell and the

other is all heaven. So much as you have pride within you, you have of the fallen angels alive in

you, so much as you have true humility, and so much you have the Lamb of God within you.

Could you see what every stirring of pride does to your soul, you would beg of everything you

meet to tear the viper from you, though with the loss of a hand or an eye. Could you see what a

sweet, divine, transforming power there is in humility, how it expels the poison of your nature,

and makes room for the Spirit of God to live in you, you would rather wish to be the footstool of

all the world than want the smallest degree of it." --Spirit of Prayer, Pt.II, p.73, Edition of Moreton,

Canterbury, 1893.

fields.title: Chapter 2. The Secret Of Redemption
fields.body_html:
As it is that every tree is dependent on its roots, every Christian should be dependent on God.

See how believers should root themselves in Jesus, the root of redemption that causes us to be

purposeful while on earth.

ave this mind among yourselves, which is yours in Christ Jesus, who, though he was in the

form of God, did not count equality with God a thing to be grasped, but emptied himself, by

taking the form of a servant, being born in the likeness of men. And being found in human form,

he humbled himself by becoming obedient to the point of death, even death on a cross. Therefore

God has highly exalted him and bestowed on him the name that is above every name, “Philippians

2:5-9.

No tree can grow except on the root from which it sprang. Throughout all its existence, it can

only live with the life that was in the seed that gave it being. The full apprehension of this truth

in its application to the first and the Second Adam helps us to understand both the need and the

nature of the redemption in Jesus. When the Old Serpent, he who had been cast out from heaven

for his pride, whose whole nature as the devil was pride, spoke his words of temptation into the

ear of Eve, these words carried with them the very poison of hell.

When she listened and yielded her desire and her will to the prospect of being as God, knowing

good and evil, the poison entered into her soul, blood, and life destroying forever that blessed

humility and dependence upon God which would have been our everlasting happiness. Because of

this, her life and the life of the race that sprang from her became corrupted to its very root with

Satan’s own pride, the most terrible of all sins and all curses.

All the wretchedness of which this world has been the scene, all its wars and bloodshed among the

nations, its selfishness and suffering, its ambitions and jealousies, its broken hearts and embittered

lives, with all its daily unhappiness, have their origin in what this cursed, hellish pride, either our

own or that of others, has brought us. It is pride that makes redemption needful. It is from our pride

H

that we need to be redeemed. Our insight into the need for redemption will largely depend upon

our knowledge of the terrible nature of the power that has entered our being. The power that Satan

brought from hell and cast into man's life is working daily, hourly, with mighty power throughout

the world. Men suffer from it, they fear, fight, and flee it, yet they know not when it comes, and

when it has its terrible supremacy.

No wonder they do not know where or how it is to be overcome. Pride has its root and strength in

a terrible spiritual power, outside of us as well as within us; as needful as it is that we confess and

deplore it as our very own, it is to know it in its satanic origin. If this leads us to utter despair of

ever conquering or casting it out, it will lead us all the sooner to that supernatural power in which

alone our deliverance is to be found - the redemption of the Lamb of God. The hopeless struggle

against the workings of self and pride within us may indeed become still more hopeless as we

think of the power of darkness behind it all; the utter despair will fit us the better for realizing and

accepting a power and a life outside of ourselves too, even the humility of heaven as brought down

and brought nigh by the Lamb of God, to cast out Satan and his pride.

No tree can grow except on the root from which it sprang. Even as we need to look to the first

Adam and his fall to know the power of the sin within us, we need to know well the Second Adam

and His power to give within us a life of humility as real and abiding and overmastering as has

been that of pride. We have our life from and in Christ, as truly, yes, more truly, than from and in

Adam. We are to walk "rooted in Him," holding fast the Head from whom the whole body

increases with the increase of God.

The life of God, which in the incarnation entered human nature, is the root in which we are to

stand and grow; it is the same almighty power that worked there, and hence onward to the

resurrection, which works daily in us. Our one need is to study, know, and trust the life that has

been revealed in Christ as the life that is now ours, and waits for our consent to gain possession

and mastery of our whole being.

In this view, it is of inconceivable importance that we should have right thoughts of what Christ

is, of what really constitutes Him the Christ, and especially of what may be counted His chief

characteristic, the root and essence of all His character as our Redeemer. There can be but one

answer: it is His humility. What is the incarnation but His heavenly humility, His emptying

Himself and becoming man? What is His life on earth but humility; His taking the form of a

servant? And what is His atonement but humility? "He humbled himself by becoming obedient"

(Philippians 2:8). And what is His ascension and His glory, but humility exalted to the throne and

crowned with glory? "Therefore God has highly exalted him" (Philippians 2:9). In heaven, where

He was with the Father, in His birth, in His life, in His death, in His sitting on the throne, it is all

nothing but humility.

Christ is the humility of God embodied in human nature, the Eternal Love humbling itself, clothing

itself in the garb of meekness and gentleness to win, serve, and save us. As the love and

condescension of God make Him the benefactor, helper, and servant of all, so Jesus of necessity

was the incarnate Humility. So, He is still in the midst of the throne, the meek and lowly Lamb of

God. If this be the root of the tree, its nature must be seen in every branch, leaf, and fruit.

If humility be the first, the all-including grace of the life of Jesus, if humility be the secret of His

atonement, then the health and strength of our spiritual life will entirely depend upon our putting

this grace first too, and making humility the chief thing we admire in Him, the chief thing we ask

of Him, the one thing for which we sacrifice all else. Is it any wonder that the Christian life is so

often feeble and fruitless when the very root of the Christ life is neglected, is unknown? Is it any

wonder that the joy of salvation is so little felt when that which Christ found and brings is so little

sought? Until a humility which will rest in the end and death of self, which gives up all the honor

of men as Jesus did to seek the honor that comes from God alone, which absolutely makes and

counts itself nothing, that God may be all, that the Lord alone may be exalted, until such a humility

be what we seek in Christ above our chief joy, and welcome at any price, there is very little hope

of a religion that will conquer the world.

I cannot too earnestly plead with my reader, if possibly his attention has never yet been specially

directed to the want there is of humility within him or around him, to pause and ask whether he

sees much of the spirit of the meek and lowly Lamb of God in those who are called by His name.

Let him consider how all want of love, all indifference to the needs, the feelings, and the weakness

of others, all sharp and hasty judgments and utterances, so often excused under the plea of being

outright and honest.

All manifestations of temper and touchiness and irritation, all feelings of bitterness and

estrangement have their root in pride that ever seeks itself. His eyes will be opened to see how a

dark, devilish pride creeps in almost everywhere, the assemblies of the saints not excepted. Let

him begin to ask what would be the effect if, in himself and around him, towards fellow saints and

the world, believers were really permanently guided by the humility of Jesus. Let him say if the

cry of our whole heart, night and day, ought not to be, O, for the humility of Jesus in myself and

all around me!

Let him honestly fix his heart on his own lack of the humility which has been revealed in the

likeness of Christ's life, and in the whole character of His redemption, and he will begin to feel as

if he had never yet really known what Christ and His salvation are. Believer! Study the humility

of Jesus. This is the secret, the hidden root of your redemption. Sink into it deeper day by day.

Believe with your whole heart that this Christ, whom God has given you, even as His divine

humility wrought the work for you, will enter in to dwell and work within you too, and make you

what the Father would have you be.

NOTE B

We need to know two things: One is that our salvation consists wholly in being saved from

ourselves, or that which we are by nature, and the other is that in the whole nature of things, nothing

could be this salvation or saviour to us but such a humility of God as is beyond all expression.

Hence, the first unalterable term of the Saviour to fallen man. Except a man denies himself, he

cannot be My disciple (Matthew 16:24). Self is the whole evil of fallen nature, while self-denial is

our capacity of being saved. Humility is our saviour, whereas the self is the root, the branches, and

the tree of all the evil of our fallen state. All the evils of fallen angels and men have their birth in

the pride of self. On the other hand, all the virtues of heavenly life are the virtues of humility.

It is humility alone that makes the impassable gulf between heaven and hell.

What then, or what lies in the great struggle for eternal life? It all lies in the strife between pride

and humility. Pride and humility are the two master powers, the two kingdoms in strife for the

eternal possession of man. There never was, nor ever will be, but one humility, and that is the

humility of Christ. Pride and self are all of man, till man has all from Christ. He therefore only

fights the good fight whose strife is that the self-idolatrous nature which he has from Adam may

be brought to death by the supernatural humility of Christ brought to life in him.

fields.title: Chapter 3. Humility In The Life Of Jesus
fields.body_html:
The life of Jesus while on earth was that of complete humility. If we emulate him and put

God in everything we do, it will be easy for us to humble ourselves before men and allow God

to do in us what He alone pleases. Learn how important it is to seek knowledge to understand

and live a purposeful life guided by humility, as exemplified by Jesus Christ.

"But I am among you as the one who serves." Luke 22 27.

n the Gospel of John, we have the inner life of our Lord laid open to us. Jesus speaks frequently

of His relation to the Father, of the motives by which He is guided, of His consciousness of the

power and spirit in which He acts. Though the word humble does not occur, we shall nowhere in

Scripture see so clearly wherein His humility consisted. We have already said that this grace is in

truth nothing but that simple consent of the creature to let God be all, in virtue of which it

surrenders itself to His working alone.

In Jesus, we shall see how both as the Son of God in heaven, and as man upon earth, He took the

place of entire subordination, and gave God the honor and the glory which is due to Him. And

what He taught so often was made true to Himself: "whoever humbles himself will be exalted."

(Matthew 23:12). As it is written, "Therefore God has highly exalted Him" (Philippians 2:9).

Listen to the words in which our Lord speaks of His relation to the Father, and how unceasingly

He uses the words not, and nothing, of Himself. The not I, in which Paul expresses his relation to

Christ, is the very spirit of what Christ says of His relation to the Father.

"The Son can do nothing of his own accord" (John 5:19).

"I can do nothing on my own. As I hear, I judge, and my judgment is just, because I seek not my

own will."

(John 5:30).

"I do not receive glory from people" (John 5:41).

"I have come down from heaven, not to do my own" (John 6:38).

"My teaching is not mine" (John 7:16)

I

"I have not come of my own" (John 7:28)

"I can do nothing on my own" (John 8:28)

"I came not of my own accord, but he sent me" (John 8:42).

"I do not seek my own glory" (John 8:50)

"The words that I say to you I do not speak on my own authority" (John 14:10).

"The word that you hear is not mine" (John 14:24).

These words open to us the deepest roots of Christ's life and work. They tell us how the Almighty

God was able to work His mighty redemptive work through Him. They show what Christ counted

the state of heart that became Him as the Son of the Father. They teach us what the essential nature

and life are of that redemption which Christ accomplished and now communicates. It is this:

He was nothing, that God might be all. He resigned Himself with His will and His powers entirely

for the Father to work in Him. Of His own power, His own will, and His own glory, of His whole

mission with all His works and His teaching, of all this He said, It is not I; I am nothing; I have

given Myself to the Father to work; I am nothing, the Father is all.

This life of entire self-abnegation, of absolute submission and dependence upon the Father's will,

Christ found to be one of perfect peace and joy. He lost nothing by giving all to God. God honored

His trust, and did all for Him, and then exalted Him to His own right hand in glory (Acts 5:31).

And because Christ had thus humbled Himself before God, and God was ever before Him, He

found it possible to humble Himself before men too, and to be the Servant of all. His humility was

simply the surrender of Himself to God, to allow Him to do in Him what He pleased, regardless

of whatever men around might say of Him, or do to Him.

It is in this state of mind, in this spirit and disposition, that the redemption of Christ has its virtue

and efficacy. It is to bring us to this disposition that we are made partakers of Christ. This is the

true self-denial to which our Saviour calls us, the acknowledgment that self has nothing good in

it, except as an empty vessel which God must fill, and that its claim to be or do anything may not

for a moment be allowed. It is in this, above and before everything, in which the conformity to

Jesus consists, the being and doing nothing of ourselves, that God may be all. Here we have the

root and nature of true humility. It is because this is not understood or sought after that our humility

is so superficial and so feeble.

We must learn of Jesus, how He is meek and lowly of heart. He teaches us that true humility takes

its rise and finds its strength in the knowledge that it is God who works all in all, that our place is

to yield to Him in perfect resignation and dependence, in full consent to be and to do nothing of

ourselves. This is the life Christ came to reveal and to impart, a life to God that came through death

to sin and self. If we feel that this life is too high and beyond our reach, then we must seek it in

Him. It is the indwelling Christ who will live in us this life, meek and lowly.

If we long for this, let us, in the meantime, above everything, seek the holy secret of the knowledge

of the nature of God, as He every moment works all in all. The secret, of which all nature, every

creature, and above all, every child of God, is to be the witness, that it is nothing but a vessel, a

channel, through which the living God can manifest the riches of His wisdom, power, and

goodness. The root of all virtue and grace, of all faith and acceptable worship, is that we know that

we have nothing but what we receive, and bow in deepest humility to wait upon God for it.

It was because this humility was not only a temporary sentiment, awakened and brought into

exercise when He thought of God, but the very spirit of His whole life, that Jesus was just as

humble in His intercourse with men as with God. He felt himself the Servant of God for the men

whom God made and loved. As a natural consequence, He counted Himself the Servant of men

that through Him God might do His work of love. He never for a moment thought of seeking His

honor, or asserting His power to vindicate Himself. His whole spirit was that of a life yielded to

God to work in.

It is not until Christians study the humility of Jesus as the very essence of His redemption, as the

very blessedness of the life of the Son of God, as the only true relation to the Father, and therefore

as that which Jesus must give us if we are to have any part with Him. The terrible lack of actual,

heavenly, manifest humility will become a burden and a sorrow, and our ordinary religion will be

set aside to secure this, the first and chief marks of Christ within us.

Brother, are you clothed with humility? Ask about your daily life. Ask Jesus. Ask your friends.

Ask the world. And begin to praise God since He has opened up to you in Jesus a heavenly humility

of which you have hardly known, and through which a heavenly blessedness you possibly have

not yet tasted can come into you.

fields.title: Chapter 4. Humility In The Teaching Of Jesus
fields.body_html:
Throughout Jesus’ life and teaching, humility is evidenced. In this chapter, Andrew explicitly

explains the basis and the works of humility in the life of a believer picking the example from

Jesus and how he lived successfully on earth with the virtue of humility.

"Learn from me, for I am gentle and lowly in heart" Matthew 11:29. "And whoever would be first

among you must be your slave, even as the Son of Man came not to be served but to serve"

Matthew 20:27.

e have seen humility in the life of Christ so, as He laid open His heart to us, let us listen

to His teaching. There we shall hear how He speaks of it, and how far He expects men,

and specially His disciples to be humble as He was. Let us carefully study the passages, which I

can scarcely do more than quote, to receive the full impression of how often and how earnestly He

taught it. This will help us to realize what He asks of us.

Look at the commencement of His ministry. In the Beatitudes with which the Sermon on the Mount

opens, He speaks: "Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven. Blessed are

the meek, for they shall inherit the earth." (Matthew 5:3, 5). The very first words of His

proclamation of the kingdom of heaven reveal the open gate through which alone we enter.

The poor, who have given up everything for the sake of Christ, to them the kingdom comes. One

might say: “But some Christians are really wealthy, owning land, cars, and lots of businesses.”

Yes, that can be very possible, especially as children of the Most High, but if they consider it

vanity, they can easily give it away for the gospel; they are poor in the Spirit. The meek, who seek

nothing in themselves, theirs the earth shall be. The blessings of heaven and earth are for the lowly.

For the heavenly and the earthly life, humility is the secret of blessing.

W

"Learn from me, for I am gentle and lowly in heart, and you will find rest for your souls." (Matthew

11:29). Jesus offers Himself as a Teacher. He tells what the spirit both is, which we shall find in

Him as Teacher, and can learn and receive from Him. Meekness and lowliness are the one thing

He offers us, and in them we shall find the perfect rest of the soul.

In the New Testament, we see the disciples disputing who would be the greatest in the kingdom

and had agreed to ask the Master (Luke 9:46, Matthew 18:3-5). He set a child in their midst and

said, "Whoever humbles himself like this child, shall be exalted." "Who is the greatest in the
