God's provision, experiencing a deep, abiding peace that comes from trusting Him

comp letely. The chapter underscores the importance of resting in God’s promises and

finding true peace in surrender.

n my last chapter, I tried to settle the question of the scripturalness of the Higher Christian Life. I

best describe it as the "life hidden with Christ in God." I now, therefore, consider it settled. The

Scriptures promise Jesus' believers a life of perfect rest. It will be a constant victory, beyond normal

Christian experience. They present a Saviour who can save us from the power of our sins, just as He

saves us from their guilt.

The next point to consider is, what this hidden life is. How does it differ from other Christian

experiences? It means letting the Lord manage our affairs and carry our burdens, instead of trying to

do it all ourselves. Most Christians are like a man, toiling along the road under a heavy burden. A

wagon overtook him, and the driver kindly offered to help him. He accepted the offer with great

enthusiasm. But, when seated, his burden weighed him down. He still had it on his shoulders. “Why

don’t you lay down your burden?” asked the kind - hearted driver. “Oh!” replied the man, “I feel that it

is almost too much to ask you to carry me, and I could not think of letting you carry my burden too.”

Christians, who have entrusted themselves to the Lord Jesus, still bear their burdens. They often grow

weary and heavy-laden on their journey. By "burdens," I mean anything that troubles us, whether

spiritual or temporal.

I

I mean, first of all, ourselves. The greatest burden we have to carry in life is self. The most difficult

thing we have to manage is self. Our daily lives, feelings, and unique flaws and desires trouble us most.

They often lead us into bondage and darkness.

In laying off your burdens, so, the first one you must get rid of is yourself. You must hand over to God

your inner self. This includes your temptations, temperament, and feelings. Then, leave them there. He

made you, and so He understands you and knows how to manage you, and you must trust Him to do it.

Say to Him, “Here, Lord, I abandon myself to you. I have tried in every way I could think of to manage

myself and to make myself what I know I ought to be, but have always failed.

Now I give it up to you. Do take entire possession of me. Work in me all the good pleasure of your

will. Mould and fashion me into such a vessel as seems good to you. I leave myself in your hands. I

believe you will, as you promised, make me a vessel for your honor. "Sanctified, and fit for the Master's

use, and prepared for every good work." Now, you must rest, trusting Him completely. Next, you must

lay off every other burden. Your health, reputation, Christian work, houses, children, business, and

servants. Everything that concerns you, inward or outward.

Christians always commit their souls to the Lord for eternity. They know, without a doubt, that they

cannot keep themselves. But, they take the things of this life into their own keeping. They try to carry

them with an unconfessed feeling. It is a lot to ask the Lord to carry them, and they cannot think to ask

Him to carry their burdens too.

I knew a Christian lady who had a very heavy temporal burden. It took away her sleep and her appetite,

and there was danger of her health breaking down under it. One day, it felt especially heavy. She

noticed a little tract called "Hannah's Faith" on the table near her.” Attracted by the title, she picked it

up and began to read. She did not know it would revolutionize her whole experience. The story was

about a poor woman who had endured great sorrow.

Once, she told a kind visitor the history of her life. At the end, the visitor said, “O, Hannah, I cannot

see how you could bear so much sorrow!” "I did not bear it," was the quick reply. "The Lord bore it

for me." "Yes," said the visitor. "That is the right way." "You must take your troubles to the Lord."

"Yes," replied Hannah. "But, we must do more; we must leave them there. Most people," she continued,

"take their burdens to Him, but they bring them back. They're as worried and unhappy as ever." But I

take mine, and I leave them with Him, and come away and forget them. And if the worry returns, I take

it to Him again. I do this over and over, until I forget my worries and am at perfect rest.”

My friend was very much struck with this plan and resolved to try it. She could not change her life. So,

she took it to the Lord. She handed it over to Him. Then, she believed He took it. She left all her worries

and anxieties with Him. Her anxieties returned often. She took them back. So, though things remained

unchanged, her soul found perfect peace. She felt she had found a blessed secret. From then on, she

tried never again to carry her own burdens or manage anything for herself. The secret worked wonders

in her outer affairs. It was even more effective in her inner ones, which were even more unmanageable.

She gave her whole self to the Lord. She trusted Him with all she had. So, she stopped worrying. Her

life became happy, for she belonged to Him. And this was the Higher Christian Life! It was a very

simple secret she found out.

Only this. One could obey God's commandment in these words: " Do not be anxious about anything,

but in everything by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known to

God. “Philippians 4 :6. If one obeyed, the result would be, according to the promise, that the "peace of

God, which passes all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus." There is

more to say about this life hid with Christ in God. Many details exist about what the Lord Jesus does

for those who abandon themselves to Him. The gist of the matter is here. The soul that knows this secret

has a key.

It will unlock God's treasure-house. I hope I have made you long for this blessed life.

Would you not like to get rid of your burdens? Do you not long to hand over the management of your

unmanageable self into the hands of one who can manage you? Are you not tired? Does the rest I speak

of not look sweet to you? Do you recall the blissful rest you felt after a tiring day, before bed? How

delightful it was to relax every muscle. To let my body go in perfect ease and comfort. The strain of

the day had ceased for a few hours at least, and the workers had thrown off the work of the day. You

no longer had to hold up an aching head or a weary back. You trusted the bed completely. It held you

up without any struggle. You rested. But suppose you had doubted your bed's strength. And, you feared

it would give way and drop you to the floor. Could you have rested then? Wouldn't every muscle have

strained to hold yourself up? Wouldn't the weariness have been greater than not to have gone to bed at

all?

Let this analogy teach you what it means to rest in the Lord. Let your souls lie down upon His sweet

will, as your bodies lie down in your beds at night. Relax every strain and lay off every burden.

Abandon all ease and comfort. Trust that, when He holds you up, you are safe. Your only task is to

rest. His part is to sustain you, and He cannot fail. Or, take another analogy, which our Lord has

sanctioned: that of the child- life said, “And calling to him a child, he put him in the midst of them and

said, 'Truly, I say to you, unless you turn and become like children, you will never enter the kingdom

of heaven.” Mathew 18:2 -3

Now, what are the characteristics of a little child, and how does he live? He lives by faith, and his

primary characteristic is thoughtlessness. His life is one long trust from year’s end to year’s end. He

trusts his parents, caretakers, and teachers. He even trusts some unworthy people, due to his confiding

nature. And his trust receives a generous response. He provides nothing for himself, and yet he receives

everything. He makes no plans for tomorrow. Yet, he plans his life. His paths open up to him as he

reaches them, hour by hour, day by day. He enters and leaves his father's house with ease and freedom.

He enjoys its treasures, having spent nothing to get them.

Plague may walk through the streets of his city, but he regards it not. Famine, fire, and war may rage

around him. But, under his father's care, he rests in perfect peace. He lives in the present, accepting life

as it comes. I once visited a wealthy house with an adopted only child. He received all the love and

care that human hearts and means could provide. Watching that child run in and out, day by day, I saw

a picture of our wonderful position as children in our Father's house. The child was free and light-

hearted, with the happy carelessness of childhood.

I thought, "If nothing could grieve her loved ones, it would be to see this child worry about herself."

How much more must our God's loving heart grieve at His children's worries? I understood the reason

our Lord had emphasized, "Take no thought for yourselves." Who is best cared for in every household?

Is it not the little children? And does not the least of all, the helpless baby, receive the largest share? A

late writer said that the baby "toils not, neither does he spin; nor yet someone feeds him, clothes him,

loves him, and rejoices in him." No one rejoices in him more than he does.

This life of faith, then, about which I am writing, consists in this: being a child in the Father’s house.

When someone says this, they say enough. It can transform every weary, burdened life into one of

blessedness and rest.

Let the carefree confidence of your little ones teach you how to be with God. It pleases you and wins

your hearts. Leave yourselves in His hands. "Do not be anxious about anything, but in everything by

prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known to God. And the peace of

God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your minds in Christ Jesus."

Philipians4:6-7

Notice the word 'nothing' in the above passage. It covers all possible grounds for anxiety, both inward

and outward. We often feel pressured to believe it is our duty to be anxious about certain matters.

We will think, "it's right to give up all anxiety. In spiritual matters, anxiety is wrong. But we must be

anxious about some things. It would be a sin not to be. We must worry about our children, those we

love, our church, the truth, and our business." It would show a great want of right feeling not to be

anxious about such things as these.” Or, we may think, "Ye s, it's right to trust the Lord with our loved

ones and affairs. But we should worry about our inner lives, our faith, our temptations, and our sins. If

we don't, they will neglect them."

We find the answer to such suggestions, and to all similar ones, in our text: “Therefore I tell you, do

not be anxious about your life, what you will eat or what you will drink, nor about your body, what

you will put on. Isn't life more than food, and the body more than clothing?

Look at the birds of the air: they neither sow nor reap nor gather into barns, and yet your heavenly

Father feeds them. Are you not of more value than they? And which of you by being anxious can add

a single hour to his span of life? And why are you anxious about clothing? Consider the lilies of the

field, how they grow: they neither toil nor spin, yet I tell you, even Solomon in all his glory was not

arrayed like one of these. But if God so clothes the grass of the field, which today is alive and tomorrow

is thrown into the oven, will he not much more clothe you, O you of little faith? Therefore do not be

anxious, saying, ‘What shall we eat?’ or ‘What shall we drink?’ or ‘what shall we wear?’’ Mathew

6:25-31

“For the Gentiles seek after all these things, and your heavenly Father knows that you need them all.

But seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things will be added to you.

“Therefore do not be anxious about tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for itself. Sufficient for

the day is its own trouble.” I n Matt. 6:32-34, our Lord illustrates this being without anxiety, by telling

us to behold the fowls of the air and the lilies of the field, as examples of the sort of life He would have

us live. We must, without anxiety or fear, be like the birds and lilies. The birds rejoice in God's care

and receive food. The lilies grow in His sunlight. Let the sparrows speak to us:

"I am a tiny sparrow, a bird of low degree. My life is of little value, but the dear Lord cares for me. I

have no barn nor storehouse. I neither sow nor reap. He gives me a sparrow's portion, but never a seed

to keep. "I know there are many sparrows. People find them all over the world. But our heavenly Father

knows when one of us falls to the ground. "Though small, we are never forgotten. Though weak, we

are never afraid. For we know the dear Lord keeps the life of the creatures he made. "I soar above the

densest trees and settle on many branches." I have no chart nor compass, but I never lose my way."

I fold my wing at twilight, wherever I may be. The Father is always watching. No harm will come to

me. I am only a little sparrow, a bird of low degree. But I know the Father loves me. Have you less

faith than we?”

fields.title: Chapter 4. How To Enter In
fields.body_html:
Entering the Higher Christian Life is a gift from God, not something we earn. It begins

with total surrender to God’s will, trusting Him completely, just as a patient follows a

doctor’s instructions for healing. Faith is essential, as we must believe God will deliver

us not only from sin's guilt but also from its power. The key steps to this life are complete

abandonment and faith, leading to peace and victory over life's

challenges.

have tried to settle the question of the scripturalness of the experience of this life of full trust. I have

also shown a little of what it is. The next point is how to reach and realize it. And first, I would say

that we must not look upon this blessed life in any sense as an attainment but as an obtainment. We

cannot earn it, we cannot climb up to it, we cannot win it; we can do nothing but ask for it and

receive it. It is the gift of God in Christ Jesus. And where a thing is a gift, the only course left for the

receiver is to take it and thank the giver. We never say of a gift, "See what I have attained," and boast

of our skill in gaining it. Instead, we say, "See what the giver has given me," and we boast of the giver's

love and generosity.

And everything in our salvation is a gift. From beginning to end, God is the giver and we are the

receivers. The richest promises are not for those who do great things. They are for those who "receive

plenty of grace, and of the gift of righteousness." To know this inner life, the soul must be receptive. It

must recognize completely that it is to be God's gift in Christ Jesus. We cannot gain it through any

efforts or works of our own. This will make things much simpler. The only question left is who will

receive this gift from God, and how to accept it. I would answer that He grants it only to the soul that

is completely consecrated. You must receive it by faith.

I

Consecration is the first thing. Not in any legal sense, nor to buy or deserve it. But, to remove the

obstacles and allow God to give it. To create a beautiful vessel from a lump of clay, the potter must

have complete control over it. It must lie passive in his hands. To make a soul a vessel for God's honor,

it must be "sanctified and meet for the Master's use, and prepared unto every good work." It must be

completely abandoned to Him and remain passive in His hands. This is manifest at the first glance.

I once tried to explain to a hospital doctor the meaning and need for consecration. But, he seemed

unable to understand. At last, I said to him, "Suppose, in your rounds, you meet a man who begs you

to cure him. But, he won't tell you all his symptoms or take your remedies.

He'd say, 'I'm willing to follow your directions on some things, as they seem good to me. But, in other

matters, I prefer to follow my own judgment.' What would you do?" I asked.

“Do!” he replied with indignation, “do! I would soon leave such a man as that to his own care. "Of

course," he added. "I could do nothing for him. He must obey my directions." "So, patients must obey

doctors to be cured?" "Implicitly obeyed!” was his emphatic reply. “And that is 20 consecration,” I

continued. "God must have the whole case, without reserves. His directions must be followed

implicitly.” “I see it,” he exclaimed, -- “I see it! And I will do it. God must have His own way with me

from henceforth.”

Some may think "abandonment" is a better word. But whatever we use, we mean a total surrender to

God. We give Him our spirit, soul, and body. We want Him to do with us as He pleases. We mean that

our soul's language in all things should express, "Your will be done. “We mean giving up all choice.

We mean a life of inevitable obedience. To a soul ignorant of God, this may look hard. But to those

who know Him, it is the happiest and most restful of lives. He is our Father. He loves us and knows

what is best. So, His will is the most blessed thing that can come to us, no matter the circumstances. I

do not understand how it is that Satan has succeeded in blinding the eyes of the Church to this fact. But

it seems God's children fear His will more than anything. His lovely, lovable will means only good for

their souls. It brings loving-kindness, tender mercies, and great blessings.

I wish I could only show everyone the unfathomable sweetness of the will of God. Heaven is a place

of infinite bliss. His will is perfectly done there. Our lives share in this bliss as His will is done in them.

He loves us, loves us, and the will of love is always a blessing for its loved one. Some of us know love.

If we could, we would bless our beloved ones. We would shower them with all that is good and lovely

in life if we had the power to fulfill our wish for them.

And if this is the way of love with us, how much more must it be so with our God, who is love itself.

If we could see, even for a moment, the depths of His love, we would rush to embrace His will as our

greatest treasure. We would abandon ourselves to it, filled with joy and gratitude for such a privilege.

Many Christians believe their Father in heaven wants to make them miserable and take their blessings.

They imagine, poor souls, that if they cling to their own will, they can stop Him from doing this. I am

ashamed to write the words, and yet we must face a fact which is making wretched hundreds of lives.

A Christian lady, feeling this way, told a friend how hard it was to say, "Your will be done," and how

afraid she was to do it. She was the mother of one only little boy, who was the heir to a great fortune,

and the idol of her heart. After she shared her troubles, her friend said, "What if your little Charley runs

to you tomorrow?" He says, 'Mother, I have decided to let you have your way with me from now on.'

I'm always going to obey you. "I want you to do what you think is best with me."

I know you love me, and I will trust your love. How would you feel towards him? Would you say to

yourself, ‘Ah, now I shall have a chance to make Charley miserable?

I will take away all his pleasures, and fill his life with every hard and disagreeable thing I can find. I

will force him to do the hardest things. Then, I w ill give him all sorts of impossible commands.” “Oh,

no, no, no!” exclaimed the indignant mother. “You know I would not. I would hug him to my heart and

cover him with kisses. I would fill his life with the sweetest, best things.” “And are you more tender

and more loving than God?” asked her friend. "Ah, no," was the reply. "I see my mistake. I will not

fear saying 'Your will be done,' to my Heavenly Father, any more than I'd want my Charley to fear

saying it to me."”

Better and sweeter than health, or friends, or money, or fame, or ease, or prosperity, is the adorable will

of our God. It brightens the dark hours with a divine halo. It sheds bright sunshine on the gloomiest

paths. He always reigns who has made it his kingdom; and nothing can go amiss to him. A glorious

privilege is opening before you. The first step to enter the life hidden with Christ in God is complete

consecration. I cannot have you look at it as a hard and stern demand. You must do it with joy,

appreciation, and enthusiasm. You must enter what I call the privilege side of consecration. I assure

you, from a blessed experience, it is the happiest place you will ever find.

Faith is the next thing. Faith is essential to receiving any gift. Our friends may give us something in its

entirety, but we do not own it until we believe they have given it and we claim it. This is especially

true for gifts that are purely mental or spiritual. Another may love us without limit. But, until we believe

it, it never becomes ours. I suppose most Christians know this about their forgiveness.

They know that the preaching of Jesus' forgiveness of sins might have gone on forever. But, it would

never be theirs until they claimed the forgiveness. They had to believe it first. But, in living the

Christian life, they lose sight of this. They think, having been saved by faith, they must now live by

works. Instead of continuing to receive, they now must begin to do. This makes our declaration that

the life hid with Christ in God is to be entered by faith, seem perfectly unintelligible to them.

And yet it is plainly declared, that “as we have received Christ Jesus the Lord, so we are to walk in

Him.” We received Him by faith, and by faith alone; so we are to walk in Him by faith, and by faith

alone. Our faith in this hidden life is the same as the faith that moved us from the kingdom of darkness

to God's Son. It just relies on a different thing. Then we believed that Jesus was our Saviour from sin's

guilt. Our faith made it so. Now, we must believe He is our Saviour from sin's power. Our faith will

make it so. We trusted Him for our justification, and it became ours. Now, we must trust Him for our

sanctification, and it shall be ours, too. Then we took Him as a Saviour in the future from our sins'

penalties. Now, we must take Him as a Saviour in the present from our sins' bondage.

Then He was our Redeemer, now He is to be our Life. Then He lifted us from the pit. Now, He is to

seat us in heavenly places with Himself. I mean this based on both experimental and practical evidence.

I know, theologically and judicially, that every believer has everything at conversion. But

experimentally, nothing is his until by faith he claims it. “ Every place that the sole of your foot will

tread upon me have given to you, just as I promised to Moses. “Joshua 1:3. “Blessed be the God and

Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us in Christ with every spiritual blessing in the

heavenly places,"Ephesians1:3. But, until we have faith in them, they are not ours. “According to our

faith,” is always the limit and the rule.

But this faith of which I am speaking must be a present faith. No faith that people exercise in the future

tense amounts to anything. A man may believe forever that some future time will forgive his sins, and

he will never find peace. He has to come to the now belief, and say by faith, “My sins are now forgiven,”

before he can live the new life. Also, no faith that seeks future rescue from sin will lead a soul into the

life we describe. The enemy delights in this future faith. He knows it is powerless to achieve any results.

But he trembles and flees when a believer claims to be free from his power. In short: to enter this

blessed life of rest and triumph, you must take two steps. First, abandon all.

Second, have absolute faith.

Whatever your troubles, these two steps will help you. If you take them, and stick to them, they will

lead you to a better Christian life. You may be sure of this. If you will set aside all else, and focus on

these two points, your progress will be swift. You will reach your soul's desired haven sooner than you

now think possible.

Must I repeat the steps, that there may be no mistake? You are a child of God, and long to please Him.

You love your precious Saviour, and are sick and weary of the sin that grieves Him. You long for

someone to deliver you from its power. All you've tried has failed. In despair, you now wonder if, as

these happy people say, the Lord can and will save you. You know in your soul that He can. To save

you from all your enemies is His purpose.

Then trust Him. Commit your case to Him. Abandon all else and believe He will take it. Knowing what

He is and what He has said, claim that He provides complete salvation for you now. At first, you

believed He freed you from sin's guilt because He said so. Now, believe that He frees you from sin's

power because He says so. Let your faith now lay hold of a new power in Christ. You have trusted Him

as your dying Saviour, now trust Him as your living Saviour. Just as much as He came to deliver you

from future punishment, didn’t He also come to deliver you from present bondage. As He came to bear

your sins for you, He has come to live His life within you.

You are completely powerless in both cases. You could rid yourself of your own sins with the same

effort. As you could now achieve practical righteousness. Christ, and Christ only, must do both for you.

Your part is to give the thing to Him, and then believe He does it.

A now eminent lady, in a great darkness, sought to enter in. She said to a friend trying to help her, "You

all say, 'Abandon yourself, and trust.' But I do not know how." I wish you would just do it out loud, so

that I may see how you do it.”Must I do it out loud for you?

"Lord Jesus, You can and will deliver me from all the cares and troubles of my Christian life. You died

to set me free, not in the future, but now and here." you are stronger than Satan. You can keep me, even

in my weakness, from falling into his traps or obeying him. And, Lord, I am going to trust thee to keep

me. I have tried to maintain my composure, and I have failed, suffering a significant setback. I am

completely helpless; so, I will trust you now. I will give myself to thee; I hold nothing back. Body,

soul, and spirit, I present myself, a worthless lump of clay. Make me into whatever thy love and wisdom

choose. And now, I am thine.

You accept what I present. Your power has taken my weak, foolish heart. You have begun to work in

me to will and to do of your good pleasure. I trust you completely, and I trust you now! Are you afraid

to take this step? Does it seem too sudden, too much like a leap in the dark? Do you not know that the

steps of faith always “fall on the seeming void, but find the rock beneath”? A man, having to descen d

a well by a rope, found, to his horror, when he was a great way down, that it was too short. He had

reached the end, and yet was, he estimated, about thirty feet from the bottom of the well. He knew not

what to do. He lacked the strength or skill to climb up the rope, and letting go would dash him to pieces.

His arms began to fail. He decided to let go and meet his fate. He resigned himself to destruction, and

loosened his grasp. He fell! To the bottom of the well it was -- three inches! If ever your feet are to

touch the "rock beneath," you must let go of every hold and drop into God. For, there is no other way.

And to do it now may save you months and even years of strain and weariness. In all the old castles of

England there used to be a place called the keep. It was the castle's strongest, best-protected place. It

hid the weak and helpless in times of danger. If you were a timid, helpless woman in a castle under

siege, would you have dared to hide there?

Would you have been afraid to do it? Must we fear to hide in the keeping power of our Divine Keeper?

He neither slumbers nor sleeps. He has promised to preserve our going out and coming in, now and

forever.

fields.title: Chapter 5. Difficulties Concerning Consecration
fields.body_html:
Consecration often leads to doubt because believers rely on feelings rather than faith.

The author emphasizes that consecration is an act of faith — once we surrender to God,

we must trust that He accepts us, regardless of our emotions. Believers are encouraged

to affirm their surrender, stand firm in faith, and rely on God's promises instead of

feelings.

hristians must know the enemy's devices. He will oppose every step of the soul's progress. And,

especially, he is busy when he sees a believer awakened to a hunger for righteousness. They seek

to grasp all the fullness in the Lord Jesus Christ. One of the first difficulties he throws in their way is

about consecration. The seeker after holiness receives the instruction to consecrate himself. He tries to

do so. But at once he meets with a difficulty. He has done it, as he thinks. Yet, he feels no different.

Nothing seems changed, as he expected. He feels baffled and, in despair, asks, "How am I to know

when I am consecrated?"

At this point, the one grand temptation is to feel. It always tries to assert itself, and it often succeeds.

The soul cannot believe it is consecrated until it experiences consecration. It cannot believe God has

taken it, as it does not feel that. As usual, it puts feeling first and faith second. Now, God's rule is

simple: faith first, feelings second, in all things. It's futile to try to change this.

To resist this temptation about consecration, take God's side. Put faith before feeling. Surrender

yourself completely and without reservation to the Lord. Use your current understanding. Ask the Holy

Spirit to reveal anything in your heart or life that is against God. If He shows you anything, give it to

the Lord immediately, and say in reference to it, “Your will be done.” If He shows you nothing, then

you must believe that there is nothing, and must conclude that you have given Him all. Then you must

believe that He takes you. You must not wait to feel either that you have given yourself or that He has

taken you. You must simply believe it, and reckon it to be the case.

C

If you were to give an estate to a friend, you would have to give it, and he would have to receive it by

faith. No one can hand over an estate. Its gift and reception are a mental transaction, and thus, a matter

of faith. If you gave an estate to a friend for one day, you might wonder if you really had, and if he

took it. You might then feel the need to renew the gift the next day. If, on the third day, you still felt

uncertain, you would renew it again. You would repeat this process daily for months or years.

What would your friend think? And what would your mind be like after all that?

Your friend would doubt if you meant to give it to him. You would be so confused that you wouldn't

know if the estate was yours, his, or someone else's. Now, is this not how you have acted towards God

in this matter of consecration? You have given yourself to Him daily for months. But, after each time,

you have wondered if you truly gave yourself to Him and if He accepted you. Since you felt no

different, you concluded, after much doubt, that it was not done.

Dear believer, this confusion will last forever unless you end it with faith. You must accept the matter

as settled. Only then can you expect a change of feeling. The law of offerings to the Lord proves that

everything given to Him becomes holy. It is set apart and cannot be used for any other purpose. To do

so would be disrespect.

"Devoted things, both of man and beast, are most holy to the Lord. “They cannot sell or redeem them.

Once the Israelites gave the devoted thing to the Lord, they reckoned it as belonging to the Lord." No

one dared to reclaim it. The giver might have made his offering with reluctance and a lack of

enthusiasm. But, once made, the matter was out of his hands. By God's own law, the gift became "most

holy unto the Lord."”

It was not the intention of the giver that made it holy, but the holiness of the receiver. “The altar

sanctifies the gift.” And an offering once laid upon the altar, from that moment belonged to the L ord.

I can imagine the one who had deposited a gift. He might then doubt his sincerity and honesty in doing

so. He would return to the priest, anxious about his sincerity. I am sure the priest would have silenced

him at once. He would have said, "I do not know your motives in giving your offering."

The facts are that you did give it, and that it is the Lord’s, for every devoted thing is most holy unto

Him. "It is too late to recall the transaction now." All Israel, not just the priest, would be shocked at a

man who, having offered his gift, tried to take it back. And yet, day after day, earnest Christians, who

would shudder at a Jew's disrespect, are guilty of a similar act. They consecrate themselves to the Lord,

then take it back through unbelief. Because God is not visibly present to the eye, it is difficult to feel

that a transaction with Him is real.

If, when we consecrated ourselves, we could see Him, it would feel real. We would know we had given

our word and could not take it back, no matter how much we might want to. It would have to us the

binding power of a spoken promise to an earthly friend. It always has that power to a man of honor.

We need to see that God's presence is always a certain fact. Every act of our soul is done right before

Him. A word spoken in prayer is as really spoken to Him, as if our eyes could see Him and our hands

could touch Him.

Then, we will no longer have vague ideas about our relations with Him. We will feel the weight of

every word we say in His presence. I know some will say, "Ah, yes. “But, if He would only speak to

me and say that He took me when I gave myself to Him, I would then believe it."

"No, of course you would not. But, He does not usually say this until the soul has first proved its

loyalty by believing what He has already said. It is he that believes who has the witness, not he that

doubted. And by His very command to us to present ourselves to Him as a living sacrifice, He has

pledged Himself to receive us.

I cannot imagine an honorable man asking another to give him a thing he was doubtful about taking. I

can imagine even less a loving parent acting so towards a darling child. “My son, give me your heart,

and let your eyes observe my ways .” Proverbs 23:26.This is a sure warrant. It means that th e moment

the heart is given, it will be taken by the One who has commanded the gift. We must, then, feel the

utmost confidence. When we surrender to the Lord, as He commands, He then receives us. From that

moment, we are His.

A real transaction has taken place. It cannot be violated without dishonor on our part. We know He will

not violate it. In Deut. 26:17- 19 shows God's way of working: “You have declared today that the LORD

is your God, and that you will walk in his ways, and keep his statutes and his commandments and his

rules, and will obey his voice. And the LORD has declared today that you are a people for his treasured

possession, as he has promised you, and that you are to keep all his commandments, and that he will

set you in praise and in fame and in honor high above all nations that he has made, and that you shall

be a people holy to the LORD your God, as he promised .”

We declare the Lord our God. We will walk in His ways and keep His commandments. He declares us

to be His, and we must keep all His commandments. And from that moment, He takes possession of

us. This has always been His principle of working, and it continues to be so. “Every devoted thing is

most holy to the Lord.” This is so plain that it admits no question. But, if you stil l doubt, let me refer

you to a New Testament declaration. It approaches the subject differently, but it settles it, I think, quite

definitively. It is in 1 John 5:14- 15, and reads: “ And this is the confidence that we have toward him,

that if we ask anything according to his will he hears us. And if we know that he hears us in whatever

we ask, we know that we have the requests that we have asked of him .”

Is it according to His will that you should be fully consecrated to Him? There can be, of course, but

one answer to this, for He has commanded it. Is it not also according to His will that He should work

in you to will and to do of His good pleasure? This question also can have but one answer, for He has

declared it to be His purpose. You know, then, that these things are according to His will. So, on God's

word, you must know that He hears you. Now, you must go further. You must know that you have the

petitions you desired of Him.

That you have, I say, not will have, or may have, but have now in actual possession. It is so that we

“ Obtain promises” by faith. It is so that we have “access by faith” into the grace that is given us in our

Lord Jesus Christ. Only by this do we know our hearts are "purified by faith."

We can then live, stand, and walk by faith. I want to make this subject so clear and practical that no

one will have further trouble with it. So, I will repeat what your soul must do to resolve your doubts

about consecration.

I trust you have faith in the Lord Jesus to forgive your sins. I hope you know what it is to belong to

God's family and to be an heir of God through faith in Christ. And now you feel springing up in your

soul the longing to be conformed to the image of your Lord. You must fully surrender yourself to Him.

Only then may He work in you all the good pleasure of His will. You have tried to do this, but with no

success. I want to help you now. Now, you must come to Him again. Surrender your whole self to His

will, as completely as you can.

You must ask Him to show you any hidden rebellion by His Spirit. If he reveals nothing, believe there

is none. Your surrender is complete. We must, then, consider this a settled matter. You have abandoned

yourself to the Lord. From now on, you do not belong to yourself. Never listen to any suggestion to the

contrary. If you wonder if you've fully surrendered, assert that you have. Do not even argue the matter.

Repel any such idea without hesitation and with firm resolve.

You meant it then, you mean it now, you have accomplished it. Your emotions may clamor against the

surrender, but your will must hold firm. God looks at your purpose, not your feelings about it. So, your

will is all you need to attend to. Having made a surrender, never question or recall it. Next, believe that

God takes what you have surrendered. Reckon it is His. Not that it will be at some future time, but is

now; and that He has begun to work in you to will, and to do, of His good pleasure. And here you must

rest. You have nothing more to do. You belong to the Lord now, completely in His hands. He has taken

on the care and management of you. He will, as His word says, "work in you that which is well-pleasing

in His sight through Jesus Christ."

But you must maintain a firm grip here. If you doubt your surrender, or God's acceptance of it, your

faith will waver. A wavering faith will lead to a shaky experience, and He cannot work. But, while you

trust He works, His work changes you. It makes you more like Christ, from glory to glory, by His

mighty Spirit. Do you, now, at this moment, surrender yourself wholly to Him? You answer, yes. Then,

my dear friend, reckon that you are His. He has taken you. He is working in you to will and to do of

His good pleasure. And keep on reckoning this.

It will help you to put your thoughts into words. Say to yourself and to God, "Lord, I am yours. I yield

myself to you, and I believe you do take me." I leave myself with you. "Work in me all the good

pleasure of thy will. I will only lie still in thy hands and trust you." Make this a daily act of your will.

Many times a day, return to it as your constant attitude before Him. Confess it to yourself. Confess it

to your God. Confess it to your friends. Always declare the Lord as your God. Commit to walking in

His ways and keeping His laws.

You will then find that He has claimed you as His special people. You must keep all His

commandments and be "a holy people unto the Lord, as He has spoken."

You may find a few simple rules helpful here. I advise using them in daily devotions. They should test

the soul until we gain clarity on this matter.

I. State clearly your faith in Christ as your Saviour. Also, acknowledge that you believe He

has reconciled you to God, as per 2 Cor. 5:18- 19 “ All this is from God, who through Christ

reconciled us to himself and gave us the ministry of reconciliation; that is, in Christ God

was reconciling the world to himself, not counting their trespasses against them, and

entrusting to us the message of reconciliation.”

II. Definitely, acknowledge God as your Father. You are His redeemed and forgiven child,

according to Galatians 4:5, “ to redeem those who were under the law, so that we might

receive adoption as sons.”

III. Surrender completely to the Lord, body, soul, and spirit. Obey Him in everything where His

will is known, per Romans. 12:12. “Rejoice in hope, be patient in tribulation, be constant in

prayer.”

IV. Believe, against all odds, that God takes what you abandon to Him. He will work in you,

unless you frustrate His grace. See 2 Corinthians. 6:17- 18 “ Therefore go out from their

midst, and be separate from them, says the Lord, and touch no unclean thing; then I will

welcome you, and I will be a father to you, and you shall be sons and daughters to me, says

the Lord Almighty .” , and Philippians. 2:13. “For it is G od who works in you, both to will and

to work for his good pleasure.”

V. Don't use your feelings to test your relations with God. Focus on your will and faith instead.

And count all these steps you are now taking as settled, though the enemy may make it seem

otherwise. Heb. 10:22-23. “Let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith, with

our hearts sprinkled clean from an evil conscience and our bodies washed with pure water.

Let us hold fast the confession of our hope without wavering, for he who promised is

faithful.”

VI. Never, under any circumstances, should you doubt or feel discouraged. Remember, that all

discouragement is from the devil, and refuse to admit it; according to John 14:1 “Let not

your hearts be troubled. Believe in God, believe also in me ” V27 “Peace I leave with you;

my peace I give to you. Not as the world gives do I give to you. Let not your hearts be

troubled, neither let them be afraid.”

VII. Cultivate the habit of expressing your faith in clear words. Repeat often, "I am all the Lord's.

He is working in me now to will and to do of His good pleasure," according to Heb. 13:21

“ equip you with everything good that you may do his will, working in us that which is

pleasing in his sight, through Jesus Christ, to whom be glory forever and ever.

Amen.

fields.title: Chapter 6. Difficulties Concerning Faith
fields.body_html:
Faith is the next step after consecration, leading the soul into the fullness of Christian

life. It is not a tangible feeling but simply believing God’s promises, much like

trusting others in daily life. True faith means resting in God’s word without worry or

doubt, trusting Him as we trust those around us. Just as slaves had to believe in their

freedom to experience it, we must believe in God’s promises to receive His blessings.

Trusting God glorifies Him and leads to the fulfillment of His will in our lives .

fter consecration, the next step is faith. It leads the soul out of the wilderness of Christian

experience into a land flowing with milk and honey. And here, as in the first step, the enemy is

very skilled at creating difficulties and obstacles. The child of God, seeing the fullness in Jesus

for him, longs to grasp it. But, every teacher he asks asserts that only faith can receive it. But, his

mind is a mystery about faith. This assertion, instead of helping, makes it more difficult and complex

than ever.

“Of course it is to be by faith,” he says, “for I know that everything in the Christian life is by faith. But

then, that is what makes it so hard, for I have no faith, and I do not even know what it is, nor how to

get it.” And, baffled by this difficulty, he is plunged into despair. This trouble arises from a

misunderstanding of faith. In truth, faith is the simplest thing in the world, and the easiest to attain.

Your idea of faith, I suppose, has been something like this. You view it as a sort of thing. It's either a

religious exercise of the soul or a gracious disposition of the heart. It's something tangible. When you

have it, you can rejoice in it. You can use it as a passport to God's favor, or a coin to buy His gifts. You

have been praying for faith. You expected to get something like this. But, you never received anything.

So, you insist that you have no faith. Now faith, in fact, is not in the least this sort of thing.

It is nothing at all tangible.

A

It is simply believing God, and, like sight, it is nothing apart from its object. You might as well shut

your eyes and look inside to see if you have sight, as to look inside to see if you have faith. You see

something, and thus know that you have sight; you believe something, and thus know that you have

faith. For, as sight is only seeing, so faith is only believing. The only necessary thing about seeing is,

to see the thing as it is. So, the only necessary thing about believing is, to believe the thing as it is.

The virtue does not lie in your believing, but in the thing you believe. If you believe the truth, you are

saved; if you believe a lie, you are lost. The belief is the same in both cases. The things believed in are

exactly opposite. This is what makes the mighty difference. Your salvation comes, not because your

faith saves you. It is because it links you to the Saviour who saves. Your faith is really nothing but the

link.

I beg you to see, then, the simplicity of faith. It is just believing God when He says He has done

something for us, or will do it. Then, we must trust Him to do it. It is so simple that it is hard to explain.

If anyone asks what it means to trust someone to do a job for me, I can only answer this: It means

letting them do it. I feel it is unnecessary to do it myself. We have all trusted others with important

work. We felt perfect rest in this trust. It was because we had confidence in those who took it on. How

often do mothers trust their precious infants to nurses, without a hint of anxiety?

We all trust our health and lives to cooks, coachmen, engine drivers, and train conductors. We do this

without fear. These paid servants could ruin us in an instant if they chose to or if they were careless.

All this we do, and make no fuss about it. We often trust people after a brief acquaintance. We need

only a general knowledge of human nature and common social rules. We never feel we're doing

anything remarkable. You have done all this yourself, dear reader, and are doing it continually. You

could not live in this world for a day if you could not trust your fellow men. And it never enters into

your head to say you cannot.

But yet you do not hesitate to say, continually, that you cannot trust your God! Please, imagine acting

in your human relations as you do in your spiritual ones. Imagine you must start tomorrow with a

thought in your head: you could trust nobody, as you had no faith. At breakfast, you would say, "I

cannot eat anything on this table. I have no faith. I can't believe the cook hasn't poisoned the coffee. Or

that the butcher hasn't sent diseased meat. So you would starve. Then, you'd say, "I cannot ride the

train. “I have no faith, so I cannot trust anyone."

You would have to walk everywhere. You would grow very weary. Also, you could not reach many

places you could have reached by train. When your friends or business agent brought you statements,

you'd say, "I'm sorry, but I can't believe you. “I have no f aith and can't trust anyone." If you read a

newspaper, you'd have to put it down. You'd say, "I can't believe a word it says. I have no faith. I don't

believe there is a queen, for I've never seen her. And I don't believe in Ireland, for I've never been

there." And I have no faith, so of course I cannot believe anything that I have not actually felt and

touched myself. It is a great trial, but I cannot help it, for I have no faith.”

Imagine such a day. It would be disastrous for you. It would seem foolish to anyone who watched you

throughout the day. Know your friends would feel insulted. Your servants would quit. Then ask

yourself this: If it's so dreadful to distrust your fellow men, what of telling God you can't trust Him?

You say it's a great trial, but you can't help it; you have no faith. Can you trust your fellow men but not

your God? That you can receive the “witness of men,” and cannot receive the “witness of God?” That

you can believe man’s records, and cannot believe God’s record? You trust your weak, failing fellow-

creatures with your dearest interests. Yet, you fear to commit your soul to the blessed Saviour.

He shed His blood to save you. He is "able to save you to the Uttermost."

Surely, dear believer, your name implies you can believe. So, you will never again dare to excuse your

lack of faith. This means, of course, that you have no faith in God. You are not asked to have faith in

yourself. If you did, it would be a very wrong state of soul. I beg you, when you think or say these

things, to complete the sentence. Say, "I have no faith in God, I cannot believe in God." I am sure this

will soon become so dreadful to you that you won't dare to continue it.

But you say, I cannot believe without the Holy Spirit. Very well; will you conclude that your want of

faith is because of the failure of the blessed Spirit to do His work? If it is, then you are not to blame.

You need to feel no condemnation. All my urges to believe are useless. But, no! Do you not see that,

in taking this position, you have no faith and cannot believe? You are "making God a liar." You are

also showing a complete lack of trust in the Holy Spirit. For He is always ready to help our infirmities.

We never have to wait for Him, He is always waiting for us. I have complete faith in the Holy Ghost.

He is always ready to do His work. So, I say to you all: you can believe now, at this moment. If you do

not, it is not the Spirit's fault, but your own.

Put your will then over on to the believing side. Say, “Lord I will believe, I do believe,” and continue

to say it. Insist on believing, even when every suggestion of doubt tempts you. In your unbelief, throw

yourself on God's word and promises. Dare to trust in the saving power of the Lord Jesus. If you have

ever trusted a friend with something precious, I urge you to trust yourself now. Trust your spiritual

interests to your Heavenly Friend. Never, never, NEVER doubt again.

And remember, trust and worry are more incompatible than oil and water. Would you call it trust? If

you ask a friend to do something for you, then you spend your days and nights worrying if they will do

it right. Can you call it trust? You have put your soul in the Lord's hands. But, you spend hours each

day and night, filled with anxiety as you question it. When a believer really trusts anything, he ceases

to worry about that thing which he has trusted.

And when he worries, it is a plain proof that he does not trust. Tested by this rule how little real trust

there is in the Church of Christ! No wonder our L ord asked the pathetic question, “When the Son of

Man comes shall he find faith on the earth?” He will find much activity and earnestness. There will be

many devoted hearts. But, will he find faith? It is the one thing He values most. It is a solemn question,

and I would that every Christian heart would ponder it well. But, may our past lives suffice us. We

have shared in the world's unbelief. So, let us, who know our blessed Lord, prove His truth.

His trustworthiness is beyond words. We must, with our hearts, trust Him fully.

I remember, very early in my Christian life, an appeal in a volume of old sermons. It stirred my every

tender and loyal impulse. It urged all who loved the Lord Jesus to show others His worthiness by their

own steadfast faith in Him. I remember my soul cried out with a longing. I longed to walk those dark

paths. My total distrust would be a blessed, glorious privilege.

"You have not passed this way before," it may be. But today, it is your happy privilege to prove, as

never before, your loyal confidence in the Lord. Start with Him on a life of faith, lived in absolute,

childlike trust in Him. You have trusted Him in a few things, and He has not failed you. Trust Him now

for everything. See if He does not do for you more than you could ever ask or think. It won't be by your

strength, but by His mighty power. It will work in you all the good pleasure of His most blessed will.

You trust the Lord to manage the universe and all creation. Can your case be more complex than these?

You need not be anxious about his management of it. Away with such unworthy doubting! Trust in

your God. Observe how all problems will vanish swiftly before a strong will to believe. Trust in the

dark, the light, at night, and in the morning. You will find that, though faith may start as a mighty effort,

it will become a natural habit of the soul.

All things are possible to God. Mark 11:23“And Jesus said to him , if you can’! All things are possible

for one who believes" "Faith has, in the past, 'subdued kingdoms, wrought righteousness, obtained

promises, stopped the mouths of lions, quenched the violence of fire, escaped the edge of the sword,

waxed valiant in fight, [and] turned to fight the armies of the aliens.' And faith can do it again." Our

Lord says, “Because of your little faith. For truly, I say to you, if you have faith like a grain of mustard

seed, you will say to this mountain, ‘Move from here to there,’ and it will move, and nothing will be

impossible for you. “Mathew 17:20 If you are a child of God, you must have at least a mustard seed's

worth of faith. So, you cannot say again that you cannot trust because you have no faith. Say, "I can

trust my Lord, and I will. Not all the powers of earth or hell shall make me doubt my glorious, faithful

Rede emer!"”

This century's greatest event, the emancipation of our slaves, is a great lesson in faith. The slaves

received their freedom by faith, just as we must receive ours. They received the good news that the

government had proclaimed their freedom. They became free the moment the Proclamation was issued.

But, they didn't truly believe it until they heard the good news. The fact had to come first. But, they

had to believe before the fact was available. The feeling would follow last of all. This is the divine

order always, and the order of common-sense as well.

I. The fact.

II. The faith.

III. The feeling.

But man reverses this order and says, I. The feeling. II. The faith. III. The fact. If the slaves had followed

man's order about their freedom, they might have stayed in slavery for a time. They should have refused

to believe it until they had felt it. I have heard of one instance where this was the case. In a remote

Southern town, a Northern lady found, two or three years after the war, some slaves who hadn't claimed

their freedom. An assertion of hers, that the North had set them free, aroused the attention of an old

colored auntie. The auntie interrupted her with an eager question.

" Oh, miss, are we free?"

“Of course, you are," the woman replied.

“Oh, are you sure?" the woman urged, with intense eagerness.

“Certainly, I am sure,” the lady replied, her voice steady and assured. “Why, is it possible you did not

know it?”

Well,” said the woman, “we heard that we were free, so we asked the master, and he said we weren’t,

so we were afraid to leave. Then we heard again that we were free, so we went to the colonel, and he

said we should stay with our old master. So, we’ve just been uncertain. Sometimes we thought we were

free, and other times we thought we weren’t. But now, miss, if you’re sure we are free, could you tell

me all about it?” Seeing that this was a real need, the lady explained everything to the poor woman.

She told her about the war, the Northern army, and Abraham Lincoln. She spoke about his

Emancipation Proclamation and the freedom it brought.

The poor slave listened with the most intense eagerness. She heard the good news. She believed it. And

when the story was ended, she walked out of the room with an air of the utmost independence, saying

as she went, -- “I’m free! I’m not staying with that old master anymore!” She had at last received her

freedom, and she had received it by faith. The government had declared her free long before. But, this

had not availed her. She had never believed in this declaration. The good news had not profited her,

not being “mixed with faith” in the one who heard it. But now she believed, and believing, she dared

to reckon herself to be free. And this, not due to any change in herself or her surroundings, nor to any

feelings of her own heart. But, because she had faith in another. He had come to her with the news of

her freedom.

Need I make the application? In a hundred messages, God has declared our freedom. He urges us to

see ourselves as free. Let your faith then lay hold of His proclamation, and assert it to be true. Declare

to yourself, to your friends, and in the secret of your soul to God, that you are free. Refuse to listen for

a moment to the lying assertions of your old master that you are still his slave. Let nothing discourage

you, no inward feelings nor outward signs. Hold your beliefs despite all opposition. I promise you,

based on the authority of our Lord, that you will see it done according to your faith.

Of all the worships we can bring our God, none is as sweet to Him as this, our utter, self-abandoning

trust. None brings Him so much glory. In every dark hour, remember this: "Now, for a time, you are in

heaviness through many temptations." It is so. "Your faith's trial is more precious than gold. Gold

perishes, even if fire tests it. May you find your faith to praise, honor, and bring glory at the appearing

of Jesus Christ."

fields.title: Chapter 7. Difficulties Concerning The Will
fields.body_html:
After initial peace, doubts may lead believers to question their faith and feel

disconnected from their emotions. The chapter emphasizes that true faith is rooted in

the will, not emotions. By surrendering their will to God, believers can overcome

emotional struggles and grow spiritually. Aligning the will with God's leads to victory,

regardless of fluctuating feelings, and encourages Christians to trust their decision to

follow God's path despite emotional turmoil.

hen a child of God, with trust, abandons himself to Christ, he may know the joy of the life hid

with Christ in God. But, a new difficulty may arise. After the initial peace and rest fade, he

feels an utter unreality in his experiences. If those feelings never came, he feels a hypocrite for

thinking they are real. He thinks his belief is shallow, a lip-service. So, it is worthless. His

surrender is not from the heart, so it cannot please God.

He fears to say he is the Lord's, for it may be untrue. Yet, he cannot deny it, as he longs for it so. The

difficulty is real and disheartening. But, it will be easily overcome. The Christian must understand the

new life and learn to live in it. People believe that "life hid with Christ in God" means to trust emotions.

So, the soul focuses on them. If they are satisfying, the soul rests. If not, it is troubled. Now, the truth

is, this life is not to be lived in emotions. It is to be lived in the will. So, the varying emotional states

do not affect life. If the will remains steadfast in its center, God's will.

W

To make this plain, I must enlarge a little. Fenelon says somewhere that “pure religion resides in the

will alone.” He means that the will is the governing power in a man's nature. If the will is set straight,

then all his nature must harmonize. By the will I do not mean the man's wish, nor his purpose. I mean

the choice, the deciding power, and the king, to which all in the man must obey. It is the man, in short,

the “Ego,” that which we feel to be ourselves. It is sometimes thought that emotions are the governing

power in our nature. But, from experience, we know there is something within us. It is behind our

emotions and wishes. It is an independent self that decides and controls everything.

Our emotions are ours. We suffer and enjoy them. But, they are not ourselves. If God is to possess us,

He must enter our central will or personality. If He reigns there by the power of His Spirit, all of our

nature must submit to Him. As the will is, so is the man. This truth is very relevant to the difficulty I

am considering. Our will often opposes our emotions. If we trust our emotions, we may feel like

hypocrites.

We would be declaring real what our will alone has decided. But if we see the will as king, we will

ignore any protest. We will accept its decisions as real, no matter how the emotions may rebel.

I know this is a tough subject. But, it is vital to the life of faith. So, I urge you, dear reader, to stick with

it until you master it. An example may help. A young man, eager to start a new life, was very smart.

But, he was a slave to a strong habit of doubting. This discouraged him. To his emotions, nothing

seemed true or real. The more he struggled, the more unreal it all became. He was told a secret about

the will. It was, if he chose to believe, to put his will on the believing side. In short, he must say, "I will

believe!" I do believe!” He need not worry about his emotions. They would, eventually, find harmony.

“What!” He said, "Do you mean I can choose to believe that, when nothing seems true to me? “Will

that belief be real?" "Yes. Your task is this: put your will on God's side in this matter of believing. If

you do this, God will take possession of it. He will work in you to will His good pleasure. Soon, you

will find that He has subdued your whole nature to Hi mself."” “Well,” was the answer, “I can do this?

I cannot control my emotions. But, I can control my will. The new life seems possible, if only my will

needs to be set straight. "I can give my will to God, and I do!" From that moment, he ignored his

emotions.

They accused him of being a hypocrite. This young man held on to his decision. He answered every

accusation with a firm belief. He chose to believe; he meant to believe; he did believe. After a few

days, he triumphed. Every emotion and thought was now captive to the mighty power of the blessed

Spirit of God. He had given his will to God.

He had held fast his faith without wavering. Yet, he felt he had no real faith to hold fast. At times, it

drained all his will to say he believed. It was so contrary to all his senses and feelings. But, he knew

his will was, after all, himself. If he kept it on God's side, he was doing all he could. Only God could

change his emotions or control his being. It has produced one of the grandest Christian lives I know. It

is a life of marvelous simplicity, directness, and power over sin. The secret lies just here. Our will, the

source of all our actions, is, in its natural state, under the control of self. But, self has been working it

in us to our ruin and misery. Now God says, "Yield yourselves to me, as those alive from the dead. I

will work in you to will and to do my good pleasure.”

The moment we yield ourselves, He takes possession of us. He works in us "that which is well pleasing

in His sight through Jesus Christ I appeal to you therefore, brothers, by the mercies of God, to present

your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable to God, which is your spiritual worship . “ Do not

be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewal of your mind, that by testing you may

discern what is the will of God, what is good and acceptable and perfect . (Rom. 12:1-2.)Let us take

another illustration. A lady, hidden with Christ, faced a great trial. Every emotion within her rebelled

against it. If she'd considered her feelings her king, she'd have been in despair. But she had learned this

secret of the will. Knowing, at her core, she chose God's will for her, she ignored her emotions.

She met every anxious thought about the trial with the words, repeated over and over, "Your will be

done!" Your will be done!” She chose to submit her will to God's. His will should be, and was, her

delight. In a very short time, every thought was subdued. She even found her emotions rejoicing in

God's will.

Again, there was a lady who had a besetting sin, which in her emotions she dearly loved, but which in

her will she hated. She believed she must control her emotions. So, she thought she couldn't conquer

them unless her emotions changed first. But she learned a secret about the will. Going to her knees, she

said, "Lord, You see that, with one part of my nature, I love this sin. But, in my true self, I hate it." And

now I put my will over on thy side in the matter. I will not do it anymore. Do you deliver me.”

Immediately, God took over the will she had surrendered to Him. He began to work in her. His will

then mastered her emotions. She found herself delivered, not by an outward command, but by an inward

power.

The Spirit of God working in her that which was well pleasing in His sight. And now, dear Christian,

let me show you how to apply this principle to your difficulties. Stop considering your emotions. They

are only servants. Your will is the real king in you. So, focus on it. Is that given up to God? Is that put

into His hands? Does your will decide to believe? Does your will choose to obey? If this is the case,

then you are in the Lord’s hands, and you decide to believe, and you choose to obey; for your will is

yourself. And the thing is done. The transaction with God is as real, where only your will acts, as when

every emotion coincides.

It does not seem as real to you; but in God’s sight it is as real. When you find this secret, you need not

attend to your emotions. Simply focus on your will. Then, all the Scripture commands become possible

to you. They include: yielding to God, being a living sacrifice, abiding in Christ, walking in the light,

and dying to self. You know your will can act and take God's side in all these. But if your emotions

had to do it, you would despair, knowing they are uncontrollable. So, when you feel unreal or

hypocritical, do not worry. It is just your emotions and not worth a moment's thought. Only ensure your

will is in God's hands. Abandon yourself to His work. Choose His side, and there leave it.

Your surging emotions, like a tossing vessel, must yield to a steady pull. This is the power of God, to

which you chose to attach yourself. Your emotions must come into captivity, and give their allegiance

to Him. You will prove true the say ing, “If any man will do His will, he shall know of the doctrine.”

The will is like a wise mother in a nursery; the feelings are like a set of clamoring, crying children. The

mother decides upon a certain course of action, which she believes to be right and best. The children

clamor against it, and declare it shall not be. But the mother, knowing she is the mistress, remains calm.

Unmoved by the children's clamors, she tries to soothe them. Eventually, the children must yield and

accept her decision.

Thus order and harmony are preserved. But if that mother thought the children were the mistresses,

chaos would reign. Such instances have been known in family life! And how many souls, at this very

moment, are confused? They are so because feelings govern, not the will! Remember, then, that your

will decides what is real. Not your emotions. It is more dangerous to be a hypocrite by trusting your

feelings than to stick to your will. If your will is on God's side, you are no hypocrite. So, claim as your

own the blessed reality of belonging to Him. Your emotions may say otherwise, but they don't matter.

I believe that, throughout the Bible, the "heart" does not mean emotions. It means the will, the man's

true self. God's goal is to have this "I" yielded to Him, and to take full control of this central life. It is

not the feelings of the man God wants, but the man himself. Have you given Him yourself, dear reader?

Have you abandoned your will to His working? Do you consent to surrender the very centre of your

being into His hands? Then, let your nature's outposts clamor as they may. You can, even now, say

with the apostle, "I am crucified with Christ; nevertheless, I live; yet not I, but Christ lives in me. And

the life which I now live in the flesh, I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me, and gave

Himself for me."

After the chapter was sent to the printer, Pasteur T. Monod of Paris gave a remarkable, practical

example of its teachings. It is a Presbyterian minister's experience. This pastor had kept it for many

years.

NEWBURGH, Sept. 26, 1842.

Dear Brother, -- I take a moment of my time, devoted to the Lord, to write a short letter to you, His

servant. It is sweet to feel we are wholly the Lord’s, that He has received us and called us His. Th is is

religion. It is a giving up of self-ownership. It is a full embrace of the idea, "I am not my own, I am

bought with a price." Since I last saw you, I have been pressing on. Yet, there is nothing remarkable in

my experience to share. I do not know if it is best to seek remarkable things. But I strive to be holy, as

God is holy, pressing on toward the prize.

I do not feel qualified to instruct you; I can only tell you the way in which I was led. The Lord deals

differently with each soul. We should not copy others' experiences. But those seeking a clean heart

must attend to certain things. We must personally consecrate all to God. We must make a covenant

with Him to be wholly and forever His. I made this, using only my mind. My heart is hard and dark,

full of sin and disbelief. I feel nothing. I covenanted to be the Lord’s, and laid all upon the altar, a living

sacrifice, to the best of my ability. And after I rose from my knees, I was conscious of no change in my

feeling.

I was painfully conscious that there was no change. But I was sure I did. With all my sincerity, I made

an eternal, complete dedication of myself to God. I did not consider the work done by any means. But,

I engaged to be a living, perpetual sacrifice, wholly devoted to God. And now came the effort to do

this. I knew that I must believe that God did accept me, and had come in to dwell in my heart. I was

conscious that I did not believe this, and yet I desired to do so. I read with much prayer John’s First

Epistle, and endeavored to assure my heart of God’s love to me as an individual. I was sensible that

my heart was full of evil.

I seemed to have no power to overcome pride or to repel evil thoughts, which I abhorred. But Christ

was manifested to destroy the devil's works. The sin in my heart was the devil's work. I was enabled,

therefore, to believe that God was working in me. He was to will and to do, while I worked out my

own salvation with fear and trembling.

I was convinced of unbelief, that it was voluntary and criminal. I clearly saw that unbelief was an awful

sin; it made the faithful God a liar. The Lord showed me my besetting sins. They had dominion over

me. They were, especially, preaching myself instead of Christ. I also indulged in complacent thoughts

after preaching. I was enabled to make myself of no reputation, and to seek the honor which cometh

from God only. Satan struggled hard to beat me back from the Rock of Ages.

But thanks to God, I found a way to live in the moment. Then, I found rest.

I trusted in the blood of Jesus as a full atonement for my past sins. I committed my future to the Lord,

agreeing to do His will as He revealed it. I saw that I had to look to Jesus for grace. I had to trust Him

to cleanse my heart and keep me from sin now. I felt a need to depend on the grace of Christ, if only

for a moment. I would not let the enemy trouble me about the past or future. I expected, each moment,

a supply for that moment. I agreed to be a child of Abraham. I would walk by faith in the Word of God,

not by my feelings. I would seek to be a Bible Christian. Since that time the Lord has given me a steady

victory over sins which before enslaved me.

I delight in the Lord, and in His Word. I delight in my work as a minister: my fellowship is with the

Father and with His Son, Jesus Christ. I am a baby in Christ; I know my progress has been small

compared with that made by many. My feelings vary. But when I feel, I praise God and trust His word.

When I'm empty and feel nothing, I do the same. I have covenanted to walk by faith and not by feelings.

The Lord is beginning to revive His work among my people. “Praise the Lord.” May the Lord fill you

with all His fullness and give you all the mind of Christ. Oh, be faithful! Walk before God and be

perfect. Preach the Word. Be instant in season and out of season. The Lord loves you. He works with

you. Rest your soul completely upon that promise, “Look, I am with you always, even unto the end of

the world.”

Your fellow soldier,

WILLIAM HILL

There may be some who will object to this teaching, that it ignores the work of the blessed Holy Spirit.

But I must refer such to the introductory chapter of this book, in which I have fully explained myself.

I am not writing upon that side of the subject; I am considering man ’s part in the matter, and not the

part of the Spirit. I know that all a man can do would be useless if the Holy Spirit did not work in him

continually. I write as I do because I believe in the Spirit. It is a mighty, ever-present power, ready to

do his work. But, like the wind that blows where it wants, you hear its sound. But you cannot tell where

it comes from or where it goes. The Spirit's actions are beyond our control and understanding.

The results we know, and the steps on our part which lead to those results, but we know nothing more.

And yet, like a factory worker, we dare to urge men to act. They must, like the worker, trust an unseen

power, called steam, behind their machinery. It can accomplish the impossible. We know the mighty

Spirit will always provide the power needed for each moment's act. We boldly claim that we, as writers,

can say, as earnestly as any other Christians, "We believe in the Holy Ghost."

fields.title: Chapter 8. Is God In Everything?
fields.body_html:
Recognizing God's presence in all aspects of life, including human actions and trials,

is essential. Everything, even suffering caused by others, is part of God's plan and

must be accepted as His will. By trusting in His sovereignty, believers can face

difficulties with peace, knowing that God oversees all and uses even challenges for

spiritual growth and triumph.

major obstacle to living a life of total surrender is the difficulty of seeing God in everything.

People say, "I can submit to things from God. But, I cannot submit to man. "Most of my trials

come through humans." Or, "It's fine to talk of trusting. But, when I commit a matter to God,

man is sure to come in and mess it up. I can trust God, but I see serious problems with trusting

men."”

This is no imaginary trouble. It is of vital importance. If it cannot be met, it makes faith an impossible,

visionary theory. Nearly everything in life comes to us through human means. Most of our trials result

from someone's failure, ignorance, carelessness, or sin. We know God cannot be the author of these

things. Yet, unless He is the agent, how can we say to Him, "Your will be done"? Besides, what good

is it to trust our affairs to God, if man can come in and disrupt them? And, how can we live by faith if

we can't trust humans? They will have too much influence on our lives.

Moreover, things in which we can see God’s hand always have a sweetness in them which consoles

while it wounds. But, man's trials are full of bitterness. So, we must see God in everything. We must

accept all things as His direct gifts, with no second causes. We must be brought to this. Only then can

we know a lasting experience of total abandonment and perfect trust. Our abandonment must be to

God, not to man, and our trust must be in Him, not in any arm of flesh, or we shall fail at the first trial.

A

The question is, "Is God in everything? “Do we have scripture to accept everything from Him? It was

caused by other factors."" I answer, unhesitatingly, yes. To the children of God, all comes from their

Fath er's hand. It matters not who the apparent agents were. There are no “second causes” for them. The

whole teaching of the Bible asserts and implies this. “Not a sparrow falls to the ground without our

Father.” The very hairs of our head are all numbered. We are not to be careful about anything, because

our Father cares for us. We are not to avenge ourselves, because our Father has charged Himself with

our defence.

We are not to fear, for the Lord is on our side. No one can be against us, because He is for us. We shall

not want, for He is our Shepherd. When we pass through the rivers, they shall not overflow us. When

we walk through the fire, we shall not be burned. He will be with us. He shuts the mouths of lions, that

they cannot hurt us. He delivers and rescues. He changes the times and the seasons; He removes kings

and sets up kings. A man’s heart is in His hand, and, as the river of water, He turns it whithersoever

He will.” "He rules over all the heathen kingdoms. In His hand is power and might. None can withstand

Him."

He rules the raging of the sea; when the waves thereof arise, He stills them. He brings the advice of the

unruly to mischief; He makes the devices of the people of no effect. Whatsoever the Lord pleases that

does Him in heaven, and in earth, in the seas, and all deep places. If you see the poor oppressed and

justice perverted, don't marvel. For there is one higher than the highest. He sees all. These are a part of

His ways, but how little a portion is heard of Him? But the thunder of His power, who can understand?”

"Have you not known, have you not heard? The everlasting God, the Lord, the Creator of the ends of

the earth, does not grow faint or weary. There is no searching of His understanding.

And this God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble. Therefore we will not fear. The

earth may be removed. The mountains may be carried into the sea. The waters may roar and be troubled.

The mountains may shake with their swelling. I will say of the Lord, He is my refuge and my fortress,

my God, in Him will I trust. Surely He shall deliver thee from the snare of the fowler, and from the

noise of some pestilence. He shall cover me with His feathers, and under His wings shall I trust. His
