tempted. But it's really an embarrassment . We are ashamed because we secretly congratulated

ourselves. We believed our tastes were too pure and our separation from the world too complete for

such things to tempt us. We expected something from ourselves. We are disappointed to find it lacking.

As a result, we are discouraged. This embarrassment and discouragement are worse than the

temptation. They seem humble, but they only stem from wounded self-love.

True humility can bear to see its own weakness and foolishness revealed. It never expected anything

from itself. It knows its only hope must be in God. So, instead of discouraging the soul from trusting,

it drives it to a deeper and more utter trust. But counterfeit humility, born of self, plunges the soul into

despair. It drives it into the very sin it so despises. I remember once hearing an allegory that illustrated

this to me wonderfully. Satan called together a council of his servants to consult how they might make

a good man sin. One evil spirit started up and said, “I will make him sin.” “How will you do it?” asked

Satan. “I will set before him the pleasures of sin,” was the reply; “I will tell him of its delights and the

ri ch rewards it brings.” “Ah,” said Satan, “that will not do; he has tried, it, and knows better than that.”

Then another spirit started up and said, “I will make him sin.”

“What will you do?” asked Satan. “I will tell him of the pains and sorrows of v irtue. I will show him

that virtue has no delights, and brings no rewards.” “Ah, no!” exclaimed Satan, “That will not do at all.

He has tried it. He knows, 'wisdom's ways are pleasant, and her paths are peace.' Another said, I will

make him sin. And what will you do? Asked Satan, again. I will discourage his soul, was the short

reply. Ah, that will do,” cried Satan, “that will do! We shall conquer him now.” And they did. An old

writer says, all discouragement is from the devil. I wish every Christian would remember this and keep

it as a pocket-piece. We must fly from discouragement as we would from sin. But this is impossible if

we fail to recognize the true agency in temptation. For if the temptations are our own fault, we cannot

help being discouraged. But they are not.

The Bible says, “Blessed is the man who remains steadfast under trial, for when he has stood the test

he will receive the crown of life, which God has promised to those who love him. ”(James 1:12) It urges

us to "count it all joy when we fall into diverse temptations." Temptation, therefore, cannot be sin. It is

no more a sin to hear evil whispers in our souls than to hear the swearing of bad men as we pass along

the street. The sin only comes in either case by our stopping and joining in with them. If, when the

wicked thoughts come, we turn from them at once, as we would from wicked talk, and ignore them,

we do not sin. But if we carry them on in our minds, and roll them under our tongues, and dwell on

them with a half consent of our will to them as true, then we sin.

We may be enticed by evil a thousand times a day without sin, and we cannot help these enticing. But

if the enemy can make us think his temptations are our sin, he will have won half the battle. He will

then likely win completely.

A dear lady once came to me under great darkness, simply from not understanding this. She had been

very happy in her faith for some time. She had been free from temptation, and thought she would never

be tempted again. But suddenly a very peculiar form of temptation had assailed her, which had horrified

her. She found that the moment she began to pray, dreadful thoughts of all kinds would rush into her

mind. She had lived a very sheltered, innocent life. These thoughts seemed so awful to her, that she felt

she must be one of the wicked of sinners to have them. She began by thinking she could not have

entered into the rest of faith. She ended by concluding that she had never been born again.

Her soul was in an agony of distress.

I told her that these dreadful thoughts were the enemy's doing. He came to her the moment she kneeled

in prayer and filled her mind with them. She was not to blame for them at all. She could not help them

any more than she could help hearing a wicked man blaspheme in her presence. I urged her to see them

as from the enemy. She should not blame or discourage herself. Instead, she should turn to Jesus and

commit them to Him. I showed her how much the enemy had gained. They made her think these

thoughts were her own. This condemned and discouraged her. I assured her she would win quickly if

she ignored them. She should turn her back on them and look to the Lord.

She grasped the truth, and the next time these thoughts came she said to the enemy, “I have found you

out now. It is you who are suggesting these dreadful thoughts to me, and I hate them, and will have

nothing to do with them. The Lord is my Saviour; take them to Him, and settle them in His presence.”

The baffled enemy, found out, fled in confusion. Her soul was perfectly delivered.

Another thing also. The enemy knows that if a Christian sees a hint of evil as his, he will reject it. He

will do so more quickly than if it seems to be his own mind's suggestion. If Satan began each temptation

with, "I am Satan, your enemy; I have come to make you sin," we would likely resist. He has to hide

himself in order to make his baits attractive. Our victory will be easier if we are not ignorant of his

tricks. We must recognize him at his first approach. We also make a mistake about temptations. We

think that all time spent fighting them is wasted. Hours pass, and we seem to have made no progress,

because we have been so beset with temptations. But, we may have served God more truly during these

hours than in our freer times, when we faced fewer temptations.

Temptation is really more the devil’s wrath against God, than against us. He cannot touch our Saviour.

But, he can wound Him by conquering us. Our ruin matters to him only as it does this. So, we fight our

Lord's battles when we resist temptation. In these cases, an hour is worth a day's time. We read,

“Blessed is the man who remains steadfast under trial, for when he has stood the test he will receive

the crown of life, which God has promised to those who love him ."(James 1:12).I am sure this means

to endure its continuance and frequent recurrence.

Nothing cultivates the grace of patience like enduring temptation. And, nothing drives the soul to

depend on the Lord Jesus like it. And finally, nothing brings more glory to our Lord than the trial of

our faith, which comes through many temptations. It is said to be more precious than gold, though

tested by fire. We, who endure the trial, shall receive a reward. It is "the crown of life" which the Lord

has promised to those who love Him.”

We cannot wonder at the Holy Ghost's urging at the start of the Book of James: " Count it all joy, my

brothers, when you meet trials of various kinds, for you know that the testing of your faith produces

steadfastness. And let steadfastness have its full effect, that you may be perfect and complete, lacking

in nothing. ”(James 1:2)Temptation is God's tool to complete our perfection. So, the enemy's own

weapons are turned against him. We see that all things, even temptations, can work for good to them

that love God.

To resist temptations, I don’t need to tell my audience: it is by faith. For this is, of course, the foundation

upon which the whole interior life rests. Our one great motto is throughout, “We are nothing, and Christ

is all.” A nd always and everywhere we have started to stand, and walk, and overcome, and live by

faith. We have found our own helplessness. We cannot help ourselves. Our only way, therefore, is to

hand the temptation over to our Lord and trust Him to conquer it for us.

But when we put it into His hands, we must leave it there. We must commit to Him for victory as we

did for salvation. He must do all for us in the one case, as completely as in the other. It was faith only

then, and it must be faith only now.

The Lord works miracles in conquering the temptations of those who trust Him. Thousands can testify

to this. But I cannot expand on this now. I aimed to show temptation in its true light, not to detail the

way to overcome it. I want to free good, faithful souls from bondage. They will be trapped if they

confuse temptation with sin. They must understand temptation's true nature and use. I want them to

know that temptations are vital for our souls' growth. Whatever their source, God uses them to build in

us graces of character that would otherwise be missing.

Wherever temptation is, there is God also, superintending and controlling its power. “Where were you,

Lord I, while I was being tempted?” cried the saint of the desert. "Close beside you, my son, all the

while," was the tender reply. Temptations try us. We are worth nothing if we are not tried. They develop

our spiritual strength and courage and knowledge, and our development is the one thing God cries for.

How shallow would all our spirituality be if it were not for temptations? "Blessed is the man who

endures temptation. He will receive the crown of life, which the Lord has promised to those who love

Him." This "crown of life" will be worth all the trials and endurance it costs to obtain it; without those,

it could not be attained.

A sick woman once bought a cocoon . It held a very beautiful butterfly with magnificent wings. She

hoped to see it emerge from the cocoon in her chamber. She watched it eagerly as spring drew on.

Finally, she was delighted to see the butterfly beginning to emerge. But it seemed to have great

difficulty. It pushed, and strained, and struggled. It made so little headway that she concluded it must

need help. With a pair of delicate scissors, she clipped the tight cord that bound the cocoon's opening.

Immediately the cocoon opened wide, and the butterfly escaped without any further struggle. She

congratulated herself on her experiment's success. But, something was wrong with the butterfly.

It was all out of the cocoon, it's true. But, its great wings were lifeless and colorless. They dragged

behind it, a useless burden. For a few days it lived a miserable sickly life, and then died, without having

once lifted its powerless wings. The lady was sorely disappointed and could not understand it. But

when she related the circumstance to a naturalist, he told her that it had all been her own fault. That it

took just that pushing and struggling to send the life fluid into the wings' veins. Her misguided kindness

in shortening the struggle had left the wings lifeless and colorless.

So, our spiritual wings need the struggle of resisting temptation. To save us from it would weaken our

souls' power to "mount up with wings as eagles." It would also deny us the "crown of life" promised to

those who endure.

fields.title: Chapter 13. Failures
fields.body_html:
Failures in the Christian life are inevitable but should not lead to despair. When we

sin, immediate confession and trust in God’s forgiveness restore our fellowship with

Him. Hidden sin can cause spiritual defeat, and we must deal with it honestly. Failures

should drive us closer to God, not away, and through His grace, we continue walking

in holiness.

he very title of this chapter may startle some. “Failures,” they will say; “we thought t here were no

failures in this life of faith!” To this I would answer that there ought not to be, and need not be;

but, as a fact, there sometimes are. And we have got to deal with facts, and not with theories. No

teacher of this inner life says we can't sin. They only insist that we don't have to. A chance for

constant victory is now possible. Few deny that, at times, they have given in to temptation.

Of course, in speaking of sin here, I mean conscious, known sin. I do not touch on the sins of ignorance.

Nor do I discuss the so-called inevitable sin of our nature. Both are covered by the atonement and do

not disturb our fellowship with God. I have no desire or ability to discuss the doctrines of sin. I will

leave that to the theologians. I will speak only of the believer's experience. I want it to be clear that I

will refer only to what is within our consciousness. Misunderstanding, then, on this point of known sin,

is dangerous to the higher Christian life. A believer, who trusts he is on the highway of holiness, may

be surprised into sin. He is then tempted to either give up, or to hide his sin. To preserve doctrine, he

may call it an "infirmity" and refuse to be honest.

T

Either of these courses is equally fatal to any real growth and progress in the life of holiness. We must

face the sad truth. We must name it and find, if we can, its cause and cure. This life of union with God

requires the utmost honesty with Him and with ourselves. The sin would only momentarily disturb the

communion. But, any dishonesty with it would surely destroy it. A sudden failure is no reason for being

discouraged and giving up all as lost. Neither is the integrity of our doctrine touched by it. We are not

preaching a state, but a walk. The highway of holiness is not a place, but a way. Sanctification is not a

thing to be gained at a certain stage of our experience and forever possessed. It is a life to be lived day

by day and hour by hour.

We may briefly stray from a path. But our wandering does not erase it. We can quickly return. In this

life of faith, we may fail at times. These failures are sad and to be deplored. But, if met rightly, they

need not disturb our complete trust in God. They should not interrupt our happy communion with Him

for long.

The great point is an instant return to God. Our sin is no reason for ceasing to trust, but only an

unanswerable argument why we must trust more fully than ever. No matter the cause of our failure,

discouragement won't help. A child learning to walk might despair after a fall. He might refuse to try

again. A believer, learning to live by faith, must not give up for having sinned. The only way in both

cases is to get right up and try again. After a disastrous defeat.

“Then Joshua tore his clothes and fell to the earth on his face before the ark of the Lord until the

evening, he and the elders of Israel. And they put dust on their heads. And Joshua said, "Alas, O Lord

God, why have you brought this people over the Jordan at all, to give us into the hand of the Amorites,

to destroy us? Would that we had been content to dwell beyond the Jordan! O Lord, what can I say

when Israel has turned their backs before their enemies? For the Canaanites and all the inhabitants of

the land will hear of it and will surround us and cut off our name from the earth. And what will you do

for your great name?"(Joshua 7:6-9)

What a wail of despair this was! And how it is repeated by many a child of God today. Their hearts

melt, like water, because of a defeat. They cry, “And Joshua said, 'Alas, Lord G OD , why have you

brought this people over the Jordan at all — to deliver us into the hand of the Amorites, to destroy us?

Oh, that we had been content, and dwelt on the other side of the Jordan !" They predict further failures

and even defeat by their enemies. No doubt, Joshua thought, as we now do. After such a failure,

discouragement and despair seemed the only safe response. But God thought otherwise. " So the L ORD

said to Joshua: “Get up! Why do you lie thus on your face? " They should not surrender to despair,

however humble it might seem. They must face the evil and get rid of it. They must "sanctify

themselves" at once.”

“Up, sanctify the people,” is always God’s command. “Lie down and be discouraged” is always the

enemy’s temptation. We feel it is presumptuous, even impertinent, to go at once to the Lord after having

sinned against Him. We should suffer our sins' consequences for a while and endure our guilty

consciences. We can hardly believe the Lord would want to welcome us back into His loving

fellowship. A little girl once expressed the feeling to me, with a child's honest straightforwardness. She

asked if the Lord Jesus always forgave our sins if we asked Him. I said, "Yes, of course He does."”

“Just as soon” she repeated, doubtingly. “Yes,” I replied, “the very minute we ask, He forgives us.”

“Well,” she said deliberately, “I cannot believe that. I should think He would make us feel sorry for

two or three days first. And then I should think He would make us ask Him a great many times, and in

a very pretty way too, not just in common talk. I believe that is how He does. You need not try to make

me think He forgives me at once, no matter what the Bible says.”

She only said what most Christians think. Worse, most act on it. Their remorse now separates them

from God more than their sin would.

It is so contrary to how we want our children to act, that I wonder how we could have conceived such

an idea of God. A mother grieves when her naughty child goes off alone in despair. She doubts her

willingness to forgive. But, her heart welcomes the darling who runs to her and begs forgiveness!

Surely, our God knew this love when He said, “ Return, O faithless sons; I will heal your faithlessness.

Behold, we come to you, for you are the Lord our Go d.”(Jeremiah3:22)

The same moment that reveals sin, should reveal forgiveness. This is vital for a steadfast walk on the

holy path. Here, we cannot tolerate an instant of separation from God. We can only walk this path by

looking to Jesus, moment by moment. If we take our eyes off Him to see our sin and weakness, we will

leave the path at once. The believer, who trusts he is on this path, must flee to the Lord if sin overcomes

him. He must act on ( 1 John 1:9) “If we confess our sins, He is faithful and j ust to forgive us our sins,

and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.” He must not hide his sin and seek to salve it over with

excuses, or to push it out of his memory by the lapse of time. But he must do as the children of Israel

did. He must rise up "early in the morning," and "run" to where the evil thing is hidden. Then, he must

take it from its hiding place and lay it "out before the Lord.”

He must confess his sin. Then he must stone it, burn it, and put it away. Then, he must raise a great

heap of stones to hide it forever. He must, then and there, believe that God is. He must believe,

according to His word, that God is faithful and just to forgive him his sin, and that He does do it. He

must also believe that God cleanses him from all unrighteousness. He must, by faith, claim an

immediate forgiveness and cleansing. Then, he must trust more than ever.

Once Israel's sin was uncovered and removed, God's word came. It was a message of great

encouragement: " And the LORD said to Joshua, “Do not fear and do not be dismayed. Take all the

fighting men with you, and arise, go up to Ai. See, I have given into your hand the king of Ai, and his

people, his city, and his land. ”(Joshua 8:1) Our courage must rise higher than ever. We must trust the

Lord more. Then, His mighty power can work in us to fulfill His will. Moreover, we must forget our

sin as soon as it is thus confessed and forgiven. We must not dwell on it, and examine it, and indulge

in a luxury of distress and remorse. We must not idolize it, then walk around and view it. That would

make it a mountain that hides our God from us. We must follow Paul's example. We must "forgetting

those things which are behind, and reaching forth unto those things which are before." Then, we must

"press toward the ma rk for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus."”

I would like to bring up two contrastive illustrations of these things. One was an earnest Christian. He

was an active church worker. For several months, he had enjoyed full salvation. He was suddenly

overcome by a temptation to treat a brother unkindly. He thought it impossible to sin again. So, he was

deeply discouraged. He concluded he was wrong. He had never truly trusted. His discouragement grew

into despair. He concluded he had never been born again, and gave himself up for lost. He spent three

years in misery. He drifted further from God and fell into one sin after another. His life became a curse

to himself and to those around him.

His health failed under the terrible burden. Fears arose for his reason. At the end of three years, he met

a Christian lady, who understood the truth about sin that I had been trying to explain. After a brief chat,

she learned his trouble. She said, "You sinned in that act, no doubt. Don't try to excuse it."

But have you never confessed it to the Lord and asked Him to forgive you?” “Confessed it!” He

exclaimed, "I have done nothing but confess it. I have begged God to forgive me for these three dreadful

years." “And you have never believed He did forgive you?” asked the lady. “No,” said the poor man,

“how could I, for I never felt as if He did?” “But suppose He had said He forgave you, would not that

have done as well as for you to feel it?”

“Oh, yes,” replied the man, “if God said it, of course I would believe it.” “Very well, He does say so,”

was the lady’s answer, and she turned to the verse we have taken above. “If we confess our sins, he is

faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness . ”(1 John 1:9) and read

it aloud. "Now," she continued, "for three years you've confessed your sin. All the while, God's record

has declared He is faithful and just to forgive and cleanse you. Yet, you have never once believed it."

You have been ‘making God a liar’ all this while by refusing to believe His record.”

The poor man saw the whole thing. He was dumbfounded and alarmed. When the lady suggested they

kneel, he obeyed like one in a maze. She wanted him to confess his past sins and claim, then and there,

forgiveness and cleansing. But the result was glorious. In a few moments, the light broke in, and he

burst out into praise at the wonderful deliverance. In three minutes, his soul, by faith, traversed the

long, weary journey of three years. He found himself resting in Jesus, rejoicing in His full salvation.

The other illustration was of a Christian lady. She had been in salvation for about two weeks. She had

a bright, victorious experience. Suddenly, at the end of that time, she was overcome by a violent burst

of anger. For a moment, a flood of discouragement swept over her soul. The enemy said, “There, now,

that shows it was all a mistake. Of course, you have been deceived about the whole thing, and have

never entered into the life of full trust at all.

You might as well give up. You can't consecrate or trust yourself more than you did this time. So, it is

plain this life of holiness is not for you!” These thoughts flashed through her mind in a moment. But

she was well-taught in God's ways. So, she said, "Yes, I have sinned, and it is very sad." But the Bible

says that if we confess our sins, God will forgive us. He is faithful and just. He will also cleanse us

from all unrighteousness. I believe He will do it.” She did not delay. Still boiling with anger, she ran,

not walked, into a room to be alone. Kneeling by the bed, she said, "Lord, I confess my sin." I have

sinned, I am even at this very moment sinning.

I hate it, but I cannot get rid of it. I confess it with shame and confusion of face to God. And now I

believe that, according to your word, you do forgive and you do cleanse.” She said it out loud, for the

inward turmoil was too great for it to be said inside. As the words “You do forgive and you do cleanse”

passed her lips, the deliverance came. The Lord said, “ And he awoke and rebuked the wind and said to

the sea , ' Peace! Be still!” And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm ,” ( Mark 4:39) and there was

a great calm. A flood of light and joy burst on her soul, the enemy fled, and she was more than a

conqueror through Him that loved her. It had taken only five minutes, the sin and its cure. Now, her

feet trod more firmly than ever on the blessed highway of holiness. So, the valley of anchor became a

door of hope. She sang her song of deliverance, with deeper m eaning: “Then Moses and the people of

Israel sang this song to the LORD, saying, 'I will sing to the LORD, for he has triumphed gloriously;

the horse and his rider he has thrown into the sea” (Exodus 15:1 )

In every crisis, the only remedy is to trust in the Lord. If this is all we can do, is it not better to do it at

once? I have often been brought up short by the question, “Well, what can I do but trust?” I realized at

once the folly of seeking deliverance any other way. I thought, "I will have to trus t in the end. “Then,

why not do it now?" We have entered a life of faith. If we fail, our only recovery must be an increase

in faith, not a decrease.

Let every failure, if any occur, drive you to the Lord. Abandon yourself to Him and trust Him

completely. Though sad, these failures won't end your rest or your sweet communion with Him. I have

shown the way to escape failure. Now, I want to discuss the causes of failure in this life of full salvation.

The causes do not lie in the strength of the temptation, our own weakness, or, above all, any lack in our

Saviour's power or will to save us. The promise to Israel was positive, “ No man shall be able to stand

before you all the days of your life. Just as I was with Moses, so I will be with you. I will not leave you

or forsake you. ” (Joshua1:5). And the promise to us is equally positive, " No temptation has overtaken

you that is not common to man. God is faithful, and he will not let you be tempted beyond your ability,

but with the temptation he will also provide a way of escape, that you may be able to endure it.” 1

Corinthians 10:13)

So about three thousand men went up there from the people. And they fled before the men of Ai It was

not the strength of their enemy, neither had God failed them. Their defeat had another cause, which the

Lord declares: "Israel hath sinned. They have also transgressed my covenant which I commanded them.

They have taken of the accursed thing. They have also stolen and dissembled, and put it among their

own stuff."

"So, the children of Israel could not stand before their enemies. They turned their backs upon their

enemies."” It was a hidden evil that conquered them. Deep beneath the earth, in a tent in that vast army,

was something against which God had a controversy.

This hid den thing made the whole army helpless before their enemies. “Israel, there is something wrong

among you . You cannot stand before your enemies until you remove it."”

The teaching is this: Any hidden evil in our hearts, no matter how small, will cause us to fall before our

enemies. Any cherished bitterness, harsh judgments, or slackness in obeying the Lord will cripple our

spiritual life. So will any doubtful habits or surroundings. We may have hidden the evil in our hearts.

We may have covered it up, refusing to see it. But, we are secretly aware of it.

We may ignore it and declare our full trust. We may be more earnest in our religious duties. We may

see more truth and beauty in the life of faith. We may seem to have won, both to ourselves and others.

Yet, we may suffer bitter defeats. We may wonder, question, despair, and pray. But, nothing will help

until the accursed thing is dug up, brought to light, and laid before God. If a believer living an inner

life is defeated, he must seek the cause. It is not the enemy's strength. It is a hidden lack of dedication

at his core.

A headache is not a disease, but a symptom of one. It is in some other part of the body. So, in a Christian,

sin is only a symptom. It reveals an evil that likely exists in another part of his being.

Sometimes, one may hide evil even in what, at a cursory glance, looks like good. Hidden behind a

strong desire for the truth, there may be a tendency to judge or favor our own opinions . Clear Christian

faithfulness may hide an absence of Christian love. Beneath a seemingly rightful care for our affairs,

we may hide a great want of trust in God. Our blessed Guide, the indwelling Holy Spirit, is. He secretly

discovers these things to us. He does so through little twinges and pangs of conscience. So, we are left

without excuse. It is easy to ignore His gentle voice. We convince ourselves that all is well. This will

hide a fatal evil among us, causing unexpected defeats.

A capital illustration of this occurred to me once in my housekeeping. I moved into a new house. In

checking it for readiness, I found a very clean cider cask in the cellar. It was headed up at both ends. I

debated whether to take it from the cellar and open it. It seemed empty and looked nice. So, I decided

to leave it, as it would have been a lot of work to get it up the stairs. I didn't feel completely comfortable,

but I pushed aside my doubts and left it. Every spring and fall, during house-cleaning time, I would

remember that cask. A twinge of my housewifely conscience nagged at me. I could not rest in a

perfectly cleaned house while it remained unopened. For how did I know it did not hide some evil

beneath its fair exterior?

Still, I eased my doubts. I feared the trouble of investigating it. For two or three years, the harmless-

looking barrel sat in my basement. Then, most unaccountably, moths began to fill my house. I used

every possible precaution against them and made every effort to eradicate them, but in vain. They

increased rapidly and threatened to ruin everything I had.

I suspected my carpets were the cause, and subjected them to a thorough cleaning. I suspected

something was wrong with my furniture, so I had it redone. I suspected all sorts of impossible things.

At last, the thought of the cask flashed on me. I had it brought up from the cellar, and the head knocked

in.

I think it's safe to say that thousands of moths poured out. The previous occupant must have left

something that bred moths. This was the cause of all my trouble.

I now believe that some habit or indulgence, some safe, minor thing, causes us little twinges of

conscience. It's not been fairly examined under God's searching eye. I think it lies at the root of most

failures in this higher life. All is not given up. Some secret corner is kept locked against the entrance

of the Lord. And therefore, we cannot stand before our enemies, but find ourselves smitten down in

their presence.

To prevent failure, or to find its cause if we do, we must keep this prayer before us: "Search me, O

God, and know my heart; try me and know my thoughts; and see if there be any evil way in me, and

lead me in the way everlasting.""

There may be something very deceptive in our sufferings over our failures. We may think we are

focused on God's glory. Yet, our souls may be troubled by self alone. We are not as saintly as we

thought. This discovery hurts our self-love. Our frustration can be a bigger mistake than the original

wrongdoing. The only safe way to treat our failures is to avoid justifying or condemning ourselves.

We should, instead, lay them quietly before the Lord. We should look at them in peace and with love.

The old mystic writers say that a simple, peaceful turning to God helps us more than regretting our

straying from Him. "Only be faithful," they say. "Turn only to Him, the moment you see your sin. His

presence will free you from the snares that have trapped you." To look at self-plunges you deeper into

the slough, for this very slough is after all nothing but self; while a simple look towards God can calm

and comfort your heart.

Finally, let us never forget, no matter our failures. The Lord Jesus is able, as declared, to save us from

our enemies. Then, we may "That we, being delivered from the hand of our enemies, might serve him

without fear, in holiness and righteousness before him all our days."(Luke1:74-75). Let us pray, each

of us, day and night: " Keep back your servant also from presumptuous sins; let them not have dominion

over me .”(Psalm19:13). “ But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you, and you will

be my witnesses in Jerusalem and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the end of the earth.”(Acts 1:8). We must be

so pliable in His hands, and trust Him. Then He will “ Equip you with everything good that you may

do his will, working in us that which is pleasing in his sight, through

Jesus Christ, to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen.” (Hebrews 13:21)

fields.title: Chapter 14. Doubts
fields.body_html:
Christians often struggle with doubts that hinder their faith. Doubt is seen as a sinful

habit that must be rejected, just like other temptations. Overcoming it requires fully

surrendering to God, trusting in His promises, and refusing to entertain doubts. A life

of continuous trust in God’s love and faithfulness is essential.

great number of Christians are slaves to the habit of doubting. No drunkard was ever more

completely bound by the chains of his fatal habit than they are by those chains. Their whole

Christian life is a constant battle. An army of doubts lies in wait to attack at any chance. Their

lives are wretched. Their doubts hinder their usefulness and break their communion with God.

The soul's entry into the life of faith, which this book discusses, often banishes doubts. But, they

sometimes resurge. They can cause stumbling and despair. They can't fully turn the believer back to

the dreary wilderness.

We all remember, doubtless, the childish mix of fascination and horror in that story. It was about

Christian's imprisonment in Doubting Castle by the wicked giant Despair. We felt extremely happy in

his escape from those massive gates and that cruel tyrant. We did not suspect then that we would be

imprisoned by the same giant, in the same castle. And yet I fear to every member of the Church of

Christ there has been at least one such experience. If it's not fresh in your minds, please read the account

again. You may find there experiences of your own. They were very hard to bear and sorrowful to

remember.

It's strange that people called Believers must confess such doubts. Their name suggests their only trait

is belief. It is such a universal habit that, if the Church were renamed, "Doubters" would be the only

fitting name. Most Christians have accepted their doubts. They see them as a painful, inevitable illness.

They must resign themselves to it as part of life's discipline. They complain about their doubts as a man

might complain about his aches and pains. They want to be seen as an "interesting case" of rare trial,

needing deep sympathy and great care.

A

This is often true of believers. They long to live by faith and have taken many steps towards it. They

may have lost their old doubts. They once tormented them. They wondered if their sins were forgiven

and if they'd reach Heaven. But, they still doubt. They have simply shifted the habit to a higher

platform. They are saying, perhaps, “Yes, I believe my sins are forgiven, and I am a child of God

through faith in Jesus Christ. I dare not doubt this anymore.

But then, and this "but then" includes doubts about every promise our Father has made to His children.

They fight with them, refusing to believe until they have better proof of their truth than God's word.

They wonder why they can walk in such darkness. They see themselves as martyrs. They groan under

the unique spiritual conflicts they must endure. Spiritual conflicts! Far better would they be named did

we call them spiritual rebellions! Our fight is to be a fight of faith, and the moment we doubt, our fight

ceases and our rebellion begins.

I desire to put forth, if possible, one vigorous protest against this whole thing. I might as well join in

with a drunkard's complaints. I might as well pray with him for grace to endure his fatal indulgence. It

is as foolish as to console the enslaved souls with their weak complaints. I can do nothing else but

proclaim to them the perfect deliverance the Lord Jesus Christ has for them. I implore, entreat, and

command them, with all my being, to accept it and be free. Not for one moment would I listen to their

despairing excuses. You ought to be free, you can be free, and you must be free!

Will you undertake to tell me that it is an inevitable necessity for God to be doubted by His children?

Is it an inevitable necessity for your children to doubt you? Would you tolerate their doubts a single

hour? Would you pity your son if he said, "Father, I cannot believe your word, I cannot trust your

love"? Would you find him an interesting case? I remember once seeing the indignation of a mother I

knew, stirred to its very depths by a little doubting on the part of one of her children. She had brought

two little girls to my house to leave them while she did some errands. One of them, with a child's happy

confidence, abandoned herself to my nursery. She found all the pleasures there. She sang and played

until her mother returned.

The other one, with unfortunate caution of maturity, sat alone in a corner. She wondered if her mother

would remember to come back for her. She feared being forgotten. She imagined her mother would be

glad to get rid of her, since she was a naughty girl. In the end, she worked herself into a perfect frenzy

of despair. I shall not easily forget the look on that mother's face. It was after her weeping little girl

returned and told her what the matter was. Grief, wounded love, indignation, and pity, all strove

together for mastery. But indignation gained the day, and I doubt if that little girl was ever so vigorously

dealt with before. That scene has come before me a hundred times since. It has taught me deeply. It has

compelled me to refuse doubts about my Heavenly Father's love. Those doubts have clamored at my

heart's door for entrance.

I am convinced that, for many, doubting is a luxury. To deny themselves that would be the hardest self-

denial they know. It is a luxury that, like all other luxuries, brings sorrowful results. Perhaps, seeing

the sadness it has caused in your own Christian life, you may be tempted to say, Sad! This is no luxury

to me, but only a fearful trial.” But pause for a moment. Try gi ving it up, and you will soon find out

whether it is a luxury or not. Don't your doubts come to you like a group of friends? They sympathize

with your troubles and want to comfort you.

Is it not a luxury to sit with them, entertain them, and listen to their arguments? To join in their

condolences? Would it be no self-denial to turn resolutely from them, and refuse to hear a word they

have to say?

If you don't know, try it and see. Have you never enjoyed the luxury of hard thoughts against those

who wronged you? Have you never known the joy of brooding over their unkindness? Of prying into

their malice? Of imagining all sorts of wrong, uncomfortable things about them? It has made you

wretched, of course. But, it is a fascinating sort of wretchedness that you cannot easily give up. And

just like this is the luxury of doubting. Things have gone wrong with you in your experience.

Dispensations are mysterious. Temptations are odd. Your case seems unique. What could be more

natural than to conclude that, for some reason, God has forsaken you? That he does not love you and

is indifferent to your welfare? And how strong is the belief that you are too wicked for Him to care, or

too difficult for Him to manage?

You do not blame Him or accuse Him of injustice. You feel that you deserve His indifference and

rejection due to your unworthiness. This trick lets you doubt yourself while pretending to be humble.

But you are indulging in hard, wrong thoughts about your Lord, as much as you did of a human enemy.

He says He came not to save the righteous, but sinners. Your sinfulness and unworthiness are your best

claims to His love and care.

The poor little lamb that has wandered and got lost in the wilderness might well say, "The shepherd

does not love, care for, or remember me, because I am lost." He only loves and cares for the lambs that

never wander.” As well might the ill man say, “The doctor will not come to see me, nor give me any

medicines, because I am ill. He only cares for and visits well people.” Jesus say s , “ Those who are well

do not need a physician, but those who are sick.”(Mathew 9:12) And again He says, “What man of you,

having a hundred sheep, if he has lost one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine in the open country,

and go after the one that is lost, until he finds it? And when he has found it, he lays it on his shoulders,

rejoicing. And when he comes home, he calls together his friends and his neighbors, saying to them,

‘Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep that was lost.”(Luke15:4 -6)

Any thoughts of Him that differ from His own words are hard thoughts. To indulge in them is far worse

than to indulge in hard thoughts of any earthly friend or foe. From the beginning to the end of your

Christian life it is always sinful to indulge in doubts. Doubts are all from the devil, and are always

untrue. And the only way to meet them is by a direct and emphatic denial. And this brings me to the

practical part of the whole subject, as to how to get deliverance from this fatal habit. My answer would

be that the deliverance from this can be by no other means than the deliverance from any other sin. It

is to be found in the Lord and in Him only. You must hand your doubting over to Him, as you have

learned to hand your other temptations. You must do just what you do with your temper, or your pride.

You must give it up to the Lord.

I believe the only remedy is to take a pledge against it. As you would urge a drunkard to do against

drink. Trust in the Lord alone to keep you steadfast.

Like any other sin, the stronghold is in the will. You must surrender your will to doubt, just as you

would to any other temptation. God always takes possession of a surrendered will. If we say we will

not doubt and surrender our core to Him, His Spirit will work in us. We shall be kept from doubting by

His great power. The trouble is, the soul often does not fully surrender. It reserves a small freedom to

doubt, seeing it as sometimes necessary. "I do not want to doubt anymore," we will say, or, "I hope I

shall not." But , it is hard to say, "I will not doubt again."”

But no surrender is effectual until it reaches the point of saying, “I will not”. The liberty to doubt must

be given up forever. And the soul must consent to a continuous life of inevitable trust. I think, it is often

necessary to end this doubt. We must reach a decision on it. I believe it is quite as necessary in the case

of a doubter as in the case of a drunkard. It will not do to give it up by degrees. The total abstinence

principle is the only effectual one here. Once surrendered, the soul must rest entirely on the Lord for

deliverance in every temptation. It must lift up the shield of faith the moment the assault comes. It must

hand the very first suggestion of doubt over to the Lord, and must tell the enemy to settle the matter

with Him.

It must refuse to listen to the doubt a single moment. No matter how plausible or humble it seems, the

soul must say, "I dare not doubt; I must trust." The Lord is good, and HE DOES love me. Jesus saves

me; He save s me now.” Those three little words, repeated over and over, -- "Jesus saves me, Jesus

saves me," -- will defeat the greatest army of doubts that ever attacked a soul. I have tried it times

without number, and have never known it to fail. Do not stop to argue the matter out with your doubts,

nor try to prove that they are wrong. Pay no attention to them whatever; treat them with the utmost

contempt. Shut your door in their faces, and emphatically deny every word they say to you. Bring up

some “It is written,” and hurl it after them. Look right at Jesus, and tell Him you trust Him, and you

mean to trust Him. Let the doubts clamor as they may, they cannot hurt you if you will not let them in.

It may seem like you are shutting the door on your best friends. Your heart will long for your doubts

more than the Israelites longed for the flesh-pots of Egypt. But deny yourself; take up your cross in this

matter. Unmercifully refuse to listen to a word. A perfect army of doubts awaited my waking and

clamored at my door for admittance. Nothing seemed real or true. Least of all, it seemed possible that

I -- miserable and wretched -- could be the object of the Lord's love, care, or notice. If only I could let

these doubts in. If I could invite them to sit and make themselves at home, what a luxury that would

be! But years ago, I pledged against doubting. I would as soon violate my pledge against liquor as this

one.

I dared not admit the first doubt. I lifted my shield of faith the moment I noticed these thoughts. I gave

my whole army to my Lord to conquer. Then, I kept saying, "The Lord does love me." He is my present

and my perfect Saviour; Jesus saves me, Jesus saves me now!”

The victory was complete. The enemy came in like a flood. But the Lord raised a standard against him.

He was routed and put to flight. My soul sings the song of Moses and the children of Israel. It says,

" Then Moses and the people of Israel sang this song to the LORD, saying, I will sing to the LORD,

FOR he has triumphed gloriously; the hor se and his rider he has thrown into the sea.” (Exodus 15:1)

“The Lord is my strength and my song, and he has become my salvation; this is my God, and I will

praise him, my father’s God, and I will exalt him. The Lord is a man of war; the Lord is his

name. ”(Exodus 15:2 -3). It will help you to resist the assaults of this temptation to doubt, to see clearly

that doubting is sin. It directly disobeys our Lord, who commands us, “Peace I leave with you; my

peace I give to you. Not as the world gives do I give to you. Let not your hearts be troubled, neither let

them be afraid” (John 14:27)

The Bible everywhere commands us to trust, with no exceptions. Time and room would fail me to refer

to one hundredth part of these. But no one can read the Psalms without being convinced. The man who

trusts without question is the only one who pleases and is accepted by God. The “provocation” of Israel

was that they did not trust; “Yet they sinned still more against him, rebelling against the Most High in

the desert. They tested God in their heart by demanding the food they craved. They spoke against God,

saying, “Can God spread a table in the wilderness? He struck the rock so that water gushed out and

streams overflowed. Can he also give bread or provide meat for his people? “Therefore, when the Lord

heard, he was full of wrath; a fire was kindled against Jacob; his anger rose against Israel, because they

did not believe in God and did not trust his saving power.” (Psalms 78:17 -22.)

In contrast, Isaiah says of those who tr ust, “You keep him in perfect peace whose mind is stayed on

you, because he trusts in you. "(Isaiah 26:3) Nothing wounds us like a friend's doubt. I am convinced,

nothing grieves God more than our doubt.

One of my children, now with the Lord, said to me one evening as I tucked her in bed, "Well, mother,

I have had my first doubt."” “Oh, Ray,” I said, “What was it?” “Why,” she replied, “Satan came to me

and told me not to believe the Bible, for it was not a word of it true.” “And what did you say to him?”

I asked. “Oh,” she replied, triumphantly, “I just said to him, Satan, I will believe it. So there!” I was

delighted with the child's spiritual intelligence. She knew how to meet doubts. I encouraged her,

explaining that all doubts and discouragements are from the enemy. He is a liar, so never listen to him.

The next night, I had forgotten all about it. So, I was surprised when she said, as I tucked her in, "Well,

mother, Satan has been at it again."” “Oh, Ray darling!” I exclaimed in dismay, “what did he say this

time?” "Well," she replied, "he just told me I was such a naughty girl that Jesus could not love me. It

was foolish to think He did."” “And what did you say this time?” I asked. “Oh!” she replied, “I just

looked at him cross and said, Satan, shut your mouth!” And then she added, with a smile, “He can’t

make me unhappy one bit.” A grander battle no soul ever fought than this little child had done, and no

greater victory was ever won!

Dear, doubting soul, go and do likewise; and a similar victory shall be yours. As you lay down this

book take up your pen and write out your determination never to doubt again. Make it a real transaction

between your soul and the Lord. Give up your liberty to doubt forever. Put your will in this matter over

on the Lo rd’s side, and trust Him to keep you from falling. Tell him of your weakness and your doubts.

Your enemy has you helpless. Commit the whole battle to Him. Tell Him you will not doubt again.

Then, keep your gaze on Jesus.

Turn away from yourself and your doubts. Hold on to your faith, for He is faithful who has promised.

If you stay confident to the end, you will, through Him who loves you, be more than a conqueror in

this matter.

fields.title: Chapter 15. Practical Results
fields.body_html:
True Christian faith is demonstrated through actions reflecting Christ's holiness.

Believers are called to live humbly, forgive others, and serve God, avoiding worldly

pursuits. By surrendering to God’s guidance, Christians grow in Christlikeness,

becoming a testimony to His transformative power and love.

f all that has been said about the life hid with Christ in God is true, it should show in our daily lives.

Those who enjoy it should be a "peculiar people, zealous of good works." My son at college once

wrote to a friend that Christians must be God's witnesses. The world won't read the Bible, but they

will read our lives. Their belief in our religion depends on the report our lives give. As we all know,

this is an age of facts. Inquiries are shifting from theories to realities.

If our religion is to make any headway, it must be proved to be more than a theory. We must show, to

our age's critical minds, the grand facts of lives transformed by God's mighty power working in us to

do His will. "Show us 'forms of life,' say the scientists, and we will be convinced. When the Church

presents to them, in all its members, a holy life, their last stronghold will be conquered." I wish, before

closing my book, to speak very solemnly of the fruits of a life of faith, such as I have been describing.

I believe they are necessary. I urge my readers to feel their duty to walk worthy of their high calling.

I would speak to some of you, as personal friends. I am sure that, through this book, a mutual longing

has grown in your hearts, as it has in mine. We should show forth the praises of Him who has called us

out of darkness into His marvellous light. As a friend, I may speak plainly to friends. Please pardon me

if I discuss some vital details of life and character. They are important for true Christian growth.

I

The standard of holy living among Christians is low. Any real devotion in life and walk surprises, and

often disapproves, many in the Church. Most professed followers of the Lord Jesus Christ are unlike

Him. An outside observer would see little harmony between them.

But we, who have heard God's call to total devotion and trust, must do differently. We must come out

from the world and be separate, and must not be conformed to it in our characters nor in our purposes.

We must no longer share in its spirit or its ways.

Our talk must be in Heaven. We must seek things above, where Christ sits at God's right hand. We

must walk through the world as Christ walked. We must have the mind that was in Him.

As pilgrims and strangers we must abstain from fleshly lusts that war against the soul. As good soldiers

of Jesus Christ, we must avoid the world's affairs as much as possible. This is to please Him who chose

us to be soldiers.

We must abstain from all appearance of evil. We must be kind and forgiving to each other. God, for

Christ's sake, has forgiven us. We must not resent injuries or unkindness. Instead, we should return

good for evil and turn the other cheek to those who hurt us. We must take always the lowest place

among our fellowmen; and seek not our own honor, but the honor of others. We must be gentle, and

meek, and yielding; not standing up for our own rights, but for the rights of others. All that we do must

be done for the glory of God. In summary, since He who called us is holy, we must be holy in our

behavior. It is written, "Be you holy, for I am holy."”

Now, dear friends, this is all very practical. It surely means a life very different from most professors'

lives. It means that we do really and absolutely turn our backs on sel f, and on self’s motives and self’s

aims. We are a peculiar people, both to God and the world. Our Christ like lives and words will show

that we follow the Lord Jesus Christ. We are not of the world, even as He was not of the world. We

shall no longer feel that our money is our own, but the Lord’s, to be used in His service. We cannot use

our energies only to seek worldly things. If we first seek God's kingdom and His righteousness, we will

have what we need.

We will be forbidden to seek high places or worldly gains. We shall not be permitted to be conformed

to the world in our ways of thinking or of living. We will have no desire to take part in the world's silly

distractions. We should love heavenly things, not earthly ones. We will not serve ourselves, but our

Lord. We will perform our duties better than ever. We will work "not with eye service as men pleasers,

but as the servants of Christ, doing the will of God from the heart."”

Clear standard of Christian life, we may not recognize His voice due to ignorance. So, I want to be very

plain and definite in my statements. I have noticed that, where there is a faithful following of the Lord

in a consecrated soul, several things follow, sooner or later. Over time, meekness and quietness of spirit

become the daily life. There is a submissive acceptance of God's will, as it comes in the daily events.

There is also a pliability in God's hands to do or suffer His will. Next, there should be sweetness under

provocation, calmness amid chaos, and yieldingness to others' wishes. There is an insensibility to

slights and an absence of worry. Fear and care vanish. All these, and many other similar graces, are the

natural result of that inward life which is hid with Christ in God.

As for their habits: We always see such Christians, sooner or later, giving themselves to some work for

God and their fellowmen. They are willing to spend and be spent in the Master’s service. They become

indifferent to their houses' furniture and their living style. They make all personal adornment secondary

to the things of God.

The voice is dedicated to God, to talk and sing for Him. The purse is placed at His disposal. The pen

is dedicated to write for Him, the lips to speak for Him, the hands and the feet to do His bidding. Year

after year, such Christians grow more unworldly and heavenly-minded. They become more like Christ.

Their faces show a beautiful, divine life within them. All who look at them know they live with and

abide in God.

I am sure you have each felt some Divine hints. They foreshadow the life I now describe. Have you not

begun to feel, deep in your soul, the voice of God speaking to you about these things? Has it not been

a pain and a distress to you of late to discover how much is wrong in your life? Hasn't your soul been

troubled by doubt about some habits you once indulged in? Have you not begun to feel uneasy with

some habits? Do you wish you could change them? Have not paths of devotedness and of service begun

to open out before you, with the longing thought, “Oh that I could walk in them”?

All your longings, doubts, and distress are the Good Shepherd's voice. It seeks to call you away from

all that is against His will. Oh! Let me entreat you not to turn away from His gentle pleadings. You

little know the secret paths He means to lead you to by these very steps. You don't know the great

blessings that lie at their end. If you did, you would eagerly obey all His requirements. You can reach

the heights of Christian perfection. To do so, you must follow the Guide who will lead you there. He

reveals your way one step at a time, through your daily life. He asks only that you yield to His guidance.

If you are convinced of any sin, it is the voice of your Lord. Surrender it at once to His bidding.

Rejoice that He has begun to lead and guide you.

Be completely soft in His wise hands. Go where He entices you. Turn away from all that makes you

shrink. Obey Him perfectly. He will lead you swiftly and easily to a wonderful life of conformity to

Himself. It will be a testimony to all around you, beyond what you will ever know.

I knew a soul who surrendered to follow the Lord wherever He led her. In three months, she went from

deep despair to a blessed union with the Lord Jesus Christ.

In her darkness, she consecrated herself to the Lord. She surrendered her will to Him. She wanted Him

to work in her, to do His good pleasure. He began to speak to her by His Spirit in her heart. He suggested

small acts of service for Him. He called her away from all un-Christ ways.

She recognized His voice. She feared only disobeying Him. So, she followed Him, yielding to each of

His requests, wherever He led her. He led her on, day by day. He conformed her to His will. Her life

became a testimony to those around her. Even some who opposed and disbelieved were forced to admit

that it was of God. They were won to a similar surrender.

After three short months of this faithful following, it came to pass. So swiftly had she gone that her

Lord was able to reveal some of His deepest secrets of love to her wondering soul? He fulfilled the

promise of ( Acts 1:5) “for John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit not

many days from now.” baptising her with the Holy Ghost.

Do you think she has ever regretted fully following Him? Or that anything but joy fills her heart? She

is grateful for the path that brought her to this amazing place. Some of those steps were difficult at the

time, but she doesn't regret them. If you want a blessing, give yourself completely to the Divine Master,

just like she did. Don't hold back from any surrender, He asks of you .

The perfect way is hard to flesh. It is not hard to love. If you were sick and in need of God, how swiftly

would you move? Surely, you can trust Him! Some may call for things of little worth to you. They may

seem unworthy of the Lord's attention. Remember, He sees not as man sees, what is small to you may

be, in His eyes, the key to the deepest thing. To shape you to His will, He must have you soft. This

flexibility is more quickly reached by yielding in small things than in greater ones. Your one great

desire is to follow Him fully; canst thou not say then a continual “Yes, Lord!” to all His sweet

commands, small or great, and trust Him to lead you by the shortest road to your fullest Blessedness?

My dear friend, this, and nothing less than this, is what thy consecration meant, whether you knew it

or not. It meant inevitable obedience. It meant that the will of your God was henceforth to be your will

under all circumstances and at all times. It meant that, from then on, you gave up your freedom. You

surrendered completely to your Lord's control. It meant an hour of following Him, wherever He led

you. No dreams of turning back. Now, I ask you to keep your word. Let everything else go. Live, in

daily life, the Divine life within you. You are united to your Lord by a wondrous tie. So, walk as He

walked. Show the world His power to save by letting Him save you completely. You need not fear to

consent to this, for He is your Saviour, and His power is to do it all. He is not asking you, in your

weakness, to do it. He only asks you to yield to Him. Then, He will use His power to make you want

to do it and to do it. Your job is to yield yourself. His is to work. He will never give you a command

without giving you the power to obey it.

Do not worry about tomorrow. Trust your loving Lord. He promised to lead His sheep on a safe and

easy path. Take each onward step as He makes it plain to you. Bring all your life in each of its details

to Him to regulate and guide. Follow gladly and quickly the sweet suggestions of His Spirit in your

soul. And, day by day, you will find Him. He will bring you more into conformity with His will in all

things. He will, as you can bear it, shape you. Then, you will be a vessel of His honor, sanctified and

ready for every good work. You will have the joy of being a letter of Christ, known and read by all.

Your light will shine so brightly that, seeing your good works, men will glorify your Father in Heaven,

not you.

We are predestined to be “conformed to the image” of God’s Son. This means, of course, not a likeness

of bodily presence, but a likeness of character and nature. It means a similarity of thought, of feeling,

of desire, of loves, of hates. It means we should think and act, as Christ would, under our circumstances.

A little girl was once questioned what it meant to be a Christian. She replied, “It means to be just what

Christ would be, if He was a little girl and lived in my house.” Th e secret of Christ's life was His selfless

love for others. If we are like Him, this will be our secret too. He saved others, but Himself He could

not save. He "pleased not Himself." So, we "not to please ourselves." Instead, we should please our

neighbor, if it is for his good.

A thoughtful Hindu, who recently visited England and America to study Christianity, said, "What

Christians need is a bit more of Christ's Christianity, and a bit less of man's." Man's Christianity teaches

sacrifice to save oursel ves. Christ's Christianity teaches sacrifice to save others. Man’s Christianity

produces the fruitless selfishness of too much of our religion. Christ's Christianity produces a blessed

unselfishness. It comes from lives poured out for others, as was His. In short, our book teaches one

thing: we are to be Christ like Christians. And all our experiences amount to nothing if they do not

produce this result. "Not everyone who says to me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ will enter the kingdom of heaven, but

the one who does the w ill of my Father who is in heaven.” (Mathew 7:21)

fields.title: Chapter 16. The Joy Of Obedience
fields.body_html:
The Joy of Obedience emphasizes that true happiness comes from fully surrendering to

God’s will. The author compares this surrender to a loving relationsh ip, where

obedience to God brings intimacy and joy. While others may follow a more relaxed

path, those who obey God experience a unique privilege and blessing. The message

encourages believers to embrace complete obedience, which leads to spiritual

fulfillment and divine rewards .

once read: "Perfect obedience would bring perfect happiness if we had perfect confidence in the

power we obeyed." It struck me. It revealed a possible, yet undreamed-of, way to be happy. Later,

despite my lawlessness, that saying haunted me. It promised a rest and a way to grow. It soothed and

satisfied my yearnings.

I must say, I have discovered this rest, not as a vision, but as a reality. I have seen in the Lord Jesus,

our Master. We can yield to Him and take His yoke upon us to find perfect rest. You, dear, hesitant

soul, don't know the joy you are missing. The Master has revealed Himself to you. He calls for your

complete surrender. You shrink and hesitate. A measure of surrender you are willing to make, and think

indeed it is fit and proper you should. But you seem to think that an utter abandonment, without any

reserves, is too much to be asked for. You are afraid of it. It involves too much, you think, and is too

great a task. To be obedient in a measurable way is your desire; the idea of being completely obedient

appalls you.

You see other souls, too. They walk with easy consciences in a wider path than the one marked out for

you. You ask yourself, why is this? It seems strange, and perhaps hard, that you must do what they

need not. And, you must leave undone what they have the liberty to do. Ah! Dear Christian, this very

difference between you is your privilege, though you do not yet know it. Your Lord says, "Whoever

has my commandments and keeps them, he it is who loves me. And he who loves me will be loved by

I

my Father, and I will love him and manifest myself to him.”(John14:21) You have His commandments;

those you envy, have them not. You know the mind of your Lord about many things, in which, as yet,

they are walking in darkness. Is not this a privilege? Is it regrettable that your soul is so close to your

Master? He can tell you things that those farther away do not know. Do you not realize what a tender

degree of intimacy this implies?

Many life relations require only a modest devotion from both parties. We may have great friendships.

Yet, we spend much of our lives in separate, differing pursuits. When together, we may enjoy each

other's company. We may find many shared interests. But, we are not distressed by separation. Other,

closer friendships do not interfere. We lack enough love to have the right or desire to share our most

private affairs. A certain degree of reserve and distance is the suitable thing, we feel. But there are other

relations in life where all this is changed. The friendship becomes love. The two hearts give themselves

to one another, to be no longer two but one.

A union of souls takes place, which makes all that belongs to one the property of the other. Separate

interests and separate paths in life are no longer possible. Things that were lawful before are now

unlawful. It's due to the closeness of the tie that binds. The reserve and distance suitable for mere

friendship become fatal in love. Love gives all, and must have all in return. One's wishes bind the other.

Each heart desires to know the other's secret wishes. It wants to fly on the wind to fulfill them.

Do people like this feel frustrated by the burden that love places on them? Do they envy the cool, calm

friendships they see? Do they regret the closeness to their beloved because of the obligations it creates?

Do they not glory in these very obligations? And, with a tender, exulting joy, pity the poor, far-off ones

who dare not come so near? Isn't every new revelation of each other's minds a delight? And, is any path

hard that their love compels them to travel? Ah! Dear souls, if you've known this, even for a few hours;

if you've ever loved someone enough to find joy in sacrificing for them; if you've ever longed to

abandon your will to another as a sweet privilege, then, by all the love of your heavenly Master, I urge

you to do the same for God!

He loves you with more than the love of friendship. As a bridegroom rejoices over his bride, so does

He rejoice over you. Only a full surrender will satisfy Him. He has given you all, and He asks for all

in return. The slightest reserve will grieve Him to the heart. He spared not Himself, and how can you

spare yourself? For your sake, He gave all He had. For His, you must do the same. Oh, be generous in

your self-surrender! Meet His measureless devotion for you, with a measureless devotion to Him. Be

glad and eager to throw yourself headlong into His dear arms, and to hand over the reins of government

to Him. Whatever there is of you, let Him have it all. Give up forever everything separate from Him. I

resign my freedom of choice. I rejoice in our union. It makes my devotion not just possible, but

necessary.

Have you never longed to love someone far away? You were not close enough for a more intimate

approach. Have you not felt a burning desire to surrender yourself to them? Yet, you had no one to

whom you could give that love. Have not your hands been full of very precious, alabaster boxes of

ointment? You have never been near enough to any heart to pour it out. If you hear your Lord's sweet

voice, He is calling you to a place of closeness to Himself. It requires a separation from all else. It will

make your devotion not just possible, but necessary. Will you shrink or hesitate?

Will you find it hard that He reveals more of His mind to you than to others? He will not let you be

happy in anything that separates you from Himself. Do you want to go where He cannot go with you,

or to have pursuits which He cannot share?

No! No, a thousand times, no! You will spring out to meet His dear will with an eager joy. Even His

slightest wish will become a binding law to you, which it would fairly break your heart to disobey. You

will rejoice in the narrowness of the path He sets for you. You will pity, with infinite sorrow, the poor,

far-off ones who have missed this joy. Love's obligations will be its sweetest privileges. Your right to

give your all to your Lord will feel like a lift into a realm of unspeakable glory. Perfect happiness will

come from perfect obedience. You will then know a bit of what Jesus meant when He said, “ I delight

to do your will, O my God; your law is within my heart.”( Psalms 40:8 )

And do you think the joy in this will be all on your side? Has the Lord no joy in those who have thus

surrendered themselves to Him, and who love to obey Him? Ah, my friends, we are unfit to speak of

this. But the Scriptures reveal glimpses of the delight, satisfaction, and joy our Lord has in us. They

ravish the soul with their wondrous hints of blessedness. That we should need Him is easy to

comprehend; that He should need us seems incomprehensible. It is natural to desire Him. But that He

should desire us is hard to believe. And yet, over and over, He says it, and what can we do but believe

Him?

He has made our hearts able to feel this great love. He has offered Himself as its object. It is infinitely

precious to Him. He says, “Whoever has my commandments and keeps them, he it is who loves me.

And he who loves me will be loved by my Father, and I will love him and manifest myself to him"(John

4:21). He knocks at every heart, seeking to be its supreme love. “Will you have me?” He says to the

believer, “ To be your beloved, will you follow me into suffering and loneliness? Will you endure

hardship for my sake? Ask for no reward but my smile and praise.

Will you throw yourself with an utter abandonment into my will? Will you give up to me the absolute

control of yourself and all that you are? Will you be content with pleasing me and me only? May I have

my way within you in all things? Will you come into so close a union with me as to make a separation

from the world necessary? Will you accept me as your only Lord, and leave all others, to cleave only

unto me?” In a thousand ways , He makes this offer of oneness with Himself to every believer. But all

do not say “Yes,” to Him. Other loves and other interests seem to them too precious to be cast aside.

They do not miss Heaven because of this. But they miss an unspeakable joy.

You, however, are not one of these. From the very first your soul has cried out eagerly and gladly to

all His offers, “Yes, Lord; yes!” You are more than ready to pour out upon Him all your richest treasures

of love and devotedness. Your enthusiasm for self-surrender may disturb some moderate Christians.

Your love makes necessary a separation from the world, which a lower love cannot even conceive of.

Sacrifices and services are possible and sweet to you. They could not come from a less devoted heart.

The life upon which you have entered gives you the right to a lavish outpouring of your all upon your

beloved One. Services, of which more distant souls know nothing, become now your sweetest privilege.

Your Lord claims from you, because of your union with Him, far more than He claims of them.

What to them is lawful, love has made unlawful for you. To you He can make known His secrets, and

to you He looks for an instant response to every requirement of His love. Oh, it is wonderful! The

glorious, unspeakable privilege upon which you have entered! It will matter little if men hate you. They

may shun you, reproach you, and cast out your name as evil for His sake! "Rejoice in that day and leap

for joy. Your reward is great in Heaven. If you share in His suffering, you shall share in His glory." In

you He is seeing of the travail of His soul, and is satisfied. Your love and devotedness are His precious

reward for all He has done for you.

It is unspeakably sweet to Him. Do not be afraid then to let yourself go in a heart-whole devotedness

to your Lord that can brook no reserves. Others may not approve, but He will, and that is enough. Do

not measure your obedience or your service. Let your heart and your hand be as free to serve Him, as

His heart and His hand were to serve you. Let Him have all there is of you, body, soul, and spirit, time,

talents, voice, everything. Lay your whole life open before Him that He may control it. Say to Him

each day, “Lord, how shall I regulate this day so as to please you? Where shal l I go? What shall

I do? Whom shall I visit? What shall I say?” Give your intellect up into His control and say,

“Lord, tell me how to think so as to please you?” Give Him your reading, your pursuits, your

friendships. Then say, "Lord, give me the insi ght to judge these things with your wisdom."” Do not let

there be a day nor an hour in which you are not intelligently doing His will, and following Him wholly.

Serving Him will give your life a halo. It will gild even the dullest life with a heavenly glow.

Have you ever grieved that the romance of youth is so soon lost in the hard realities of the world? Bring

God into your life and its details. A greater joy will thrill your soul than youth's brightest days could

know. Nothing will seem hard or stern again. The meanest life will be glorified by this. As I watched

a poor woman at her wash-tub, I thought of the disheartening aspects of her life. I wondered why such

lives must exist. Then, with a thrill of joy, I recalled the possible glorification of it. I told myself, even

this life, lived in and with Christ, following Him wherever He leads, would be glorious.

Every hour of it would be filled with enthusiasm.

I am comforted to know that God's greatest blessings lie with the poorest and most humble lives. "For,"

says our Lord Himself, "whosoever," whether rich or poor, old or young, bond or free.

Whosoever shall do the will of God, the same is my brother, and my sister, and my mother.

Pause a moment over these simple yet amazing words. His brother, sister, and mother! What would we

not have given to have been one of these! Oh, let me beg you, beloved Christian. Come, taste and see

how good the Lord is. He has wonderful things in store for those who "keep His commandments, and

do what is pleasing in His sight." "If you listen closely to the Lord your God and obey all His

commandments today, He will elevate you above all the nations on earth. If you listen to the Lord your

God, all these blessings will come upon you."

“ Blessed shall you be in the city, and blessed shall you be in the field. Blessed shall be the fruit of your

womb and the fruit of your ground and the fruit of your cattle, the increase of your herds and the young

of your flock. Blessed shall be your basket and your kneading bowl. Blessed shall you be when you

come in, and blessed shall you be when you go out. The LORD will cause your enemies who rise

against you to be defeated before you. They shall come out against you one way and flee before you

seven ways. (Deuteronomy 28:3-7)

"T he LORD will command the blessing on you in your barns and in all that you undertake. And he will

bless you in the land that the LORD your God is giving you. The LORD will establish you as a people

holy to himself, as he has sworn to you, if you keep the commandments of the LORD your God and

walk in his ways.” (Deuteronomy 28:8 -9)

“ And all the peoples of the earth shall see that you are called by the name of the LORD, and they shall

be afraid of you. And the LORD will make you abound in prosperity, in the fruit of your womb and in

the fruit of your livestock and in the fruit of your ground, within the land that the LORD swore to your

fathers to give you. The LORD will open to you his good treasury, the heavens, to give the rain to your

land in its season and to bless all the work of your hands. And you shall lend to many nations, but you

shall not borrow. And the LORD will make you the head and not the tail, and you shall only go up and

not down, if you obey the commandments of the LORD your God, which I command you today, being

careful to do them,”(Deuteronomy 28:10 -13)

For the Israelites, it was outward and temporary. For us, it is inward and spiritual. And, it is far more

glorious. May our surrendered wills leap out to embrace it in all its fullness!

fields.title: Chapter 17. Oneness With Christ
fields.body_html:
God’s purpose is to unite believers with Himself through Christ. True oneness with

He is shown in living His will, character, and actions, not just in emotions. It requires

surrender, obedience, and a Christ-like life, fully aligning with His purpose.

od's dealings with a believer's soul aim for oneness with Himself. This fulfills the Lord's Prayer:

“that they may all be one, just as you, Father, are in me, and I in you, that they also may be in

us, so that the world may believe that you have sent me. The glory that you have given me I have given

to them, that they may be one even as we are one, I in them and you in me, that they may become

perfectly one, so that the world may know that you sent me and loved them even as you loved me"(John

17:21-23)

God's glorious purpose for His people, before the world's foundation, was a soul-union. It was the

mystery hid from ages and generations. It was accomplished in the incarnation of Christ. It has been

made known b y the Scriptures. And it is realized as an actual experience by many of God’s dear

children. But not by all. It is true of all. God has not hidden it. But, many have dim eyes and unbelieving

hearts. They fail to grasp it. The Lord is stirring up believers everywhere. He wants them to abandon

themselves to Him. It is to bring them to a personal realization of this. He wants to work in them all

the good pleasure of His will.

All the previous steps in the Christian life lead up to this. The Lord has made us for it. Until we know

it, and choose to embrace it, His soul's travail for us is unsatisfied. Our hearts have not found their final

rest.

G

The usual course of Christian experience is pictured in the history of the disciples. First, they awoke to

their condition and need. They then came to Christ and pledged their allegiance to Him. Then they

followed Him, worked for Him, believed in Him, and yet, how unlike Him! They sought to be above

each other. They ran from the cross. They misunderstood His mission and words. They forsook Him

in danger. Yet, He sent them to preach. He recognized them as His disciples, with power to work for
